title: Empower Kids with Autism – Behavior Tech Role
description:
Psychology Opportunity in Grain Valley,MO

Are you a seasoned Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) seeking the ideal organization to join? We're actively seeking enthusiastic and devoted RBTs to become valued members of our team, contributing your expertise to support our clients in achieving their unique goals. As an accomplished professional in the Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) field, your skills and dedication align with our dedication to providing excellence to our clients.

Perks:

  • Same Day Pay! No more waiting for payday — now you can access a portion of your paycheck right after you clock in and out. Whether it’s an emergency or you just need funds sooner, you’ll have the flexibility to get paid immediately.

title: Business Advisory Manager
description:
Doeren Mayhew is the 36th largest U.S. tax, assurance and advisory firm headquartered in Troy, Michigan with over 25 offices across the country and abroad. Founded in 1932, Doeren Mayhew is positioned for successful future growth. If you want to join a rising firm that is consistently named among the 50 best-managed firms in the nation, this is the firm for you.

Doeren Mayhew is seeking a Manager to work in our Business Advisory department headquartered in Troy, Michigan. The ideal candidate would have 5 plus years of public accounting experience in business and individual tax preparation/review and bookkeeping.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform tax research on complex tax issues.
  • Manage engagement team members to ensure timely completion of assigned tasks and be a resource for team members.
  • Provide guidance/mentorship to associates and interns and assist them in developing technical skills.
  • Maintain timely and accurate communication with team and clients to manage expectations, deadlines and deliverables.
  • Build and maintain client relationships and ensure client needs are being met.
  • Demonstrate advanced technical aptitude of taxation and handle complex returns and projects with confidence.
  • Lead the preparation of financial reports cash-flow statements, budgets, projections, and dashboard reports. Analyze and reconcile financial accounts, support general ledger management, provide cash-flow analysis and report on budget variances.
  • Review and lead the preparation of tax returns for individuals, partnerships, C-corporations, S-corporations, trusts, personal property, and payroll.
  • Provide QuickBooks support and training to clients in a variety of industries.
  • Assist with compliance and IRS notices.
  • Participate in special projects such as strategic planning, exit planning, systems optimization, organizational design, etc.
  • Utilize analytical and decision-making skills to solve complex technical issues.
  • Seek opportunities to participate in practice development to build network of referral sources.
  • Present new ideas and improvements for ways of performing tasks in order to achieve firm and departmental goals.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Accounting or related field
  • CPA license required
  • Minimum of 5+ years’ experience in domestic tax
  • Strong leadership skills and ability to effectively train, coach, and mentor others
  • Outstanding oral and written communication skills
  • Ability to work independently, but also in a team environment
  • Ability to adapt quickly to new technology platforms
  • Ability to manage multiple projects/clients and deadlines

Doeren Mayhew is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race; color; religion; national origin; sex; age; disability; sexual orientation; gender identity or expression; genetic predisposition or carrier status; veteran, marital, or any other status protected by law.

“Doeren Mayhew" is the brand name under which Doeren Mayhew Assurance, PC and Doeren Mayhew Advisors, LLC and its subsidiary entities provide professional services. Doeren Mayhew Assurance, PC and Doeren Mayhew Advisors, LLC (and its subsidiary entities) practice as an alternative practice structure in accordance with the AICPA Code of Professional Conduct and applicable law, regulations and professional standards. Doeren Mayhew Assurance, PC is a licensed independent CPA firm that provides attest services to its clients, and Doeren Mayhew Advisors, LLC and its subsidiary entities provide tax and business consulting services to their clients. Doeren Mayhew Advisors, LLC, DM Payroll Solutions, Doeren Mayhew Capital Advisors and their subsidiary entities are not licensed CPA firms.

title: Assistant Project Manager
description:
Company Overview: Doggett Concrete Construction is a company specializing in concrete construction, particularly focusing on multifamily projects in the Southeastern United States. We have a specific expertise in utilizing post-tension building practices. We place a significant emphasis on maintaining a safe work environment for our employees, subcontractors, and clients. We pride

ourselves on building deep relationships with trade partners.


Company Vision: “Develop people and partnerships for intentional organizational growth”

Core Values: Integrity, Determined, Collaborative


The Assistant Project Manager supports the Project Manager in the planning, coordination, execution, and financial management of commercial concrete construction projects. This position is responsible for assisting with project documentation, scheduling, subcontract administration, procurement, cost tracking, and communication with field personnel, subcontractors, suppliers, and clients.


The APM is expected to develop the technical, financial, and leadership skills necessary to advance into a Project Manager role while helping ensure projects are completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with company quality standards.


Duties to include, but not limited to the following:

  • Reporting to Senior Project Managers on job specific details.
  • Understanding full scope of work for each project.
  • Manage all business aspects of multiple concurrent projects and ensure financial targets are met while maintaining established quality standards.
  • Manage all activities associated with production including labor, materials, equipment and services.
  • Manage the work load accurately as related to the contracted scope of work.
  • Manage subcontract labor and inhouse crews.
  • Schedule and manage concrete deliveries.
  • Purchases and track quantities of supplied materials to all projects.
  • Maintains a professional relationship with clients and ensures clear and consistent communication.
  • Develop and maintain updated and accurate schedules & daily reports for each project.
  • Develops and maintains a fair and professional relationship with subcontractors and vendors.
  • Ensures safe work environment and quality standards are maintained.

title: Mentor: Arches

title: Assistant Director of Pharmacy (Children's Hospital)
location: Corpus Christi TX, Edinburg TX, Houston TX, San Antonio TX, Dallas TX, Galveston TX
description:
Join CompleteRx as an Assistant Director of Pharmacy in Corpus Christi, Texas, where you can make a lasting impact on pediatric patient care in a rewarding and fulfilling leadership role.

  • Partnering with Driscoll Children’s Hospital, a 225-bed pediatric hospital with a Level IV NICU, we're seeking an innovative pharmacy leader to help drive clinical excellence, lead high-performing teams, and improve outcomes for the children and families of South Texas.
  • The Assistant Director of Pharmacy provides leadership and strategic direction at our partnered hospital while having the support and expertise of CompleteRx’s operations team as a resource.

Location: Corpus Christi, TX

We encourage candidates who have completed a Health-System Pharmacy Administration and Leadership (HSPAL) residency to apply.

CompleteRx is a national pharmacy management company. We partner with acute care hospitals and health systems to elevate pharmacy services and patient care. Our team of pharmacy subject matter experts provides operational support, clinical guidance, leadership development, and industry best practices that empower our hospital partners to achieve exceptional results.

Hospital Overview:
Join a mission-driven organization where compassion and excellence come together. Since 1953, Driscoll Children’s Hospital has been a trusted provider of pediatric care for families throughout South Texas and beyond, caring for more than 150,000 patients annually across its network of hospitals, clinics, and pediatric emergency services.

Position Summary:

The Assistant Director of Pharmacy assists the System Director of Pharmacy with ensuring that the pharmacy provides superior services, meets or exceeds all legal, accreditation, and certification requirements, and follows all applicable policies, procedures, codes, and standards of the facility.

What You Will Do:

Ensure safe, appropriate, and cost-effective drug therapies for patients according to established policies, procedures, and protocols:

  • Assist the System Director of Pharmacy in developing, enforcing, and maintaining policies and procedures that promote cost-effective, appropriate, and safe drug therapy.
  • Assist with ensuring order fills are consistent with the state-approved medication formulary.
  • Assist in the supervision of drug storage and preparation areas throughout the health system.
  • Assist in providing for the educational needs of healthcare professionals, patients, and their families in the health system.
  • Assist in ensuring the maintenance and integrity of an adequate drug supply and assist in the establishment of procurement and purchasing specifications for drugs, chemicals, and biologicals.
  • Assist in ensuring strict control and accountability for drugs dispensed to patients or distributed to floor stock.
  • Assist in the adequate control and documentation of controlled substances.
  • Perform other supervisory duties as assigned by the System Director of Pharmacy.

Contribute to the quality and effective operation of the pharmacy department:

  • Supervise pharmacy personnel as assigned by the System Director of Pharmacy.
  • Assists in the recruitment, promotion, discipline, and termination of pharmacy staff as assigned by the System Director of Pharmacy.
  • Assist in the development and maintenance of job descriptions and performance standards consistent with health system standards and as assigned by the System Director of Pharmacy.
  • Assist in the preparation of work schedules and monitor pharmacy workload as assigned by the System Director of Pharmacy.

description:
Job Title: Housing Specialist- Marian Hall

Reports to: Fair Futures Supervisor

Location: 337 East 17th Street, New York, NY 10003

Salary Range: 50K-55K Annually based on relevant post graduate education and experience

Job Summary:

Youth aging out of care in NYC face many hurdles in obtaining housing, including lack of affordable housing. The Housing Specialist will utilize a developmental approach to provide housing support to participants 17 years old and older. Supports will include developing housing leads and resources to help them locate housing; facilitating workshops to build their skills and increase knowledge related to living independently and transitioning into the community; advocating on behalf of youth with landlords and brokers to overcome any challenges to securing suitable housing; and assisting with securing resources to help with moving expenses. Each area of focus requires expertise to ensure the youth can access housing opportunities, be supported emotionally, and continue to be plugged into to a supportive network after locating housing.

Major Duties:

  • Provides housing assistance to young people in foster care including NYCHA, Section 8, supportive housing, Housing Connect and other forms of housing.
  • Develops and maintains up to date information about housing issues, available subsidies, and programs.
  • Work with participants to develop and implement individualized goals based upon the specific service needs of the participant, and with a focus on moving into to a more independent living opportunity.
  • Collaborate with Property Manager to ensure all housing requirements are communicated to residents and maintained.
  • Develop and facilitate workshops to build skills and increase knowledge around living independently. Provides expert consultation/guidance to EFFC/TFFC casework staff in their work with families with particular emphasis on those who need housing assistance.
  • Works directly with participants to assist them with housing services/problems. This may include accompanying them to apply for subsidies and to housing court appointments and fair hearings.
  • Establishes and maintains linkages with various programs providing housing services including ACS HPAD, NYCHA, DHS, EHV, Section 8 and various shelters, eviction prevention programs, legal services, realtors etc. Makes/assists with referrals as appropriate.
  • Participates in all conferences and/or meetings related to the discharge or preparation for young adulthood, i.e., Family Team Conferences, Clinical Meetings, Trial/Final Discharge meetings, goal changes and permanency planning conferences.
  • Remain familiar with current Section 8 and other housing voucher policies and procedures, and train and inform staff about housing related issues including all housing application matters.
  • Complete a 3- and 6-month assessment for youth who have transitioned out of foster care into their own home.
  • Represents GSS at outside meetings/conferences/workshops particularly as they relate to housing and foster care issues as required by the agency.
  • Maintain accurate documentation and complete the timely entry of progress notes into CONNECTIONS and Care4 in accordance with state and agency standard.
  • Implement the Fair Futures Model and attend mandatory agency and Fair Futures trainings.
  • Integrate the Sanctuary Model SELF (Safety, Emotional Management, Loss and Future) framework into daily practice to ensure quality care and an effective work environment.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s Degree Preferred
  • Associates Degree Required
  • Ability to work independently, demonstrate good judgement, and prioritize skills.
  • Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills to maintain required documentation.
  • Must be able to use public transportation systems, including subways and busses to attend various meetings and make home visits.
  • Must have a commitment to work from a strength based and/or youth development perspective.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred.
  • Must have knowledge of Connections and Microsoft Suite.
  • Must have ability to work a flexible schedule when needed including some evenings, weekends, and holidays.
  • Must have a commitment to GSS models of practice including Sanctuary and ACS principles to promote permanency, safety, and well-being.
  • Good basic knowledge of housing field and service options
  • Minimum of one year’s experience in child welfare or related systems desirable.
  • Ability to relate to a wide variety of program participants and staff.
  • Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal and organizational skills necessary.
  • Must have a commitment to work from a strength based and/or youth development perspective.

title: Field Restoration Specialist II
description:
Field Restoration Specialist II

About the Job

Cityside Fiber is seeking a motivated Field Restoration Specialist II to join our Field Operations team. Building on the Field Restoration Specialist I role, this position takes on landscape and hardscape restoration work, restoring residential and commercial properties following fiber construction while working independently to manage daily routes and multi-step site restoration. Success in this position requires strong attention to detail, pride in maintaining clean and professional communities, and the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment.

***This role is built for turf professionals. As a Field Restoration Specialist II, you’ll be our go-to expert for synthetic turf restoration, removing and protecting turf ahead of underground construction, then reinstalling it with flawless seams, edges, and finish. If you have hands-on synthetic turf installation or repair experience, we want to hear from you. ***

Responsibilities

  • Perform the removal, lifting, cutting, rolling, and temporary protection of existing turf to provide access for underground Service Drop installations and other construction activities.
  • Properly prepare and protect turf prior to construction to minimize damage and maintain the integrity of the existing turf system.
  • Reinstall and restore synthetic turf following completion of underground construction work.
  • Perform standard turf repairs, including repositioning, leveling, securing, and correcting minor cuts, separations, and displaced areas.
  • Ensure turf is properly aligned with surrounding areas and that seams, edges, transitions, and finished surfaces meet Cityside Fiber restoration standards.
  • Coordinate with Service Drop and Field Operations personnel to ensure turf restoration is completed after construction activities are finished.
  • Identify turf conditions or damage that exceed standard restoration capabilities and escalate to management when specialized repair or replacement is required.
  • Document completed turf restoration work with required photographs and work-order notes.
  • Operate and maintain pressure washing equipment to clean infrastructure, equipment pads, utility boxes, conduit areas, and other field assets
  • Remove temporary utility locate markings (paint and chalk) from streets, sidewalks, curbs, and driveways following fiber construction
  • Perform landscape restoration including sod replacement, irrigation repair, grading, mulch, decorative rock, and edging
  • Perform hardscape restoration including pavers, concrete, gravel, fencing, gates, mailbox posts, and utility lids
  • Ensure proper water usage and compliance with local environmental regulations
  • Follow safe chemical handling, equipment operation, and personal protective equipment (PPE) protocols at all times
  • Inspect equipment before and after use and report maintenance issues promptly
  • Complete daily work orders and site documentation accurately and on time
  • Coordinate with construction crews and supervisors to prioritize clean-up and restoration areas
  • Safely transport equipment, materials, and tools to and from job sites and manage daily routes effectively
  • Support facilities maintenance, fleet washing, warehouse organization, material deliveries, and inventory as needed
  • Work in various outdoor environments and weather conditions throughout the service area
  • Contribute to a culture of trust, integrity, and collaboration
  • Understand and uphold Cityside Fiber's core purpose and values and be passionate about what we do

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the position. Management reserves the right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities as business needs evolve.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2+ years of experience in pressure washing, landscaping, hardscape/concrete, construction clean-up, or a related field
  • 2+ years of synthetic turf installation or repair experience
  • Ability to work outdoors and in various weather conditions
  • Ability to lift and move equipment (50+ lbs) and perform physically demanding tasks
  • Strong attention to detail and pride in maintaining clean, professional communities
  • Ability to work independently and manage daily routes effectively
  • Familiarity with standard safety protocols and procedures, and a commitment to working safely in the field
  • Valid California driver's license, good driving record, reliable transportation, and proof of insurance
  • Availability for occasional overtime and weekend work as construction schedules require

About Cityside Fiber

Cityside Fiber is on a mission to deliver high-quality, reliable internet to communities through innovation and a people-first approach. Headquartered in Irvine, CA, we are an emerging telecommunications provider expanding rapidly due to high demand. Our culture is built on innovation, accountability, and trust, and we seek independent thinkers who want to contribute to something big.

Our core purpose is to create networks that better enable life-changing connectivity in our communities by daring to be different and having our team members put people first all while having fun. We’re building a next-generation internet provider with a focus on innovation, accountability, and trust. At Cityside Fiber, you’ll work with a passionate team, have room for growth, and make a real impact.

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.

title: Transportation Construction Inspectors (All levels - NOVA District)
description:
ATCS's Construction Services group is expanding in Virginia! We are looking for individuals with VA construction management and inspection experience that have or are able to obtain necessary VDOT certifications.

We're open to candidates with varying levels of experience - Inspectors, Trainees, Senior Inspectors to join our team in Herndon, VA and the surrounding areas!

Duties:

  • Perform transportation construction inspections on Highway, Bridges, Environmental, Traffic, and Facilities type projects
  • Write daily progress reports
  • Oversight of contractor work crews to ensure compliance with contract documents, reading and interpretation of contract documents to verify that safe construction practices are being utilized to produce quality results
  • Perform field test on materials (concrete slump/air, soil compaction, and HMA)
  • Complete documentation of materials, labor compliance, safety, processing estimates, work orders, and adjustments
  • Report on-site activities and daily progress to the Project Engineer via standardized reporting, responsible for calculation and determination of pay quantities

Requirements:

  • Varying levels of contractor or inspection experience in roadway construction with VDOT desired desired:
    • 0-3 years for Inspection Trainee candidates
    • 3-6 years of experience for Inspector candidates
    • 6+ years of experience for Senior Inspector candidates
  • Knowledgeable in VDOT Road and Bridges specifications and standards.
  • OSHA safety requirements on road and bridge construction sites.
  • Knowledge of mathematics to include algebra, geometry and trigonometry.
  • Skill in the use of field engineering and testing equipment, inspection methods and materials.
  • Possession of or ability to obtain required certifications within 12 months of employment and maintain
    • Work Zone Traffic Control
    • Asphalt Concrete Field
    • ACI Hydraulic Cement Concrete Field
    • Soils and Aggregate Compaction
    • Nuclear Safety and Transportation
    • Pavement Marking and Guardrail Installation
    • Storm Water Inspection
    • DEQ Erosion and Sediment Control Inspection
    • OSHA Safety training courses
    • Flagging
  • Valid Drivers’ License
  • Proficiency in MS Office, SiteManager, PlanGrid and other project management software

Our employees are the most critical part of ATCS. For this position, we offer a competitive salary range of $20.00 to $53.16 per hour, commensurate with experience and qualifications. The role is also eligible for overtime and an annual bonus, with a target 2% of the employee's annualized salary. . In addition to compensation, ATCS offers outstanding, employee-focused benefits for you and your family. Full-time employees are eligible for benefits coverage on the first day of the month following their start date. Including, but not limited to: generous personal PTO, inclusive holiday PTO, community involvement PTO, highly customizable medical plan options, excellent dental & vision plans, 401K match up to 3% with immediate vesting, parental leave, STD & LTD, tuition reimbursement, employee assistance program and more.

ATCS is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, disability, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran status, or genetic information. ATCS is committed to providing equal opportunities and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. To request reasonable accommodation, contact Caitlin Crockett, MBA, SPHR at ccrockett@atcs.com.

title: ERP System Administrator
description:
Classification: Full-time, Salaried

Reports To: Director of Information Technology

Location: Grand Rapids, MI

SUMMARY

As a senior technical anchor within the IT department, the ERP System Administrator owns the operational health, tactical evolution, and security of the university’s Colleague ERP environment. The ERP System Administrator is the primary steward of the university’s enterprise data environment. This role focuses on the high-level configuration, security, and health of the Colleague ERP system and its supporting SQL infrastructure. This individual leverages modern technology to automate business processes, ensure data integrity, and maintain seamless integrations across the campus ecosystem.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

· System Ownership: Drive the daily maintenance, configuration, and overall health of the Colleague ERP and supporting SQL environment, while serving as the primary architect for major installations, upgrades, and system optimization.

· Business Process Automation: Identify opportunities to modernize manual processes through low-code automation, online forms, and workflow improvements that support ERP operations.

· Integration Management: Ensure the reliability and effectiveness of integrations between the ERP and connected platforms (including the LMS), maintaining the integrity and availability of critical business data across departments. Monitor and optimize ERP–LMS data pipelines and supporting APIs to ensure student, faculty, and grade data remain accurate and synchronized.

· Connected Systems Support: Provide technical support for external systems connected to the ERP, including troubleshooting integration issues, coordinating with vendors.

· Performance Engineering: Proactively monitor system performance, troubleshoot bottlenecks, and manage the installation of new software modules or patches.

· Collaboration: Act as a technical consultant for reporting services and data management, supporting accurate SQL-based reporting, data auditing, and cross-functional problem solving.

· Data Integrity: Identify and resolve data inconsistencies, database issues, and record-level errors within the ERP environment to maintain accurate, reliable, and trusted institutional data.

· End-User Escalation & Support: Serve as a primary point of escalation for end-user issues related to the ERP environment, providing advanced troubleshooting, guidance, and resolution support to ensure timely service and minimal disruption.

· System Integrity & Continuity: Ensure robust business continuity and disaster recovery plans are maintained for all database environments.

· Emergency Support: Remain on-call for critical system issues outside regular business hours to ensure 24/7 environment availability.

· Other Duties as Assigned: Perform other related duties as assigned in support of ERP operations, IT department priorities, and broader university needs.

QUALIFICATIONS

· Education & Experience: A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field; however, 5+ years of demonstrable expertise in ERP administration or database administration is a highly valued substitute.

· Technical Stack: Proficiency in SQL (administration and programming), PowerShell, Windows Server, Hyper-V, Azure.

· Preferred Skills: Windows Server Administration, Ellucian Colleague

· Interpersonal: Strong critical thinking and a customer-centric approach to troubleshooting.

Essential Qualifications:

  • A personal relationship with Jesus Christ and an active Christian commitment.
  • A theology that supports the values and mission of Cornerstone University core commitments evidenced by an ability to affirm and sign the university’s doctrinal statement, “The Cornerstone Confession.”
  • Four other foundational pillars, along with the university’s mission and confession, form Cornerstone’s Core Commitments.
    • The Cornerstone Christian World View
    • The Cornerstone Academic Vision
    • The Cornerstone Beautiful Christian Community
    • The Marriage and Human Sexuality Position Statement

These core commitments convey who we are, what we believe and how we live and work together in community. Employees are expected to faithfully attend an evangelical and biblical church whose core beliefs and practices are consistent with Cornerstone’s confession and core commitments.

title: Staff SW Eng Back End
description:
Staff Software Engineer - Front End/ Back End

Job Number: 928

This is a remote position.

Ad Hoc is a technology company that empowers organizations to deliver scalable, impactful digital services. Using modern, agile methods, our team creates products that meet people’s needs and transform their experience of government.

Work on things that matter

Our collaborations have shaped some of the defining moments in public-sector service delivery. We’ve helped build products that connect Veterans to tailored services, help millions access affordable health care, and support important programs like Head Start. As we work with agencies to deliver critical services, we’re also changing how the government approaches technology.

Built for a remote life

Our culture, communications, and tools are built for remote work, enabling us to bring together top talent nationwide. At Ad Hoc, remote life empowers our teams to design work environments that fit their lives and that foster flexibility and collaboration to achieve positive outcomes for our customers.

Committed to high expectations and a welcoming culture

Ad Hoc values acceptance, accountability, and humility. We aren’t heroes. We learn from our mistakes and improve the process for the next time. We build small, inclusive teams to collaborate closely with our partners to solve the right problems and deliver software that works.

The Veterans Affairs business unit helps transform the VA into a modern digital services organization where Veteran outcomes are at the center of every effort. We partner with the VA to design and deliver seamless user experiences for Veterans, their families and caregivers, and VA employees. By applying better practices in service design, product management, and technology, we enable the VA to increase the use, quality, and reliability of services and decrease the time Veterans spend waiting for outcomes.

Primary Responsibilities

As a Staff Software Engineer, you’ll serve as a senior individual contributor and technical leader with a high level of trust, autonomy, and ownership. You’ll help establish technical direction, solve complex platform challenges, and improve how teams integrate with and use the Event Bus.

You will:

  • Lead the technical design and execution of next-generation platform capabilities, including easier tenant on-ramps, schema management tooling, onboarding workflows, and developer experience improvements that simplify Event Bus integration.
  • Establish technical patterns and best practices for tenant integrations, including lightweight clients, native Kafka producers, and protocol-specific listeners.
  • Work directly with producer and consumer teams across VA, providing hands-on integration support while turning lessons learned into reusable platform patterns, templates, documentation, and automation.
  • Partner closely with DevOps engineers to identify and automate operational toil and expand what the platform can automatically handle for tenant teams.
  • Plan and execute technical roadmaps for complex projects with minimal guidance from technical leadership.
  • Work across multiple technologies and languages to understand integration challenges and contribute solutions where needed.
  • Reduce ambiguity and technical debt through clear documentation, refactoring, automated testing, and improvements to existing systems.
  • Participate in planning and technical discussions with partners, product leaders, engineers, and other key stakeholders.
  • Communicate technical decisions, tradeoffs, implementation complexity, and risks in a way that helps technical and non-technical stakeholders make informed decisions.
  • Operate with a high degree of autonomy across the platform, making sound technical decisions without requiring constant oversight.
  • Mentor engineers through code reviews, technical design discussions, and hands-on collaboration while helping raise the technical bar across the team.
  • Participate in technical interviews and help evaluate engineering candidates.
  • Participate in the on-call rotation and improve tooling, documentation, and runbooks to make operational support more effective.
  • Periodically travel to collaborate with and present to clients, partners, and stakeholders.
  • Support technical demonstrations, proposals, and other client-facing activities by clearly explaining systems, architecture, design decisions, and technical outcomes.


Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree and 9+ years of professional software engineering experience. Relevant years of experience may be substituted for education.
  • Expert-level experience in at least one major technology stack, with the ability to independently lead complex technical work and help teams deliver successfully.
  • Strong software engineering fundamentals with the ability to read, understand, and contribute across multiple programming languages, including Java, Ruby, Node.js, Python, and Go.
  • Strong understanding of Kubernetes architecture and how Kubernetes operates under the hood.
  • Hands-on experience with modern continuous delivery tools such as Argo CD or equivalent.
  • Hands-on experience building and maintaining CI/CD workflows using GitHub Actions or similar tooling.
  • Experience designing, building, or supporting distributed systems in production environments.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts, architectural decisions, and tradeoffs to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience working independently on complex or ambiguous technical problems and driving them toward practical solutions.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience with Apache Kafka or another distributed event-streaming platform, particularly from a platform engineering or operational perspective.
  • Experience designing or operating internal developer platforms, developer tooling, or paved-road solutions used by other engineering teams.
  • Experience supporting integrations across multiple engineering teams, services, or technology stacks.
  • Experience working within a large or organizationally complex environment such as government, healthcare, or financial services.
  • Demonstrated ability to work across organizational silos and build alignment between engineering, infrastructure, product, and other stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with FedRAMP, FISMA, ATO, or similar compliance frameworks and an understanding of how compliance requirements influence platform architecture and engineering decisions.

To learn more about working at Ad Hoc, please visit:

Benefits:

  • Company-subsidized health, dental, and vision insurance

  • Flexible PTO

  • 401K with employer match

  • Paid parental leave after one year of service

  • Employee Assistance Program

Ad Hoc LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, age, pregnancy, disability, work-related injury, covered veteran status, political ideology, marital status, or any other factor that the law protects from employment discrimination.

We value the unique skills gained through military service and encourage veterans and transitioning service members to apply.

In support of various state and city equal pay transparency laws, Ad Hoc job descriptions feature the starting range we reasonably expect to pay to candidates who would join our team with little to no need for training on the responsibilities we've outlined above. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide range of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, and responsibility. The range of starting pay for this role is $130,000 - $150,000. Our recruiters will be happy to answer any questions you may have, and we look forward to learning more about your salary requirements.

title: Repair Tech - Commission + Free Ski Pass
description:
About Bootdoctors:

At Bootdoctors, we believe Outside is Better. It’s not just a motto, it’s a fact. It makes people happier, healthier, and more connected. That’s why we go out of our way to help people experience the mountain lifestyle by building authentic relationships, offering humble expertise, and sharing a genuine love for what we do. Driven by our unmatched passion for the outdoors, we are always advancing. In-store and online, within our industry, and with the communities we serve, we bring a spirit of innovation to every aspect of what we do. We were founded in Colorado in 1958, but we’ve been chasing adventure for much longer. Skiing and snowboarding aren’t just a job for us, it’s a lifestyle. No matter your level, we strive to give you the best experience possible and invite you to experience the joy of mountain life and sport with us.

Our Values.

We are welcoming - We meet people where they are without judgement. Whether they're seasoned veterans, first-timers, locals, or vacationers, they trust us to set them up for success with quality equipment and great service.

We are ambassadors of lifestyle - We love what makes the mountain lifestyle special: the people, the environment, and the communities. We want our guests to discover and love the mountain lifestyle as much as we do.

We are rooted in experience - By keeping the history of our roots alive, we maintain the quality service, authenticity, and expertise that our guests value and what made us special in the first place.

We are one team - We make our company a great place to work by collaborating, problem-solving, being accountable, and recognizing our accomplishments. We are each unique contributors to a greater whole.

We are always evolving - Our customer* expectations continue to evolve. To meet their needs, we must evolve to stay relevant. We embrace change and always look for the next evolution of what we can do. *Internal & External

Summary Description: As a Repair Technician, you’ll make sure our guests are set up with perfectly tuned equipment so they can enjoy the mountain to the fullest. From sharpening edges and waxing skis to handling complex repairs, you’ll use your technical skills, product knowledge, and passion for snow sports to deliver best-in-class service and keep our guests coming back.

What You’ll Be Doing (Besides Planning Your Next Powder Day):

  • Build trust with guests by providing accurate information and excellent service.
  • Assess when skis or snowboards need tuning or repair and recommend the best service option.
  • Perform ski and snowboard tuning: sharpening, waxing, mounting, drilling, and more.
  • Maintain accurate pricing and ensure promotions are up to date.
  • Keep the workshop clean, organized, and operating safely.
  • Follow all safety standards and procedures in the repair shop.
  • Monitor inventory and stay on top of industry trends and technology.
  • Support teammates and pitch in with other duties as needed.

What Makes You a Fit:

title: Trainer of Evidence Based Models
description:
The Trainer of Trainer’s (TOT) overall goal is to help workers use evidence-based models and best practices to create positive outcomes for the families in Good Shepherd’s care.   • Assist in creation and facilitation of parent and/or foster parent advisory groups to explore opportunities for continuous program improvement
  • Other duties as assigned

Requirements and Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree preferred, HS/GED required
  • Applicants must be Approved Facilitators as certified by the model developers
  • Bilingual (Spanish) preferred
  • Exemplary facilitation skills
  • Strong training and coaching skills are a must
  • Strong leadership and collaboration skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Engaging presentation style
  • Ability to maintain detailed and consistent documentation
  • Commitment to GSS mission and the use of evidence-based models to further that mission
  • Commitment to continuous professional development for self and others

title: Internship - Distributed estimation for interconnected dynamical systems
description:
MERL seeks an intern for a three month assignment to conduct research into distributed estimation and control of interconnected dynamical systems. The topic is motivated by state estimation problems associated with distributed thermofluid systems that are governed by large scale, nonlinear but sparse differential algebraic equations. The modular architecture of these systems motivates a distributed estimation and control architecture. Qualified candidates should be enrolled in a Ph.D. or equivalent program of study and have knowledge of classic and advanced methods of multivariable and nonlinear control and estimation. Experience with networked control systems or multi-agent systems is an asset.

Required Specific Experience

  • Experience with design and realization of classic and advanced nonlinear control systems.
  • Experience with design and realization of state estimation algorithms.
  • Knowledge of distributed estimation theory.
  • Experience with networked control systems or multi-agent systems.

The pay range for this internship position will be 6-8K per month.

We provide a range of programming for Vulnerable Youth/Adolescent with history of Trauma.

Job Title: Case Planner, Marian Hall

Reports to: Assistant Director of Social Services

Location: 337 E. 17th Street, New York, NY 10003

Hours: 40 Hours/Week; Non-Exempt Position requires staff to be onsite along with some field work. Some evening will be required. Hybrid Schedules are based on program needs and at leadership discretion.

Major Duties:

  • Maintain primary case planning responsibility for 16-20 cases in collaboration with the social worker.

title: Internship - 3D object detection and recognition
description:
MERL is looking for a self-motivated intern to work on 3D object detection and recognition using computer vision. The ideal candidate would be a PhD student with a strong background in computer vision and machine learning, and the candidate is expected to have published at least one paper in a top-tier computer vision, machine learning, or artificial intelligence venues, such as CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS, AAAI, etc. Proficiency in Python programming and familiarity in at least one deep learning framework are necessary. title: Commissioning Technician
description:
The Role: Commissioning Technician

Pay: $30 - $36 per hour, based on experience.

The Commissioning Technician supports the startup, commissioning, and ongoing performance of process equipment and automated systems. This hands-on role provides electro-mechanical and automation support at customer facilities and performs factory acceptance testing at CSI.

You’ll work closely with CSI’s Controls Engineering team and customers across industries including food, dairy, beverage, personal care, pharmaceutical, biotech, and nutraceutical manufacturing. Frequent overnight, extended-stay, weekend, and after-hours support may be required.

This is a travel-forward position. The Commissioning Technician is based at CSI's Springfield facility and works extensively at customer sites across the United States. Travel averages approximately 50 to 60% of scheduled workdays and varies with project schedules and customer requirements.

If you enjoy hands-on troubleshooting, solving technical challenges, and helping customers get their systems running safely and reliably, this is your kind of role.

About CSI

CSI provides state-of-the-art stainless-steel process equipment and service for manufacturers in the food, dairy, beverage, pharmaceutical, and personal care industries.

We are a growing company built on teamwork, continuous learning, and exceptional customer service. Our employees are our greatest resource, and we invest in their development through training, collaboration, and opportunities to grow.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Commissioning & Startup
  • Start up, commission, and provide sustaining support for automated process equipment and systems at customer facilities.
  • Troubleshoot mechanical systems, electrical circuits, instrumentation, and automation controls during startup and early production.
  • Perform factory acceptance testing (FAT) at CSI, including electrical and mechanical equipment hook-up in accordance with safety requirements.
  • Train customers on proper system operation and maintenance, respond to support requests, and provide after-hours assistance when systems are coming online.

Education/Experience

  • High School Diploma or equivalent, required.
  • Associate degree in Electromechanical or Mechatronic Technology, or equivalent, preferred. Valid driver’s license, required.
  • 4+ years of related experience and/or training, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
  • Maintenance or production experience in a food manufacturing plant; awareness of food safety and continuous improvement
  • Experience troubleshooting and repairing mechanical systems and electrical circuits/equipment using 480VAC/3/60, 120 VAC/1/60, and 24 VDC power
  • Allen-Bradley PLC programming and Rockwell Software experience, preferred

Why CSI

  • Competitive compensation: $30-$36 per hour.
  • Opportunity to work on specialized stainless-steel process systems across multiple industries
  • Hands-on role with direct impact on quality, safety, and customer satisfaction
  • Collaborative team environment focused on continuous improvement
  • Career growth opportunities within installation, operations, and leadership teams
  • Company culture centered on taking care of employees and customers

Benefits & Perks

CSI offers a competitive benefits package including:

  • Health and wellness benefits
  • Paid time off
  • Retirement planning options
  • Tuition reimbursement and continuing education support
  • Opportunities for internal career advancement
  • Company lunches, team events, and community volunteer opportunities

Work Environment / Physical Requirements

Travel Requirements: Extensive overnight and weekend travel is a required and essential function of this position.

  • Travel averages approximately 50 to 60% of scheduled workdays over a year and varies with project schedules and customer requirements.
  • During active startup and commissioning assignments, the technician remains at the customer site for the duration of the assignment, typically approximately one week.
  • Technicians typically return home between assignments, subject to project schedules and customer requirements.
  • During periods focused on factory acceptance testing at CSI's Springfield facility, travel is typically 20 to 25%.
  • Assignments are at customer facilities across the United States. Travel may be by air or company vehicle.
  • This role is CSI's first responder for weekend and after-hours support during startup and early production.
  • A valid driver's license is required, as is the ability to meet the travel requirements described above.
  • CSI provides required tools, travel, hotel accommodations, meals, and other miscellaneous travel expenses associated with the position.

More than 40 hours per week will normally be required in order to achieve the productivity necessary for this position. Overnight travel, Saturday, Sunday and holiday hours may be required.

This is an hands-on role in a manufacturing environment.

  • Frequent bending, kneeling, and stooping throughout the shift
  • Lifting and moving materials up to 75 lbs (with assistance)
  • Use of close, distance, and peripheral vision with strong attention to detail
  • Exposure to typical grinding and polishing conditions (noise, dust, etc.)
  • Required use of PPE including gloves, safety glasses, and steel-toe boots

CSI is committed to providing reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities during the application and employment process.

Equal Opportunity Employer

CSI is committed to equal opportunity employment. We select candidates based on their ability to perform the work in a competent and professional manner and do not discriminate based on age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or disability.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. CSI participates in E-Verify.

title: ADAS Calibration Technician & Analyst
description:
SUMMARY:

This role is a mobile position traveling throughout the assigned territory utilizing a company vehicle.

The ADAS Technician & Analyst is a hybrid role that combines both technical calibration responsibilities and analytical duties to ensure vehicles are restored to OEM safety and performance standards. This role works onsite within a CollisionRight repair center, performing dynamic and static calibrations, while also reviewing scan data, interpreting repair estimates, and coordinating with both internal and external teams. The position bridges technician execution with analyst-level oversight, providing a seamless workflow for ADAS calibration.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Calibration Responsibilities:

  • Perform static and dynamic calibrations in accordance with OEM procedures.

  • Use scan tools and calibration systems to restore ADAS components post-collision.

  • Maintain proper documentation of completed calibrations and work performed.

  • Conduct pre- and post-scans to support proper repair workflows.

  • Perform module programming as required to complete repairs and restore system functionality.

  • Troubleshoot diagnostic fault codes and address failed calibrations to determine root cause and next steps.

Analyst Responsibilities:

  • Analyze vehicle system scan data to determine required calibrations.

  • Review collision damage and repair estimates to confirm ADAS impact.

  • Research OEM procedures using approved service information tools.

  • Communicate ADAS needs to shop estimators, technicians, and leadership.

  • Ensure documentation, scan reports, and calibration records are uploaded and tracked accurately.

Collaboration & Workflow:

  • Work onsite daily at an assigned CollisionRight repair center.

  • Maintain a strong relationship with shop staff while reporting directly to 360Align leadership.

  • Support scheduling and prioritization of calibrations to ensure timely repair delivery.

  • Collaborate with centralized ADAS analysts, technicians, and managers for ongoing support.

Additional Responsibilities:

  • Maintain up-to-date training and certifications as required.

  • Participate in feedback sessions and process refinement to enhance ADAS workflows.

  • Adhere to all company and body shop safety procedures and policies.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years of experience in automotive diagnostics, collision repair, or ADAS calibrations.

  • Working knowledge of ADAS components and calibration procedures.

  • Ability to read and interpret scan data and collision repair estimates.

  • Strong communication and customer service skills.

  • Experience with OEM service software and scan tools preferred.

  • I-CAR, ASE, or manufacturer certifications preferred.

  • Ability to work independently onsite while collaborating remotely with the broader ADAS team.

  • Self-motivated with strong organizational and time management skills.

  • Must have a valid driver’s license and clean MVR.

  • Ability to work 8+ hours in a shop environment and use computers/mobile devices efficiently.

This position description is intended to be dynamic and subject to change. Position requirements and essential functions may be altered from time to time based upon the needs of the organization and department. This position may be required to execute special projects or other related duties on occasion.

title: Territory Vice President, Central

title: Manager, AI and Data Governance Operations
description:
Location: Atlanta (Full-time, Hybrid)

Fisher Phillips, a premier international labor and employment law firm, is seeking a Manager, AI and Data Governance Operations to support responsible AI adoption and information management.

Position Summary

Reporting to the Director of Information Governance, the manager serves as the central coordinator for AI and data governance across Innovation, IT, Information Security, Privacy, General Counsel, and business owners. The role leads IG’s information and privacy compliance activities and coordinates assessments, evidence, remediation, and reporting across accountable teams.

Each functional owner remains responsible for policies, decisions, controls, and enforcement within its area. Innovation leads AI implementation and adoption; Security leads security assessments and technical security requirements; IT handles day-to-day platform and service administration. General Counsel provides legal interpretation, and business owners validate data and fitness for use. Authorized firm leaders approve exceptions and accept risk through established processes.

Key Responsibilities

AI Governance Coordination

  • Coordinate AI governance procedures and policy updates with functional owners, documenting responsibilities and routing approvals through established firm processes
  • Coordinate reviews of AI tools, connectors, agents, integrations, and material changes within existing intake and delivery processes; conduct IG assessments and consolidate other teams’ findings
  • Engage Innovation, IT, Security, Privacy, and business sponsors early to identify requirements and align review timelines with project priorities
  • Agree on remediation owners, completion criteria, and dates; track progress and escalate unresolved findings
  • Document applicable requirements and accountable owners with General Counsel and other specialists, relying on each function for its assessments and conclusions
  • Develop reusable review criteria with functional owners to make assessments consistent and timely
  • Manage assigned IG staff and personally perform assessments, evidence reviews, and issue resolution
  • Coordinate governance evidence for client inquiries, audits, and outside counsel guideline reviews
  • Monitor AI governance developments and recommend relevant updates with subject matter experts
  • Support Innovation’s implementation and adoption efforts by resolving information governance requirements and dependencies

Data Governance and Lifecycle Management

  • Develop information governance standards with relevant owners for classification, appropriate access and use, retention, and information protection
  • Work with department leaders to document data owners, stewards, and approved uses of information
  • Coordinate privacy, access, retention, preservation, and disposition requirements with responsible teams, including information used by AI and transferred during partner transitions

Data Quality and Stewardship

  • Help business owners define data quality expectations and document information sources and limitations for AI use cases
  • Coordinate data quality remediation; business owners validate accuracy and fitness for use, while IT implements system and integration changes
  • Support data stewards in improving information maintenance and preventing recurring quality issues

Stakeholder Coordination and Enablement

  • Maintain IG’s work plan aligned with firm portfolio priorities and agreed responsibilities and timelines
  • Communicate requirements and escalate policy questions, exceptions, and unresolved risks to accountable owners and authorized leaders
  • Partner with training and support teams to explain approved uses, information handling requirements, and user responsibilities

Controls and Ongoing Oversight

  • Define IG requirements for classification, access, retention, and DLP with relevant owners; review supporting evidence while Security and IT assess, implement, and operate their assigned controls
  • Maintain governance records in the shared AI inventory, including uses, data sources, owners, review findings, approvals, and exceptions
  • Coordinate periodic reviews and reassessment when data sources, access, capabilities, or service status change

Governance Tools and Reporting

  • Translate information governance requirements into platform workflows with IT, which owns day-to-day administration, configuration, and operational support
  • Consolidate owners’ compliance findings and report outstanding issues, remediation progress, and review timeliness to the IG Director and designated firm leaders
  • Provide governance readiness findings to designated release owners and confirm that ongoing control, review, and support responsibilities are assigned

Qualifications

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Management, Business, Technology, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience
  • Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in information governance, data governance, information protection, or related technology operations
  • Experience translating information governance requirements into practical processes and working with IT on controls
  • Working knowledge of enterprise AI services, connectors, agents, data flows, access models, and information lifecycle risks
  • Experience coordinating cross-functional reviews and managing staff or operational work, with clear communication and sound judgment

Preferred:

  • Experience in a law firm or professional services organization and familiarity with client and matter intake, conflicts, document management, or financial systems
  • Experience with Microsoft 365, Microsoft Purview, iManage, or comparable information protection and governance platforms
  • Experience handling sensitive information and applying privacy, confidentiality, retention, and client requirements in collaboration with relevant subject matter experts

Key Competencies

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities
  • Accountability for IG responsibilities and effective coordination across functional owners
  • Ability to balance staff leadership with hands-on assessment and issue resolution
  • Service-oriented approach to change management, process improvement, and cross-functional delivery

Pay will be determined by several components, including but not limited to, location, relevant experience, internal equity, skills, qualifications, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

Why Join Us

At Fisher Phillips, we recognize that exceptional talent is the foundation of our success, enabling us to deliver outstanding service to both our internal and external clients. Joining our team means collaborating in a professional yet dynamic environment that leverages cutting-edge technology. Our leadership is committed to fostering your professional growth and providing opportunities to challenge yourself in meaningful ways.

We believe in rewarding talent with more than just a competitive salary. Our comprehensive benefits package includes health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) with profit sharing, generous paid time off, and holidays.

Your well-being is our priority. We offer 24/7 telehealth services, a variety of wellness programs, and additional optional benefits designed to support your unique lifestyle. Fisher Phillips is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants, regardless of race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including related medical conditions), gender, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, age, disability, or any other protected status, in compliance with all applicable laws.

title: Senior Advisor, Budgeting & Resource Planning
description:
Summary: The Senior Advisor serves as ASTHO’s subject matter expert in budgeting, financial planning, forecasting, project financial management, and resource allocation. The position provides strategic and technical guidance to program and operational teams, strengthens financial planning practices, and promotes consistent, accurate, and data-informed decision-making across the organization. The Senior Advisor leads the development and continuous improvement of budgeting methodologies, systems, tools, and standards; supports the implementation and optimization of the organization’s ERP system; and ensures that proposal budgets and funded activities align with organizational priorities, funder requirements, and applicable policies.

Location: Remote

Anticipated salary: $124,300 up to $153,100

Principal Functions:

  • Strengthens budgeting, forecasting, and project financial-management practices across U.S. government, foundation, philanthropic, private-sector, and other funding sources
  • Provides strategic and technical guidance to program and operational teams on budget development, financial planning, forecasting, cost management, and resource allocation
  • Develops and oversees methodologies for personnel budgeting, labor distribution, and effort planning to ensure staffing costs are appropriately allocated across grants, contracts, and organizational initiatives
  • Leads the modernization and continuous improvement of budgeting and forecasting processes by developing standardized methodologies, templates, workflows, controls, and guidance
  • Reduces reliance on manual processes by identifying opportunities for automation, system integration, and improved use of financial and operational data
  • Supports the development and implementation of the organization’s ERP system, including business requirements, automated workflows, reporting needs, dashboards, and data visualization, ensuring financial data supports timely decision-making
  • Develops and monitors key performance indicators for the budgeting and forecasting function, using data to improve accuracy, cycle times, forecast reliability, and customer service
  • Reviews proposal budgets, budget narratives, funding assumptions, indirect cost applications, fringe rates, and other financial components of funding submissions
  • Supports the development and review of budgets for requests for proposals, grant applications, contracts, and other funding opportunities
  • Assesses project financial performance and provide recommendations to improve budget accuracy, cost management, and bottom-line results
  • Identifies financial risks, funding gaps, overages, and underutilized resources, and provide scenario-based recommendations to program and organizational leadership
  • Develops and standardizes budgeting templates, financial planning tools, guidance documents, and operating procedures
  • Strengthens coordination among Program Operations, Grants, Finance, and programmatic teams throughout the proposal development and project implementation lifecycle
  • Provides guidance to program teams to ensure that project activities and expenditures are consistent with approved budgets, funder expectations, and organizational policies
  • Partners with cross-functional teams to improve the quality, consistency, and accessibility of financial and operational data
  • Develops reports and analyses that support leadership decision-making, resource allocation, and long-term financial planning
  • Drive process improvements that enhance operational efficiency, financial accountability, and compliance with funder and audit requirements
  • Supports other strategic initiatives that contribute to the organization’s long-term financial and operational health.

Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in finance, business administration, public administration, nonprofit management, accounting, or related field preferred
  • Minimum 7 years of progressively responsible experience in budgeting, financial management, grants management, business planning, or nonprofit operations
  • Extensive experience developing, reviewing, and managing complex projects and organizational budgets
  • Demonstrated experience with foundation, philanthropic, private sector, or other non-federal funding sources
  • Strong understanding of indirect cost rates, fringe benefit rates, cost allocation, budget forecasting, and project financial performance
  • Experience reviewing proposal budgets, budget narratives, grant agreements, contracts, and funder requirements
  • Experience developing and delivering financial management or budgeting training to non-financial staff
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex financial information into clear and actionable recommendations
  • Experience supporting ERP implementation, system design, business requirements, financial reporting, or process improvement initiatives
  • Proficiency with financial systems, budgeting tools, reporting platforms, spreadsheets, dashboards, and data visualization tools
  • Ability to manage multiple complex priorities and work effectively across departments and organizational levels
  • Ability to communicate effectively both orally and in writing
  • Strong collaboration, facilitation, and relationship management skills
  • Knowledge of nonprofit financial management, funder compliance, and grants administration principles preferred
  • Knowledge of federal grants administration, including familiarity with OMB Uniform Guidance, preferred
  • Ability and willingness to travel

Benefits:

  • Vacation leave, Sick leave, Personal days
  • 12 Holidays (with some floating options for personalization)
  • Medical, Dental, and Vision
  • Retirement Plans – 403B and Roth 403B, eligible employees can receive a company contribution up to 11.75%
  • Electronic communication stipend

  • Additional Benefits include: Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Pet Insurance, Legal Resources, Health & Wellness reimbursement, Flexible Spending accounts, Tuition Reimbursement, and Professional Development Assistance

title: Senior Credit Analyst - FI Connect
description:

We think like owners, embrace complexity and ambiguity, challenge conventional thinking, and continuously pursue smarter, more effective ways to solve problems and advance the business. We value people who are adaptable, resourceful, and committed to delivering quality outcomes while continuously looking for ways to improve. Ensure that all relevant information is captured and assessed to render the best possible decision on behalf of CUDC clients. Appropriately document all relevant details and rationale for decisions.
  • Follow up with lenders, applicants, and origination sources (e.g. dealers) to ensure that all relevant information and documentation is completed in accordance with lender guidance, and to ensure that CUDC maximizes the share of loans funded to approved opportunities for its lenders.

Create, manage, and analyze reports and metrics to effectively manage application pipelines, operational efficiencies, service levels, and value for CUDC clients and partners.

Actively contribute on cross-functional projects within the organization and with external stakeholders as a subject matter expert in credit analysis and loan originations on behalf of the BPO function for CU Direct.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent mix of education and relevant experience required.

Experience

  • Ten years of credit analysis/underwriting experience in within a financial institution or equivalent provider is required.
  • Proven experience working in a capacity where conflicting objectives (e.g. risk vs growth or speed vs quality) must be balanced and effectively managed.
  • Knowledge of lending operations, regulatory compliance and indirect auto lending experience is required. Additional lending experience (leasing, mortgage, retail finance, etc.) is preferred.
  • Experience adjacent to underwriting (e.g. processing, funding, QA, etc.) is a plus.

Your Strengths & Expertise

  • Exceptional service-orientation for customers as well as internal and external partners.
  • Excellent communication (oral/written) and analytical skills required.
  • Must be able to work independently with a high degree of personal initiative to establish goals, organize and prioritize work, and meet aggressive deadlines.
  • Capable of effectively engaging with stakeholders at all levels of an organization, from line-level staff to senior executives.
  • Proven ability to deliver results in a fast-paced environment with competing objectives and shifting priorities.
  • Computer knowledge with Microsoft Office programs to include: Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

Bring your attention to detail, problem-solving mindset, and unique perspective. We'll provide the opportunities, tools, and support to help you succeed.

How We Invest in You:

  • 401(k) with 8% Company Match
  • Flexible Work Environment
  • Competitive Paid Time Off
  • Tuition Reimbursement & Education Benefits
  • Comprehensive Health & Wellness Benefits
  • Microsoft Copilot and AI-Enabled Tools
  • Continuous Learning & Development Opportunities
  • A culture of connection, celebration, and growth through employee-driven programs, company events, holiday celebrations (Star Wars Day), monthly town halls, quarterly company meetings, and team traditions like Bring Your Kid to Work Day

Recognizing Your Impact

The starting salary range for this full-time position is $59000- $73700 per year. We offer competitive compensation designed to recognize the value, experience, and contributions each team member brings to Origence. Base pay is determined by factors including experience, geographic location, and internal equity, and eligible positions may participate in our annual bonus program.

Origence is an equal opportunity employer. All recruitment, hiring, training, compensation, benefits, discipline, and other terms and conditions of employment will be based upon an individuals’ qualifications regardless of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, military service, marital status, pregnancy, age, protected medical condition, genetic information, disability or any other category protected by federal, state or local law

Remote within the United States; shifts within 6:30 am-12:30 am ET Monday-Friday and Saturday; rotating 24/7 on-call with a Government laptop.
