title: Education Specialist (EFFC)
description:
The Education Specialist is responsible for meeting the educational needs of youth ages 0 to 5 years old. Additionally, he/she is responsible for monitoring the developmental needs of youth in the early childhood stages, including but not limited to, making referrals as deemed necessary to Early Intervention and/or Committee on Pre-School Education (CPSE). Build and maintain healthy rapport with parent/guardians of youth. Develop and maintain professional relationships with NYC Department of Education, Committee on Pre-School Education liaisons, and Early Intervention liaison, NYC Administration for Children Services, and other school related partnerships.

Title: Education Specialist

Reports To: Special Services Supervisor, Family Foster Care

Location: 7 West Burnside Avenue, 2nd Floor, Bronx, NY 10453

Hours: 35 Hours/Week; Non-Exempt

Major Duties:

  • Review new intakes and psychological screenings/evaluations for the assigned age group to ensure that developmental and/or educational concerns are addressed.
  • Assist parents/guardians and case planning team with initiating early intervention and/or CPSE evaluation processes.
  • Submit and monitor the progress of all referrals and evaluations for special education services and/or early intervention services for youth.
  • Provide continuous support and trainings to foster parents, parents, and case planning team as it relates to education and/or early intervention services for youth in foster care.
  • Serve as the agency liaison for school staff, early intervention, and guardians.
  • Attend and represent special services team at mandatory agency and ACS trainings, NYC DOE trainings to remain up to date on policies and procedures.
  • Maintain professional boundaries with youth, foster parents, parents, and staff.
  • Keep case records and education data information up to date and filed in the appropriate section of the case record.
  • Commit to working from a strength based prospective.
  • Document progress notes in Connections.
  • Outreach and maintain ongoing communication with foster parents and parents to ensure that they are aware of the youth’s educational and/or developmental needs and are communicating with school and/or early intervention personnel.
  • Attend and participate in IFSP (Individualized Family Service Plans), CPSE, and Turning 5 meetings.
  • Ensures that all documentation of services is obtained and filed in the appropriate education section of the case record.
  • Works with Advocates for Children and other outside organizations if legal or other advocacy is needed to ensure the child’s eligibility and access to early intervention and CPSE services.
  • Works with parents and foster parents to ensure that they are aware of the child’s educational needs and are engaged with the early intervention service coordinators and/or CPSE administrators.
  • Generates statistics and outcome information on education issues as required.
  • Effectively use and practice the Sanctuary Model tools: safety plans, community meetings, psycho-educational groups, team meetings, red flag reviews, treatment planning conferences (or similar) and self-care, when applicable, in the department/program to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Promote and model the seven Sanctuary Model commitments to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelors degree required with at least 1year experience special education and early intervention
  • Solid knowledge of the NYC public school system including education resources, children’s rights and DOE regulations/procedures.
  • Bi-lingual (English/Spanish) preferred.
  • Experience with special education and early intervention
  • Ability to be flexible to meet the demands of youth in care
  • Ability to work autonomously as well as part of a team
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office suite, especially Word and Excel
  • Excellent written, communication. And organizational skills
  • Must have a commitment to work from a strength based and/or youth & family development perspective.

title: Director of Pharmacy
location: Warsaw NY, Buffalo NY, Rochester NY, Olean NY
description:
CompleteRx is seeking a Director of Pharmacy to help provide exceptional patient care at a 25-bed critical access hospital located in Warsaw, NY.

As the Director of Pharmacy, you will provide strategic leadership and operational oversight for at our partnered hospital, Wyoming County Community Health System, while having the support and expertise of CompleteRx’s operations team as a resource. In this role, your leadership, clinical expertise, and commitment to innovation will help advance pharmacy services and enhance patient care for the communities served by the health system.

Compensation:

  • $155,000 - $173,000

Pharmacy Operating Hours:

  • Monday – Friday: 7am – 5pm
  • Saturday & Holidays: 7am – 3pm
  • Sunday: Closed

Hospital Overview:

Wyoming County Community Health System (WCCHS) is a county-owned health system based in Warsaw, NY, anchored by a 25-bed Critical Access Hospital and a 10-bed inpatient Behavioral Health Unit. The hospital provides 24/7 emergency care and supports a full range of hospital-based departments and inpatient/outpatient services. WCCHS serves patients across Wyoming County and surrounding communities through a strong network of primary and specialty services.

Why Join CompleteRx?

At CompleteRx, we believe healthcare should be about serving others. That's why our mission is to deliver better care and better service, through innovation. The goal of our exceptional teams is to perform like champions. This means we are committed to being the best at delivering quality care to the patients we serve. Each team member's dedication is essential to meeting and exceeding the needs of our patients and families.

What You Will Do

Evaluates operations on an ongoing basis to ensure safe, appropriate, cost-effective care delivery

  • Develops, enforces, and maintains policies and procedures that promote cost-effective, appropriate, and safe drug use.
  • Evaluates operations on an ongoing basis using principles of continuous process improvement.
  • Develops, implements, checks, and retools action plans to address variances and improve efficiency.
  • Develops and maintains a medical-staff-approved formulary.
  • Supervises drug storage and preparation areas throughout the hospital.
  • Provides for the educational needs of healthcare professionals and patients and their families.
  • Ensures maintenance of an adequate drug supply. Ensures the integrity of the drug supply. Establishes specifications for the procurement of drugs, chemicals, and biologicals.
  • Ensures strict control and accountability for drugs dispensed to patients or distributed to floor stock.
  • Assures adequate control and documentation of controlled substances.
  • Maintains a quality improvement plan for the department
  • Ensures the pharmacy is in compliance with all federal, state, and other regulatory agency laws and standards.

Supervises, trains, mentors, and evaluates staff.

  • Supervises pharmacy personnel.
  • Develops job descriptions, performance standards, and performance goals.
  • Evaluates and counsels staff on their performance.
  • Prepares work schedules and monitors workload statistics. Maintains an appropriate staffing level.
  • Provides for the educational needs of the pharmacy staff.
  • Acts as a positive role model, mentor, and preceptor.
  • Promotes individual professional growth.
  • Communicates with staff and promotes staff ownership in problem-solving and participation in operational decision-making.

Prepares annual budget, controls and reduces costs, forecasts operational needs, and reviews expenditures to ensure budget limits are not exceeded.

  • Prepares a pharmacy budget annually.
  • Reviews monthly financial statistics and plans expenditures within budget guidelines.
  • Monitors and justifies all expenses exceeding budgeted targets.
  • Ensures preparation and submission of patient charges and financial reports to administration in accordance with hospital policy.
  • Administers reports, documents, payroll records, employee surveys, and other required data.
  • Ensures applicable CE records and licensures are maintained in department files.
  • Ensures compliance with hospital policies and procedures that apply to pharmacy services.
  • Ensures compliance with all applicable Federal, State, and local laws, rules, and regulations.

Establishes the scope of services and develops annual implementation plans which contribute to the organizational strategic objectives.

  • Develop and implement a strategic plan for the pharmacy that supports the mission and goals of the organization.
  • Develop and implement pharmacy services in collaboration with associated department services.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain a program that improves the quality of pharmacy services and supports the quality improvement plan of the organization.
  • Participate in all committees/functions required by the organization including the Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee.
  • Establish productive collaborative relationships with physicians, nursing, administration, and other hospital staff.
  • Meet customers' needs and expectations.

Maintains competency required for current job title/position:

  • Maintain current pharmacist license.
  • Attend management meetings.
  • Sustain professional competency and promotes development through participation in in-services, workshops, seminars, and professional organizations.
  • Complete all competency/skills assessment requirements
  • Is punctual and dependable.
  • Maintain a neat, professional, well-groomed appearance. Wears identification badge.
  • Perform work within specified time frames. Adapts positively to frequent interruptions and changes in workload and/or work schedule.
  • Provide courteous, cooperative, and timely service to patients, visitors, and staff. Demonstrates good verbal and written communication.
  • Work cooperatively with hospital and pharmacy staff. Voice concerns and suggestions to appropriate persons in a positive manner. Foster a team environment.
  • Demonstrate sound professional judgment consistent with clinical/academic background.
  • Maintain strict confidentiality of patients, guests, and employee information.
  • Comply with all requirements related to risk management, safety, security, fire, and infection control.

What You Will Need

  • Bachelor of Science or PharmD degree required.
  • Current license, in good standing, to practice pharmacy in the State of New York.
  • Three (3) years of management experience.
  • Three to five (3-5) years of hospital pharmacy experience is required.

Compensation & Benefits:

As an employee of CompleteRx, your commitment to learning will be encouraged and supported through ongoing training and professional development. We nurture a collaborative, high-performance culture and offer a challenging career along with a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Medical, dental, and vision
  • Flexible Spending Account or Health Savings Account
  • Vacation and sick time
  • Continuing education: Eligible employees have access to a full complement of continuing-education courses as well as a wide variety of career development opportunities.
  • 401(k) plans: CompleteRx offers a 401(k) plan with a company match.
  • License Reimbursement
  • Short and Long-Term Disability

Company Description:

Founded in 1998 as a service-driven organization with a strong sense of community, CompleteRx embarked on a strategy to become the employer of choice in hospital pharmacy management and consulting. Since our founding, we believe our success has been driven by our employees who are our most valuable resources. We believe the very best outcomes are accomplished when all employees share a sense of mutual ownership for successful results and where each employee accepts personal accountability for their individual contributions. These beliefs are the core of our Team Covenant which guides all of our actions to the patients we care for, hospitals we support, and fellow employees we work alongside.

CompleteRx is an Equal Opportunity Employer by choice.

description:

title: Youth Ministry Director at Fort Jackson, South Carolina
description:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.

Salary:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Location:

Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:

In the USA:

  • Fort Rucker, Alabama
  • Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), Alaska
  • Fort Irwin, California
  • Camp Pendleton, California
  • Travis Air Force Base, California
  • Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling (JBAB), Washington, D.C.
  • Eglin Air Force Base, Florida
  • Fort Benning, Georgia
  • Fort Stewart, Georgia
  • Fort Riley, Kansas
  • Fort Bragg, North Carolina
  • Fort Sill, Oklahoma
  • Fort Jackson, South Carolina
  • Fort Belvoir, Virginia

Overseas:

  • Geilenkirchen, Germany and various other locations in Germany
  • Naval Base Guam
  • Aviano Air Base, Italy
  • Vicenza, Italy
  • Camp Zama, Japan
  • Yokosuka, Japan

Contact us through:
Robert Raedeke: RecruitingTeam@clubbeyond.org

Want to know more about our mission and culture?

Please check out clubbeyond.org to learn how Club Beyond has been changing the lives of military teens for over 40 years!

title: Manager, Tender & Contracts Operations
description:
As a global healthcare company, Fresenius Kabi is Committed to Life. The company’s products, technologies, and services are used for the therapy and care of critically and chronically ill patients. With more than 41,000 employees and presence in over 100 countries, Fresenius Kabi’s expansive product portfolio focuses on providing access to high-quality and lifesaving medicines and technologies.

WHAT WE OFFER!

At Fresenius Kabi Canada we foster a collaborative environment where employees are encouraged to share ideas and contribute to meaningful work. We offer unique learning opportunities to grow and build your career. In addition, we value each and every contributor and offer various benefits and rewards (as applicable) including:

  • Company paid health and dental benefits that start on your first day of employment
  • Company matched RRSP program
  • Generous vacation plan with one extra day accrual for each year of service
  • Paid float days and paid sick days
  • Employee assistance program
  • Casual office dress code
  • Employee recognition program
  • Perkopolis & Goodlife Discounts
  • Professional growth and development opportunities

We are currently seeking a Manager, Tender & Contracts Operations (French-English bilingualism strongly preferred) to join our team

The pay range for this role is: $123,00.00-$150,00.000

Placement within the range will be determined based on relevant skills, experience, qualifications, and internal equity. The final offer will reflect the successful candidate's background and demonstrated capabilities.

This position is an existing vacancy within the organization.

The Manager, Tender & Contracts Operations is responsible for leading the end-to-end tender and contract lifecycle, ensuring effective execution, governance, compliance, and management of contractual obligations for all business units within Canada. Develops and maintains systems for coordinating information flow regarding tenders, contracts pricing and capacity while continuing to focus on customer and company-wide business priorities. Manages and supports efforts of Product Managers, Business Unit Managers and sales representatives across all business units in relation to GPOs and across all customer types.

Job Responsibilities

  • Fosters a work environment conducive to an engaged team by leading by example and managing according to engagement principles and learnings.
  • Plans staffing levels and partners with Human Resources to recruit, interview, and select employees for the department.
  • Provides guidance, direction, coaching, and oversight to department employees to ensure they are properly trained and that resources are used effectively and efficiently.
  • Directly manages Contracts Department staff, assigns work, and ensures the timely completion of departmental responsibilities.
  • Proactively monitors relevant markets and tendering channels to identify applicable tender opportunities and bring them forward to the appropriate business units for evaluation and potential product submission.
  • Leads cross-functional tender submissions, coordinating all required inputs and approvals to ensure complete, accurate, and timely submissions.
  • Develops a thorough understanding of tender requirements and commercial implications, providing business units with informed insights and proactively identifying opportunities, risks, and key considerations to support sound bid decisions.
  • Serves as a customer-facing representative for tender and contract matters, participating in meetings with current and prospective customers to understand requirements, address contractual and commercial matters, and support strong customer relationships
  • Actively gathers market and customer insights through customer interactions, industry conferences, and external engagements, and shares relevant trends, opportunities, risks, and competitive intelligence across the organization.
  • Conducts a thorough final review of tender submissions prior to release, ensuring all information is complete, accurate, consistent, and compliant with tender requirements.
  • Ensures all new and existing contract pricing, rebates, chargebacks, and related commercial terms are accurately maintained across all applicable systems, including ERP and contract databases.
  • Manages the timely communication of tenders, tender awards and losses, and contract renewals to relevant stakeholders.
  • Partners closely with business units and Legal to ensure contractual terms are clear, comprehensive, commercially sound, and appropriately protect the Company’s interests while managing risk.
  • Owns the end-to-end contract lifecycle management process, ensuring contracts are effectively implemented and managed from execution through compliance, amendments, renewals, and termination.
  • Actively monitors and addresses contract obligations, milestones, pricing, and associated risks.
  • Owns and maintains accurate and timely reporting for customers, internal stakeholders, and senior management, ensuring all reporting requirements and deadlines are consistently met. Oversees the contract management system (Salesforce module) to ensure it is maintained in accordance with Company expectations.
  • Oversees the development and maintenance of standard operating procedures for the Tender and Contracts Operations function.
  • Maintains professional interactions with key customers, buying groups, and distribution partners, including MDP and McKesson, ensuring all interactions align with Company values.
  • Leads continuous improvement initiatives by proactively identifying process gaps, inefficiencies, and emerging risks, and implementing sustainable solutions to improve performance and strengthen controls.
  • Performs other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

College diploma or undergraduate degree, combined with three to five years of contract administration and/or contract management experience. Prior experience in the healthcare or pharmaceutical industry is preferred.

Skills

  • French-English bilingualism is strongly preferred due to the nature of customer, tender, and contract interactions across Canada.
  • Excellent leadership skills, with strong written and verbal communication abilities.
  • Demonstrated customer service orientation and the ability to collaborate effectively with stakeholders at all levels, both internally and externally.
  • Strong computer proficiency in Microsoft Office and PowerPoint, with advanced knowledge of SAP and experience working with enterprise business systems.
  • Self-motivated and capable of working independently with minimal supervision. Strong attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and adapt to changing workloads.
  • Excellent organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and continuous improvement skills. Proven ability to follow established standards and procedures while maintaining confidentiality.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze and interpret data, conduct investigations, and solve problems independently. Strong business acumen, sound judgment, and advanced critical thinking skills.
  • Above-average abilities in decision-making, writing, information gathering, document organization, and information retention. Excellent follow-up, project management, and execution skills.

MORE ABOUT US!

As ONE team, the companies in the Fresenius Group are committed to providing lifesaving and life-changing healthcare solutions on a global scale.

In Biopharma, Fresenius Kabi offers cutting-edge biosimilars for autoimmune diseases and oncology. With leading market positions in Clinical Nutrition, a broad portfolio of enteral and parenteral products makes a distinct difference in patients’ nutritional status. In MedTech, the company provides vital infusion pumps, cell and gene therapy devices, disposables, and more. Fresenius Kabi is the global leader in supplying blood collection bags and devices, supporting blood banks and healthcare facilities worldwide. The company’s I.V. Generics and Fluids for infusion therapy help save millions of lives every year, in emergency medicine, surgery, oncology, and intensive care.

Fresenius Kabi takes a holistic approach to healthcare and uniquely combines experience, expertise, innovation, and dedication – making a difference in the lives of almost 450 million patients annually.

Inclusion and Equal Opportunity Employment

At Fresenius Kabi Canada, we embrace diversity and inclusion for innovation and growth. We are committed to building inclusive teams and an equitable workplace for our employees to bring their true selves to work. We are taking actions to tackle issues of inequity and systemic bias to support our diverse talent, clients and communities. We are an equal opportunity employer.

In accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005 and the Ontario Human Rights Code, we are committed to providing accommodations and will work with candidates to meet their needs and provide an accessible candidate experience. If you are a person with a disability and require assistance during the application process, please let us know (hrcanada@fresenius-kabi.com). We welcome members of all backgrounds, experiences and perspectives to apply.

Moderate to heavy physical effort throughout the work day. Must be able to walk, stand and stoop for up to 80% of the work day. May be exposed to the elements (heat, cold, rain); work in area with high voltage electricity, hazardous equipment and moving parts; and work on roof tops and other high places. Must be able to set up and climb ladders safely with tools and equipment necessary for assigned work. Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs. When lifting loads over 50 lbs., use two or more people. It is your responsibility to ask for assistance. Must be able to push and/or pull wheeled carts and equipment generally weighing up to 300 lbs. May be exposed to communicable diseases including HIV and Hepatitis B viruses; industrial and household chemicals; and offensive odors.

title: Content Management and Operations Lead (Drupal)
description:
Content Management and Operations Lead (Drupal)

Job Number: 984

This is a remote position.

Ad Hoc is a technology company that empowers organizations to deliver scalable, impactful digital services. Using modern, agile methods, our team creates products that meet people’s needs and transform their experience of government.

Work on things that matter

Our collaborations have shaped some of the defining moments in public-sector service delivery. We’ve helped build products that connect Veterans to tailored services, help millions access affordable health care, and support important programs like Head Start. As we work with agencies to deliver critical services, we’re also changing how the government approaches technology.

Built for a remote life

Our culture, communications, and tools are built for remote work, enabling us to bring together top talent nationwide. At Ad Hoc, remote life empowers our teams to design work environments that fit their lives and that foster flexibility and collaboration to achieve positive outcomes for our customers.

Committed to high expectations and a welcoming culture

Ad Hoc values acceptance, accountability, and humility. We aren’t heroes. We learn from our mistakes and improve the process for the next time. We build small, inclusive teams to collaborate closely with our partners to solve the right problems and deliver software that works.

The Federal Civilian business unit supports many customers spanning the federal, commercial, and nonprofit space. Our customers include NASA, the General Services Administration, Office of Personnel Management, the Library of Congress, Health & Human Services, and the FDIC. We partner with these agencies to build new capabilities, deliver products, establish data as a strategic asset for informed decision-making, modernize legacy systems, and build the digital service infrastructure necessary to scale their mission impact.

Role Overview

Ad Hoc is seeking a Content Management and Operations Lead (Drupal) to lead content operations supporting a federal financial regulatory web services program. This position is responsible for the day-to-day management of the content operations team, including staff supervision, workload prioritization, quality assurance, performance management, and operational delivery.

The customer's mission depends on timely, accurate, and accessible communication with audiences ranging from individual consumers to financial institutions and investors. Publishing time-sensitive regulatory information requires exceptional attention to detail, strong operational discipline, and a commitment to accuracy.

In this hands-on leadership role, you will directly supervise the team responsible for developing, reviewing, publishing, and maintaining web content in Drupal. You will establish operational priorities, manage team performance, and implement the standards, workflows, and governance practices necessary to ensure the customer's digital content is accurate, accessible, secure, and delivered on time.

You will serve as a key operational leader and subject matter expert in Drupal content administration, editorial workflows, information architecture, and publishing operations. Working directly with the customer's Web Team and content coordinators across multiple divisions, you will provide leadership and guidance on content structure, accessibility, usability, and Drupal authoring best practices.

You will also oversee content operations supporting major website initiatives, including feature launches, awareness campaigns, redesigns, and content modernization efforts. This position requires someone who can balance people leadership, strategic planning, and hands-on technical expertise while maintaining accountability for service delivery in a deadline-driven federal environment.

Primary Responsibilities

Primary expectations of a Content Management and Operations Lead include:

  • Directly manage and supervise a team of content specialists, including assigning work, establishing priorities, providing coaching and performance feedback, conducting performance evaluations, and supporting professional development.
  • Oversee daily content management operations, including intake, prioritization, workload distribution, quality assurance, and publication of content requests across the public website and intranet, ensuring established service-level agreements (SLAs) are met.
  • Manage staffing capacity, resource allocation, workload distribution, and operational coverage to ensure the team meets customer requirements and program commitments.
  • Establish clear performance expectations, monitor team productivity and quality metrics, identify performance gaps, and implement improvements to strengthen operational effectiveness.
  • Serve as the program's Drupal content management subject matter expert, providing technical leadership and oversight of content types, fields, taxonomies, media libraries, menus, navigation, layouts, editorial workflows, moderation states, and user permissions.
  • Oversee website content maintenance and administration, including redirects, metadata, menus, and page layouts within Drupal, providing hands-on support for complex or high-priority requests and coordinating with development teams when custom functionality is required.
  • Develop, document, implement, and enforce content governance standards, publishing procedures, editorial workflows, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
  • Ensure published content and templates comply with Section 508 and Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.x standards, overseeing accessibility testing, issue resolution, and remediation activities.
  • Lead and coordinate training for government stakeholders and content coordinators on Drupal authoring, information architecture, page layouts, content organization, usability, accessibility, and publishing best practices.
  • Manage content planning and operational delivery for major initiatives, including website redesigns, feature launches, content migrations, and high-visibility communications campaigns.
  • Partner with design, development, and program leadership to establish content requirements, improve content models, and support enhancements to website functionality and user experience.
  • Oversee content-related site search functionality, including metadata, taxonomy, search configuration, and optimization to improve content discoverability.
  • Leverage web analytics and operational performance metrics to evaluate content effectiveness, monitor service delivery, identify trends, and drive improvements to content organization, accessibility, and user experience.
  • Direct and coordinate confidential and time-sensitive publishing activities, including regulatory announcements and bank closing events, ensuring strict adherence to customer security requirements, release procedures, and quality standards.
  • Collaborate with development, DevSecOps, design, quality assurance, and third-party teams to coordinate releases, incidents, upgrades, and other activities affecting content operations.
  • Maintain oversight of team assignments, deliverables, and operational documentation using Jira, Confluence, or equivalent customer-approved tools, contributing to weekly status reports, monthly SLA reporting, and quarterly performance reviews.
  • Lead operational planning, participate in Agile ceremonies, and coordinate cross-functional activities to support efficient and predictable content delivery.
  • Identify and address operational risks, resource constraints, quality concerns, and workflow inefficiencies, escalating issues to program leadership as appropriate.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to strengthen publishing efficiency, content governance, team effectiveness, and the overall quality of the customer's digital presence.

Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in web content operations or content management for large, public-facing websites, including demonstrated experience directly supervising employees or managing content publishing teams.
  • 4+ years of experience supporting software applications in a help desk/service desk environment.
  • Familiarity with help desk related systems such as ServiceNow and GitHub.
  • Expert-level user/author with Drupal 10/11.
  • Expert-level user with MS Office and Adobe Analytics.
  • Skilled at data entry, critical timing, and working under high stress.
  • Demonstrated experience managing team performance, assigning and prioritizing work, coordinating staffing resources, providing employee feedback, and maintaining accountability for operational delivery.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience administering or building content within Drupal 10 or 11, including content types, fields, taxonomies, Views, media management, menus, Layout Builder or Paragraphs, content moderation, editorial workflows, and user roles and permissions.
  • Strong working knowledge of HTML and CSS, with working familiarity with JavaScript sufficient to troubleshoot rendered content and template-related issues.
  • Demonstrated experience implementing and maintaining Section 508 and WCAG accessibility standards, including hands-on testing using assistive technologies such as NVDA, JAWS, or VoiceOver.
  • Experience developing, implementing, and enforcing content standards, editorial workflows, publishing procedures, and SOPs.
  • Experience managing content operations against established SLAs, including accountability for measurable accuracy, response time, resolution, and quality expectations.
  • Experience using web analytics platforms such as Google Analytics 4 (GA4) or equivalent tools, along with site search configuration and optimization.
  • Experience working within Agile delivery environments using Jira, Confluence, or equivalent project management and collaboration tools.
  • Strong organizational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities, resolve operational challenges, and maintain team accountability in a deadline-driven environment.
  • Excellent written, verbal, leadership, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to advise nontechnical stakeholders, provide training, and establish clear operational standards.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain the required federal background investigation and Public Trust suitability determination.
  • Must meet applicable contractual citizenship or lawful permanent residency requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience managing content operations teams supporting large-scale Drupal website redesigns, modernization, or replatforming initiatives, including content audits, inventory management, content modeling, template mapping, restructuring, migration, and post-launch support.
  • Acquia Certified Drupal Site Builder certification or equivalent Drupal certification.
  • Experience supporting federal government websites, particularly within financial regulatory agencies.
  • Familiarity with the 21st Century Integrated Digital Experience Act (IDEA), OMB Memorandum M-23-22, and the U.S. Web Design System (USWDS).
  • Experience administering Drupal within a FedRAMP-authorized hosting environment, such as an appropriately authorized Acquia, Pantheon, or Cloud.gov environment.
  • Familiarity with Git-based Drupal configuration management, including configuration export/import processes and CI/CD release workflows.
  • Experience with structured content, content strategy, information architecture, and federal plain-language standards.
  • Experience managing digital assets and overseeing PDF accessibility remediation using Adobe Acrobat or equivalent tools.
  • Experience managing confidential, embargoed, or time-sensitive publishing events requiring strict quality controls and coordinated release procedures.
  • Experience overseeing operational performance reporting, resource planning, and continuous improvement initiatives within a federal government contract environment.

To learn more about working at Ad Hoc, please visit:

Benefits:

  • Company-subsidized health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Flexible PTO

title: Engine Rebuild Technician
description:
Job Title: Engine Rebuild Technician
Location: Davenport, Iowa
Company: Interstate Power Systems
Employment Type: Full-Time
Department: Service / Rebuild Shop

About Interstate Power Systems

Interstate Power Systems is a leading distributor and service provider of high-quality on-highway and off-highway engines, transmissions, and related power solutions. As a factory-authorized service center for brands including Cummins, Detroit Diesel, CAT, Volvo and Allison, we support critical industries such as construction, energy production, and transportation.

Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced Engine Rebuild Technician to join our in-shop team in Davenport, Iowa. This role specializes in full ground-up rebuilds, in-frame overhauls, and complete engine overhauls on Cummins, Detroit, and Allison-powered equipment. The position is primarily shop-based, repetitive in nature, and demands precision, strong mechanical aptitude, and meticulous attention to detail to ensure every rebuild meets factory specifications and delivers long-term reliability.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform complete engine rebuilds, including disassembly, inspection, machining preparation, parts replacement, reassembly, and testing of Cummins, Detroit Diesel, and other heavy-duty engines.
  • Execute in-frame overhauls and full out-of-frame overhauls with a focus on precision and quality.
  • Work on Allison transmissions and related components as needed in conjunction with engine projects.
  • Conduct thorough inspections, measurements, and diagnostics to identify wear, damage, or required repairs.
  • Follow detailed service manuals, technical bulletins, and OEM procedures to maintain warranty and performance standards.
  • Prepare engines/transmissions for dyno testing.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work environment in the rebuild shop.
  • Document all work performed, including parts used, measurements, and test results.
  • Collaborate with service advisors, parts personnel, and other technicians to ensure efficient workflow.

Qualifications

  • Proven experience in diesel engine rebuilding, with specific expertise in full ground-up rebuilds and in-frame/overhaul work on heavy-duty engines (Cummins, CAT, and/or Detroit Diesel experience strongly preferred).
  • Familiarity with Allison transmissions is a plus.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and ability to read blueprints, schematics, and precision measuring tools (micrometers, bore gauges, dial indicators, etc.).
  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship in a repetitive, high-precision environment.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision while meeting production timelines.
  • Experience with engine dyno testing and performance validation is preferred but not required; training provided as needed.
  • High school diploma or GED required; technical/vocational training in diesel mechanics or related field preferred.
  • Valid driver's license with a clean driving record.
  • Ability to lift heavy components and stand for extended periods.

Preferred Skills

  • Prior work in mining, oil & gas, or heavy equipment service environments.
  • Certification or training from Cummins, CAT, Detroit Diesel, or Allison (or willingness to obtain).
  • Basic computer skills for work order systems and documentation.

What We Offer

  • Competitive hourly wage based on experience (with potential for overtime).
  • Comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance, retirement plans, and paid time off.
  • Opportunities for ongoing training and certification through OEM programs.
  • Tool purchase programs and other employee perks.
  • Stable, full-time shop role with no regular field travel required.
  • Supportive team environment in a growing organization with a strong reputation for quality service.

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Interstate Companies is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we encourage all qualified and interested persons to apply for this position by submitting a resume for consideration.

description:

The Club Beyond supervising staff person gives direction and trains the intern as they assist with many aspects of the ministry. Activities include camps, clubs, Bible studies as well as just "hanging out" with kids and modeling a personal example of Jesus Christ. A desire to love and serve kids should be a priority.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Training: Meet weekly with supervising staff using Club Beyond team agenda tools.
  • Direct Ministry: Participate in leadership with a team to conduct Club Beyond club and small group ministry to teens with excellence.
  • Spiritual Development: Develop a 90-day personal growth plan that fosters a vibrant spiritual life including time for solitude, retreat, reflection, prayer, and a sincere commitment to understanding God’s Word. Attend Chapel on installation as often as you are in community.
  • Leadership Development: Attend volunteer leader meetings. Meet weekly with one volunteer to discuss their involvement in Club Beyond. Meet with your supervisor and learn how to recruit and train new leaders and build a leadership team that reflects the diversity of the community.
  • Resource Development: Discuss with your supervisor raising financial support, both the benefits and the challenges. Communicate monthly updates with personal donor partners.
  • Be a role model (incarnational/relational ministry) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to believing teens, and leading and equipping volunteers for "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth ministry.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • Graduated high school at least 2 years prior
  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Financial Commitment:

  • This is a paid internship program. Each applicant is responsible to RAISE the salary needed to participate in the summer internship program, with a minimum of $1160 to a maximum of $4,000 (Depending on the location and number of weeks served).

Location:

Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world; our active locations are listed here: https://clubbeyond.org/locations.

Contact us through:
Robert Raedeke: RecruitingTeam@clubbeyond.org

Want to know more about our mission and culture?

Please check out clubbeyond.org to learn how Club Beyond has been changing the lives of military teens for over 40 years!

title: Case Planner (Temp)
description:
We are looking for a dynamic and compassionate Case Planner to join our team. In this role you will work towards timely permanency planning for children and youth in foster care.

Reports to: Foster Care Supervisor

Location: 7 West Burnside Avenue, Bronx, New York 10453

Hours: 35 Hours / Week; Non-Exempt - Position requires in office hours and field visits. Hybrid schedules are based on program needs and leadership discretion.

Salary Range: 50K-55K based on relevant experience and education.

Major Duties:

  • Assess and monitor for safety and risk.
  • Establish immediate contact with families of the children who are placed into our care, and with their foster families.
  • Conduct required casework contacts with the child, parent, foster parent and collateral contacts (schools, service providers, medical personnel, mental health practitioners, and substance abuse counselors). Make assessment-based referrals as necessary to meet the needs of the child and/or parent.
  • Visit family and child, as often as mandated and/or necessary to gather social history, to assess family strengths and concerns, and to assess existing problems in relation to the reason for placement.
  • Coordinate and supervise all visits between the family and child along with separate sibling visits.
  • Share responsibilities with agency team for the permanency planning of each child.
  • Locate resources and make referrals to any resource that would provide aid to the family and child.
  • Evaluate child’s adjustment in foster home and monitor educational and behavioral performance at home and in school.
  • Monitor foster parents in terms of their ability to meet the needs of the child in their home, and make recommendations regarding future use of the home, in conjunction with the Home finding Department.
  • Adherence to the KEEP (Keeping Foster and Kinship Parents Supported and Trained), PTC (Parenting Through Change) and YDSC (Youth Development Skills Coaching) manuals.
  • Make efficient and creative use of training manuals.
  • Capacity to work within the fidelity guidelines of the KEEP/PTC interventions while delivering the material in the manner that appeals to the needs of individual parents and youth.
  • Support and counsel foster parents in their efforts to care for the child and include them in the development of the goals and tasks.
  • Keep case records up to date within agency standards and complete all necessary ACS/Agency documentation including FASPs, Progress notes, Permanency Hearing reports and all other reports necessary to fulfill the function of the work.
  • Make all court appearances and testimony including permanency hearings.
  • Participate in Family Team Conferences, including but not limited to the placement preservation, reunification/discharge, goal changes and permanency planning conferences. Attend all necessary meetings, functions, workshop, etc. as required by the agency.
  • Keep case records up to date within agency standards and complete all necessary ACS/Agency documentation including FASPs, Progress notes, Permanency Hearing reports and all other reports necessary to fulfill the function of the work.
  • Progress notes are to be completed and submitted preferably within one day of the event but no later than the end of the given week of the event.
  • FASP and Permanency Hearing Report will be submitted on the internal date for review provided by the agency's compliance department.
  • Collaborate closely with team members.
  • Conduct Group facilitation of Keep and PTC groups with parents and foster parents.
  • Ability to enhance communication among parent group members to promote skill development and social networking.
  • Review KEEP/PTC feedback and practice strategies with families.
  • Collaborate closely with Youth Skill Trainers, monitor their interactions with youth.
  • Documents according to developer’s standards, each interaction and visit.
  • Effectively use and practice the Sanctuary Model tools: safety plans, community meetings, psycho-educational groups, team meetings, red flag reviews, treatment planning conferences (or similar), and self-care, when applicable, in the department/program to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Promote and model the seven Sanctuary Model commitments to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Integrate the Sanctuary Model SELF (Safety, Emotional Management, Loss and Future) framework into daily practice to ensure quality care and an effective work environment
  • Utilize Solution Based Casework in casework practice.
  • Implement Solution Based Casework model of casework practice within the department/program.
  • Implement and integrate the principles and procedures of Solution Based Casework: assessment, family and individual level outcomes, action plans and documentation and celebration.
  • Actively participate in case consultation, continued SBC training and the SBC certification process.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in related field required;
  • MSW or at least one year related experience preferred.
  • Must be able to establish working relationships with clients in need of counseling and supportive services.
  • Must be able to effectively engage parents.
  • Ability to apply theory of change.
  • Willingness to facilitate groups with parents and foster parents.
  • Ability to work cooperatively with their agency supervisor(s), KEEP, PTC, and YDSC consultants, ACS and other team members.
  • Excellent written and verbal skills necessary.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred.

title: Pricing Governance and Analytics Manager
description:
Shaping the Future of Lending

With 30 years of fintech leadership, Origence empowers credit unions with innovative SaaS lending solutions that make lending more accessible, efficient, and competitive. We invest in our people and foster a culture of innovation, ownership, and continuous improvement. As we help shape the future of lending, we're leveraging AI to enhance the way we work and create value for our clients, and we're seeking individuals who are excited by emerging technologies and eager to use them responsibly to solve problems and drive impact.

The Pricing & Profitability Manager is responsible for leading enterprise pricing governance and optimizing profitability across Origence’s products, services, and client relationships. This role serves as a strategic partner to Product, Sales, and Finance teams by providing financial insight, evaluating pricing proposals, and ensuring sound, data-driven decision making. The incumbent leads the Pricing Committee process, maintains strong governance and accountability over pricing decisions, identifies opportunities to improve client-level profitability, and translates complex data into actionable business insights that drive sustainable growth, profitability, and organizational performance.

***Please note, this position will follow a Hybrid schedule with a minimum of 3 days in the office/week***

The Origence Mindset

At Origence, we are self-aware, adaptable, and relentlessly focused on creating meaningful impact. We think like owners, embrace complexity and ambiguity, challenge conventional thinking, and continuously pursue smarter, more effective ways to solve problems and advance the business. If this mindset reflects who you are, you may be exactly who we're looking for.

How You'll Contribute:

Pricing Governance & Committee Facilitation

  • Facilitate recurring Pricing Committee meetings and drive the end-to-end pricing governance process.

  • Coordinate pricing reviews across Product, Sales, Finance, Operations, Legal, and leadership stakeholders.

  • Manage committee agendas, supporting materials, decision documentation, follow-up actions, and approval tracking.

  • Ensure pricing decisions are properly documented, communicated, and incorporated into enterprise pricing standards.

  • Maintain the enterprise master pricing file and serve as the primary steward of official pricing records.

  • Promote consistency, transparency, and accountability in pricing decisions across the organization.

Pricing Proposal Review & Business Partnership

  • Review and validate pricing proposals submitted by Product, Sales, or business teams to ensure assumptions, financial impact, profitability, and business rationale are sound.

  • Partner with Product and Sales teams to evaluate new pricing structures, renewals, client expansions, contract changes, and strategic pricing requests.

  • Challenge assumptions professionally and constructively while helping business partners strengthen pricing recommendations.

  • Summarize pricing proposal impacts, key risks, dependencies, and recommendations for committee and leadership review.

  • Support follow-through after pricing decisions, including documentation, communication, implementation coordination, and issue resolution.

Profitability & Business Analytics

  • Analyze product, client, channel, and transaction-level economics to identify margin improvement opportunities.

  • Review client-level profitability to identify pricing exceptions, discounting patterns, underperforming accounts, and opportunities to improve economics.

  • Evaluate pricing scenarios, volume assumptions, cost-to-serve considerations, revenue impact, and margin contribution.

  • Provide practical recommendations on price adjustments, discount strategies, pricing structures, contract terms, and profitability improvement opportunities.

  • Monitor pricing performance against approved assumptions and identify risks, opportunities, and variances.

Business Insight & Decision Support

  • Translate financial and operational data into clear insights, recommendations, and leadership-ready summaries.

  • Partner with business leaders to understand performance drivers, customer behavior, product economics, and growth opportunities.

  • Develop recurring reporting and analysis to improve visibility into pricing, revenue, margin, and profitability trends.

  • Support ad hoc analysis for Finance, Product, Sales, Operations, and leadership.

  • Use data to support fact-based decision-making while keeping recommendations practical and business-focused.

Collaboration & Process Improvement

  • Serve as a key liaison between Finance, Product, Sales, Operations, Legal, IT, and Data teams on pricing and profitability matters.

  • Build trusted relationships with business partners while maintaining financial discipline and governance standards.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify pricing processes, improve documentation, and strengthen handoffs between teams.

  • Drive accountability and follow-through on pricing decisions, open issues, and process improvements.

  • Support the continued development of a more consistent, transparent, and disciplined enterprise pricing process.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

Education

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Analytics, Business Administration, or a related field.

Experience

  • 6+ years of experience in FP&A, pricing analytics, financial analysis, business analytics, revenue analytics, ora related function.

  • Strong understanding of pricing strategy, profitability analysis, margin analysis, and business case development.

  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage recurring governance processes, deadlines, stakeholders, and follow-up actions.

  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret financial and operational data and translate findings into actionable business recommendations.

  • Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills.

  • Excellent communication, facilitation, and presentation skills.

  • Ability to work cross-functionally with Finance, Product, Sales, Operations, Legal, IT, and Data teams.

  • High attention to detail and strong ownership of data accuracy, documentation, process discipline, and decision follow-through.

Your Strengths & Expertise

  • Experience supporting Pricing Committees, deal desks, pricing governance, revenue management, or approval workflows.

  • Experience conducting client-level, product-level, or profitability analysis.

  • Experience in financial services, lending, fintech, SaaS, or technology organizations.

  • Experience using Power BI, Tableau, SQL, or similar analytical tools is helpful but not required.

  • Experience building pricing models, profitability models, dashboards, or recurring management reporting.

  • MBA, CFA, CPA, or relevant analytics certification preferred but not required.

Bring your ideas, your curiosity, and your unique perspective. We'll provide the opportunities, tools, and support to help you succeed.

How We Invest in You:

  • 401(k) with 8% Company Match
  • Flexible Work Environment
  • Competitive Paid Time Off
  • Tuition Reimbursement & Education Benefits
  • Comprehensive Health & Wellness Benefits
  • Microsoft Copilot and AI-Enabled Tools
  • Continuous Learning & Development Opportunities
  • A culture of connection, celebration, and growth through employee-driven programs, company events, holiday celebrations (Star Wars Day), monthly town halls, quarterly company meetings, and team traditions like Bring Your Kid to Work Day

Recognizing Your Impact

For this full-time role, the starting salary range is $111800 - $139800 per year. Our compensation is designed to be competitive and to reflect the value, experience, and contributions each team member brings to Origence. Offers are usually not made at the top of the range, and each compensation package is assessed carefully based on job-related factors such as relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and geographic location, in compliance with applicable laws.

Origence is an equal opportunity employer. All recruitment, hiring, training, compensation, benefits, discipline, and other terms and conditions of employment will be based upon an individuals’ qualifications regardless of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, military service, marital status, pregnancy, age, protected medical condition, genetic information, disability or any other category protected by federal, state or local law.

title: Permit Inspector
description:
Brookline DPW’s Engineering & Transportation Division is hiring a Permit Inspector to perform vital inspection and administrative work ensuring public safety and infrastructure integrity. This role centers on issuing, monitoring, and evaluating permits for construction work in public ways, utility connections, and town-owned property occupations, ensuring all projects align with Town bylaws and engineering standards.

Responsibilities

  • Manage and issue permits to contractors performing construction in public ways, connecting to public utilities (water, sewer, drain mains), or occupying town-owned property (dumpsters, newsracks, signs).
  • Perform field inspections and emergency mark-outs, utilizing metal detectors for regular or emergency DigSafe utility locations and serving as the designated Massachusetts Department of Public Safety open trench representative.
  • Monitor and evaluate contractor road work to determine if asphalt, concrete, and trench compaction are acceptable, while proactively resolving resident complaints regarding poor road conditions like potholes.
  • Enforce Town Bylaws and accessibility regulations, including sidewalk snow/ice clearance, leaf blower usage, and inspecting handicap accessibility ramps post-snow events to ensure state and federal compliance.
  • Conduct regulatory inspections, performing field investigations for commercial outdoor seating safe passage and executing final structural inspections for Certificates of Occupancy.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders, meeting with contractors to guide excavation layout decisions (curb cuts, conduit placement), verifying contractor bond statuses, and scheduling coordination meetings with town officials.

Qualifications

High school diploma with technical training equivalent to an Associate’s Degree, combined with 3 to 5 years of road construction, underground construction, trench compaction, and pavement restoration experience (or an equivalent combination of education and experience).

Required licenses / certifications

Valid Driver’s License, Class D

Ideal Candidate

Strong understanding of road excavation principles, construction and underground construction, asphalt and concrete, sidewalk/road way patching, specification and cost estimation, engineering construction standards, and engineering software. Ability to work outside in varied weather and hazardous construction conditions, frequently moving or lifting equipment up to 50 pounds, and standing, walking, or crouching during field inspections.

Pay Information

Starting hourly range: $42.32 - $44.03 depending on qualifications and experience. Brookline offers comprehensive benefits including Health insurance, dental coverage, retirement pension plan, generous vacation and sick time, and opportunities for professional development.

How to Apply

Please apply with a resume and cover letter as soon as possible. Apply before November 23, 2026 for priority consideration.

Status: Exempt

SUMMARY:
The General Manager oversees and assumes responsibility for various departments. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Forecasts goals and objectives for the department and strives to meet them.

• Maintains professional appearance.

title: PK-6 Literacy Affiliate Instructor
description:

The SEHS is fully accredited by the CAEP, CSWE, and the HLC, ensuring continuous improvement within its world-class programs.

  • We prioritize an unwavering commitment to the Christian worldview (as explicitly defined on CU's About page), extending to every facet of our educational offerings.
  • We intertwine our classroom instruction with our professional expertise, effectively bringing to life the course materials for the benefit of our students.
  • We demonstrate a commitment to fostering students' professional growth, underpinned by academic rigor, and providing experiential learning opportunities; successfully equipping our students for their chosen vocational path.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Teach undergraduate literacy and language arts courses in the Teacher Education program
  • Facilitate engaging, evidence-based instruction aligned with the Science of Reading and Michigan literacy standards
  • Teach courses such as:
    • Foundations of Literacy
    • Children’s Literature and Writing Instruction
    • Young Adult Literature and Writing Instruction
    • Teaching Literacy I (PK–3)
    • Teaching Literacy II (Grades 4–6)
  • Prepare teacher candidates to implement explicit and systematic literacy instruction in:
    • phonological awareness
    • phonics and decoding
    • fluency
    • vocabulary
    • comprehension
    • writing instruction
    • disciplinary literacy
    • literacy assessment and intervention
  • Model effective literacy instructional practices, including:
    • formative assessment
    • differentiated instruction
    • discussion facilitation
    • metacognitive strategy instruction
    • literacy-rich classroom design
    • use of mentor texts
  • Support teacher candidates in connecting reading and writing instruction through authentic literacy experiences and quality children’s and young adult literature
  • Supervise and support clinical experiences, tutoring experiences, and practicum activities in school settings
  • Collaborate with faculty to maintain program quality and alignment with CAEP, MDE, and institutional expectations
  • Utilize Brightspace and educational technology tools to support instruction and assessment
  • Integrate a Christ-centered worldview into literacy instruction and professional interactions consistent with the mission of Cornerstone University
  • Participate in departmental meetings and professional development as appropriate

Teaching in the School of Education and Human Services: To teach in the SEHS adjunct faculty must have a master’s degree or doctoral degree. In addition to the degree requirement, adjunct faculty must have professional experience within the field he or she aspires to teach in.

Courses to be taught can include but are not limited to: PK-6 Literacy.

Cornerstone University is a vibrant interdenominational evangelical university that prepares students for lives of global influence in an academically rigorous, spiritually rich educational community. It is located minutes from downtown Grand Rapids, a dynamic city in Western Michigan that offers a wealth of outdoor and cultural activities. Learn more about Cornerstone at www.cornerstone.edu

title: Internship - Anomaly Localization for Industrial Inspection
description:
MERL is looking for a self-motivated intern to work on anomaly localization in industrial inspection setting using computer vision. The relevant topics in the scope include (but not limited to): few/zero/any-shot anomaly detection, generalist/continual/online/long-tailed/multi-view/noisy anomaly detection, how to incorporate large foundation models in image anomaly localization, etc. The candidates with experiences of image anomaly localization in industrial inspection settings (e.g., MVTec-AD, VisA, Real-IAD, or MANTA datasets) and usage of large foundation models are strongly preferred. The ideal candidate would be a PhD student with a strong background in computer vision and machine learning, and the candidate is expected to have published at least one paper in a top-tier computer vision, machine learning, or artificial intelligence venues, such as CVPR, ECCV, ICCV, ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS, AAAI, etc. Proficiency in Python programming and familiarity in at least one deep learning framework are necessary. The ideal candidate is required to collaborate with MERL researchers to develop algorithms and prepare manuscripts for scientific publications. The duration of the internship is ideally to be at least 3 months with a flexible start date.

Required Specific Experience

title: Online Counseling Faculty (Marriage and Family Therapy)
description:

Teaching

Service

Scholarship

Workload

  • Teaching, supervision, scholarship, and service responsibilities aligned with institutional faculty workload policies.

Required Qualifications

Doctoral degree in one of the following:

  • PhD in Counselor Education from a CACREP-accredited program.
    OR

  • PhD in Marriage and Family Therapy from a COAMFTE-accredited program.

  • Eligibility for faculty status under CACREP and/or COAMFTE accreditation standards.

  • Demonstrated ability to teach graduate-level counseling and/or MFT coursework.

Preferred Qualifications

Current or licensure eligible in Michigan as:

  • Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC) and/or

  • Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT)

A personal relationship with Jesus Christ and an active Christian commitment.

A theology that supports the values and mission of Cornerstone University core commitments evidenced by an ability to affirm and sign the university’s doctrinal statement, “The Cornerstone Confession.”

Four other foundational pillars, along with the university’s mission and confession, form Cornerstone’s Core Commitments.

title: Partner Recruiting Assistant
description:
Location: Remote, United States

Job Full: Full-time

Fisher Phillips, a premier international labor and employment law firm, is seeking a Partner Recruiting Assistant to support the firm’s lateral partner recruiting activities.

Position Summary

Reporting to the Director of Partner Recruiting, this role provides administrative, systems, and process support to the department’s Director, Managers, and Coordinators. Responsibilities include maintaining recruiting systems and records, coordinating scheduling and logistics, processing documentation, and assisting with reports and candidate materials.

This entry-level position works within established procedures with regular guidance and review, offering exposure to the lateral partner recruiting lifecycle and opportunities to develop skills for advancement to the Coordinator level. Success requires strong organizational skills, discretion with confidential information, and responsive, professional communication in a fully remote team environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Assist in all areas of lateral partner recruiting.
  • Review and process all resume submissions and employment inquiries, enter candidate information into the applicant tracking system and maintain related data and records.
  • Schedule and arrange logistics in connection with virtual and in-person interviews for candidates.
  • Prepare and organize electronic interview evaluation packets for lateral hiring decisions.
  • Solicit and follow up with attorneys for lateral candidate interview evaluations and feedback.
  • Assist in coordination of partner strategic growth initiatives.
  • Organize and send resumes to all Partner Recruiting Team members.
  • Assist with preparing communications and reports, and responding to ad hoc data requests.
  • Collaborate with colleagues in offices and other departments regarding recruiting matters.
  • Process vendor invoices and department and candidate expenses and monitor budget
  • Perform additional duties assigned by the legal recruiting team.

Requirements

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • At least one year of law firm experience required; experience in an administrative, recruiting, or operations role preferred.
  • Experience maintaining databases, tracking tools, or applicant tracking systems preferred.
  • Interest in pursuing a career in legal recruiting.

Knowledge Skills and Abilities

  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to maintain accurate records and data.
  • Ability to manage a high volume of assignments, competing priorities, and deadlines while supporting multiple team members.
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills and a professional, service-oriented approach.
  • Ability to exercise discretion and maintain the confidentiality of candidate, compensation, and strategic information.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Outlook, and the ability to learn ATS platforms, Smartsheet, and AI tools.
  • Ability to work independently and reliably in a remote environment, communicate responsively, and follow through on assignments.
  • Willingness to learn lateral partner recruiting processes and assume additional responsibilities as skills develop.

Qualified applications with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with both the FCO and the California Fair Chance Act (FCA).

Equal Opportunity Employer

Fisher Phillips is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants, regardless of race, ethnicity, religion, sex (including related medical conditions), gender, sexual orientation, national origin, citizenship status, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, age, disability, or any other protected status, in compliance with all applicable laws.

Compensation

The hourly rate range for this position is $28.85 - $38.46. Actual base pay within this range will be determined by several components, including but not limited to, location, relevant experience, internal equity, skills, qualifications, and other job-related factors permitted by law.

Why Join Us

At Fisher Phillips, exceptional talent is the foundation of our success. Joining our team means collaborating in a professional, dynamic environment leveraging cutting-edge technology. Our leadership fosters professional growth and provides opportunities to challenge yourself.

Our comprehensive benefits include health, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) with profit sharing, 15 days of paid time off (including sick leave as applicable), and 10 paid holidays per benefit year. Wellness programs and 24/7 telehealth services support your overall well-being. Visit to learn more.

Additional Notes

The statements in this position description are not necessarily all-inclusive. Additional duties and responsibilities may be assigned, and requirements may vary from time to time.

As part of our initial screening process, we may use an AI tool to compare the skills and job titles from your resume with the job description, using machine learning or artificial intelligence based on their contextual meaning and relevancy. This is NOT an automated employment decision tool (‘AEDT’) and will not be used to make selection decisions. It is only used (occasionally) in addition to manual screening.

If you are a resident of New York City and would like to request an alternative evaluation process or reasonable accommodation, please email staffrecruiting@fisherphillips.com.

Relocation costs are not covered. We are only accepting direct applicants; third-party recruiters or agencies will not be considered. No phone inquiries, please.
