title: Fair Futures Supervisor (Travel Required)
location: New York NY, Brooklyn NY, Bronx NY
description:
Job Title: Fair Futures Supervisor

Reports to: Director of Fair Futures

Location: 337 East 17th Street, New York, NY & 2207 University Avenue/2190 University Bronx

Hours: 35 Hours/Week. Position requires staff to be onsite. Position also requires travel between programs/boros. Hybrid schedules are based on program needs and at program leadership discretion.

Salary 61K-66K based on direct & relevant post graduate experience.

Job Summary:

Within the context of a trauma informed, sanctuary, and operating from a strength-based perspective, the Fair Futures College & Career Specialist/Supervisor will oversee up to four Fair Coaches in their work with young people by providing guidance and ongoing direction to help participants achieve academic and career success. The delivery of services is to be consistent with Fair Future, Good Shepherd Services’ philosophy, and city and state mandates.

Major Duties:

  • Supervise a team of (4) Fair Futures Coaches across various Good Shepherd Services Residential Programs in New York City.
  • Provide a minimum of weekly supervision to ensure that the educational, employment and vocational needs of participants are being met.
  • Work closely with The Fair Futures Educational and Permanency Specialists.
  • Check in with Residential Program leadership on site.
  • Review documentation in advance (including any progress notes, new academic data, and goals/steps completed over the last week).
  • Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary team to implement procedure and process to promote accessibility to career and educational services that would enhance employment opportunities for participants.
  • Create and maintain community resources to serve as a conduit to career and educational opportunities, including linkages with vocational/educational agencies such as ACS, ACCES-VR, NADAP, One-Stop, DYCD, etc.
  • Plan and execute fair future events by organizing vocational, employment/educational recruitment and college tours.
  • Guide Coaches to utilize motivational interviewing to create an individualized Ed/Voc/Career plan to support participants skills, goals, and interest.
  • Assist Coach with facilitating Preparing Youth for Adulthood (PYA) groups, which focus on skills, such as: healthy communication, employment process, college application process, positive peer relationships, making positive choices, and service learning.
  • Assist Coach with identifying potential longer-term career pathways based on the participant’s interests, strengths, and academic/vocational plans.
  • Participate in trainings/ department meetings, Program Evaluation and Planning Dept (PEP) in fulfillment of the program evaluation processes, including documentation/collection, development and monitoring of program data in Connections and outcomes.
  • Promote and model the seven Sanctuary Model commitments to create a nonviolent and trauma sensitive culture.
  • Integrate the Sanctuary Model SELF (Safety, Emotional Management, Loss and Future) framework into daily practice to ensure quality care and an effective work environment.
  • Ensure Coach has appropriate external support and supplies necessary to effectively execute tasks.
  • Assist with developing program activities to explore career, educational pathways and workshops to keep participants engaged during the employment search process.
  • Track and ensure that young people are attaining employment, training, educational and internship opportunities.
  • Ensure that organizational expectations for placement and retention of young people in jobs, internships, and training are met on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis.
  • Help Coaches navigate the DOE, academic and career development goal-setting process,
  • Facilitate and assist with the submission of financial aid, ETV, ACS Dorm Project/Foster Care Room & Board, & all applicable scholarships including reviewing reference letters and college essays.
  • Assist participants with writing college essays and personal statements where needed.
  • Ensure participants are signed up for any entrance interviews/exams and apply to eligible opportunity programs (Upward Bound, etc.); Monitor Pre-SAT/SAT scores of those participants who do take them, and meet with them to discuss/refine college options.
  • Meet with participants interested in college to have an exploratory and informational session, after they are referred by their Coach, and discuss/develop individualized success plan to complete identified high school or HSE program
  • Establish contact with participants in college to ensure they are enrolled in the proper classes each semester, and assist with enrollment, if needed.
  • Assist young people with creating/updating resume and cover letter as needed.
  • Facilitate family Team Conferences when needed.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in, human services, workforce development, social work, and/education required & minimum of five years’ experience within supervisory capacity. Masters in social work and education strongly preferred.
  • A minimum of 3-5 years of proven excellence in leadership, curriculum development, and presentation skills.
  • Travel is required
  • Must have excellent written and verbal communication skills to maintain required documentation.
  • Must be able to use public transportation systems, including subways and busses to attend various meetings and make home visits.
  • Must be physically able to observe staff in their relationship with residents, be able to climb stairs when an elevator is not available.
  • Must have a commitment to work from a strength based and/or youth development perspective.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred.
  • Must have knowledge of Connections and Microsoft Suite.
  • Must have ability to work a flexible schedule when needed including some evenings, weekends, and holidays.
  • Must have a commitment to GSS models of practice including Sanctuary and ACS principles to promote permanency, safety, and well-being.

You will work closely with Growth, Business Unit leadership, solution architects, delivery teams, pricing, contracts, recruiting, and other internal partners throughout the capture lifecycle. title: Onsite Material Coordinator
description:
The Role: Onsite Material Coordinator

Pay: $30 - $35 per hour, based on experience.

Location: Onsite, Allentown, PA.

Schedule: 16 days on, 5 days off (likely), but may vary.

The Onsite Material Coordinator is a key position crucial to the overall success of CSI distribution operations. Onsite Material Coordinators operate a remote facility to support local customer business.

This position will be a temporary assignment operating within a customer facility or in close local proximity. The individual in this role will perform multiple functions including receiving, put away, inventory control, cycle counting, picking, packing, and managing and issuing customer managed material. Most fulfillment operations in this role will be Will Call and Delivery. An Onsite Material Coordinator at CSI must be able to do light repairs, have self-initiative, take pride and ownership in their tasks, and work well within a team or on their own.

About CSI

CSI provides state-of-the-art stainless-steel process equipment and service for manufacturers in the food, dairy, beverage, pharmaceutical, and personal care industries.

We are a growing company built on teamwork, continuous learning, and exceptional customer service. Our employees are our greatest resource, and we invest in their development through training, collaboration, and opportunities to grow.

What You’ll Be Doing

Receiving

  • Receive all types of material per procedure – daily
  • Inventory
  • Customer Returns
  • Customer Managed Inventory
  • Transfers
  • Receive and document lot tracked material per procedure – daily
  • Put away parts per procedure – daily
  • Check for accuracy in receiving-actual receipt vs. computer receipt
  • Check to make sure the part numbers match as well as the quantity
  • Update part attributes

Shipping

  • Pull inventory, pack, and ship orders to prevent damage - daily
  • Pull and record lot tracked material for sales orders, and transfers - daily
  • Check orders to ensure accuracy - daily
  • Pull MTR's for all 316L, AL-6XN®, C-22®, and when requested on orders - daily
  • Pick, pack and ship warehouse transfers
  • Record heat numbers on packing lists for all 316L, AL-6XN®, C-22® materials
  • Deliveries
  • Print orders using Fulfillment Workbench

General Utility in Warehouse

  • Sweep floors; warehouse – as needed
  • Empty Trash; warehouse – as needed
  • Break down and/or stack pallets – as needed
  • Break down cardboard boxes for recycling – as needed
  • Wipe down shelves and straighten up inventory – as needed
  • Submit supplies requisition to supervisor
  • Train on and operate all warehouse equipment
  • Forklift
  • Truck and flatbed trailer

Inventory Control

  • Investigate inventory discrepancies before adjustments are processed – as needed
  • Timely and accurate cycle and counts – as needed
  • Run count sheets
  • Enter Counts
  • Investigate all discrepancies
  • Submit final count to supervisor
  • Indexing using Synergy – as needed
  • Setup and move item locations – as needed
  • Identify and make available locations for new parts – as needed

Education/Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent, required
  • Ability to obtain a forklift certification, required
  • Must have or be able to obtain a chauffeurs’ license to drive delivery truck
  • Computer knowledge, required
  • Epicor Kinetic software, preferred
  • CSI experience, preferred

Why CSI

  • Competitive compensation: $30-$35 per hour.
  • Opportunity to work on specialized stainless-steel process systems across multiple industries
  • Hands-on role with direct impact on quality, safety, and customer satisfaction
  • Collaborative team environment focused on continuous improvement
  • Career growth opportunities within installation, operations, and leadership teams
  • Company culture centered on taking care of employees and customers

Benefits & Perks

CSI offers a competitive benefits package including:

  • Health and wellness benefits
  • Paid time off
  • Retirement planning options

Work Environment / Physical Requirements

Standard workday and work week for the Onsite Coordinator varies. Saturday, Sunday and holiday work will commonly be required.

Onsite Coordinator positions are very active and require constant standing, walking, bending, kneeling, stooping, crouching, crawling, and climbing. The employee must frequently lift and/or move items up to 75 pounds with assistance. Visual acuity is required to perform work using close, distance, and peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus. The employee may be exposed to environmental factors typical of welding and field installation. Working outside or in non-climate controlled environments may be required. Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment, such as fall protection, safety glasses, and steel toe shoes.

Equal Opportunity Employer

CSI is committed to equal opportunity employment. We select candidates based on their ability to perform the work in a competent and professional manner and do not discriminate based on age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or disability.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. CSI participates in E-Verify.

The ideal candidate is a trusted HR advisor who thrives in a multi-client environment. This individual must be able to balance multiple client engagements, develop practical and customized solutions, and build strong relationships with client leaders and HR teams.

  • Analyze HR data and trends and develop reports, insights, and recommendations to support clients’ workforce planning and strategic decision-making.
  • Stay current on federal, state, and local employment laws, regulations, HR trends, and emerging best practices.
  • Identify potential compliance concerns or organizational risks and provide clients with practical recommendations to address them.

Preferred Qualifications

title: Group Leader (JHS 292)
description:
Title: Group Leader

Reports To: Program Director, JHS 292

Location: 301 Vermont St, Brooklyn, NY 11207

Hours: Up to 20 hours/Week; Non-Exempt;

Schedule: School Year / September - June / Monday - Friday, 2pm to 6pm

Salary: $18.00 - 19.00/hour

Job Summary: The After School Group Leader is responsible for the overall safety, development, management, organization and planning of their group. This includes integrated educational projects, recreation, arts and crafts and group building activities.

Major Duties:

  • Overall supervision and management of identified group of participants.

  • Engage participants in after school activities and role model appropriate behavior.

  • Ensure safety of participants at all times.

  • As needed, engage in outreach activities to ensure attendance and participation.

  • Provide support to activity instructors and other group leaders.

  • Develop and facilitate a sequenced and thematic curriculum and other various activities including arts & crafts. Curriculum should promote creativity, self-expression, opportunity for mastery, and emotional growth and future focus/career exploration as well as professional growth.

  • Integrate lessons enriched with literacy, history and other related academic subjects when applicable.

  • Develop positive relationships with participants, colleagues and school/center personnel.

  • Attends all staff meetings and staff development trainings sessions, as specified (including Saturday and evening trainings).

  • Assist with monitoring and maintaining the rules of the program and upholding the afterschool model.

  • Plan and prepare culminating events for participants to showcase their activities.

  • Ensure participants are prepared and able to illustrate what they learned in culminating events.

  • Assist with organizing parent family culminating engagement events.

  • Engage with parents and guardians as necessary in a professional manner.

  • Discuss behavior problems , safety concerns and situations with supervisor as they emerge, and completing necessary documentation and paperwork.

  • Mandated Reporter.

  • Resolve conflict within your group while seeking assistance from other staff, supervisors and directors when necessary.

  • Foster a positive youth development approach focusing on , strength’s-based environment, fostering a sense of belonging, independence, generosity, mastery safety, and community to participants.

  • Supervise support staff assigned to your group (including but not limited to assistant group leader, interns, volunteers, etc.).

  • Track and support participant’s development and growth areas. Engage and facilitate group conversations, tracking and supporting students’ participant’s academic success.

  • Responsible for the safe arrival and dismissal of all program participants.

  • Demonstrate effective classroom management skills.

  • Inspect all facilities, equipment, and supplies and be sure all are locked away securely at the end of each day.

  • Available to work during holidays and OST days (13-15 days).

  • Maintain all required records for your group, including attendance..

  • Maintain strict adherence to policies and procedures at all times.

  • Participate in afterschool events and trips.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • Must be at least 18 years old.

  • High School/ GED Diploma and 1 year related experience in leading and participating in youth group development related activities required.

  • Experience building a camp culture through chants, team building activities, and community building preferred.

  • Can contribute a talent or experience in arts, music, crafts, etc. a plus.

  • A commitment to working with youth from a variety of backgrounds, while providing high quality services.

  • Must have a commitment to work from a strength-based, youth and family development and trauma-informed perspective.

title: Associate Town Counsel
description:
Are you a seasoned attorney passionate about public service and employment law? The Town of Brookline is seeking an experienced and dynamic Associate Town Counsel to join our Legal Department. This position offers a unique opportunity to provide legal counsel on a broad range of municipal matters and to work closely with elected and appointed officials, department heads, boards, commissions, and staff in a collaborative and high-performing environment.

As Associate Town Counsel, you will advise Town leadership on a wide variety of legal issues, including municipal governance, procurement and contracting, public records and open meeting law compliance, land use and regulatory matters, litigation management, risk assessment, and policy development. The successful candidate will help advance the Town's mission by providing practical, strategic, and timely legal advice in support of municipal operations and public service.

Why Brookline?

The Town of Brookline offers a competitive starting salary range of $120,223 - $126,758 along with a flexible hybrid work schedule that promotes work-life balance. As a municipal employee, you’ll enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes health, dental, life, and long-term disability insurance, plus four weeks of paid vacation annually. Brookline is committed to the professional growth of its employees, offering access to continuing legal education and other development opportunities. With its dynamic and supportive work environment, Brookline is an ideal place to build a meaningful and rewarding legal career in public service.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide legal advice and counsel to Town departments, boards, commissions, committees, and senior leadership on municipal operations and governance.
  • Draft, review, and negotiate contracts, intergovernmental agreements, licenses, permits, policies, bylaws, regulations, and other legal documents.
  • Advise on compliance with federal, state, and local laws, including public records, open meeting law, procurement, ethics, administrative, and municipal finance requirements.
  • Represent the Town before administrative agencies, regulatory bodies, and state and federal courts, either directly or through coordination with outside counsel.
  • Attend and provide legal counsel at public meetings, including meetings of the Select Board, Advisory Committee, Town Meeting, and other boards and commissions.
  • Conduct legal research and prepare written opinions, memoranda, resolutions, and legislative proposals.
  • Assist departments with risk management, claims resolution, and dispute avoidance strategies.
  • Support special projects involving land use, zoning, licensing, environmental, housing, public construction, public safety, and other municipal matters, as assigned.
  • Monitor developments in municipal law and provide guidance regarding emerging legal issues affecting local government.
  • Perform other related legal duties as assigned by the Town Counsel.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school and a minimum of five years of progressively responsible legal experience, preferably including experience in municipal law, government law, litigation, administrative law, land use, procurement, contracts, or related public-sector legal practice.

Licensure

  • Member in good standing of the Massachusetts Bar.
  • Must be eligible for admission to the U.S. District Court and U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit within 90 days of appointment.

Preferred Knowledge & Skills

The ideal candidate will possess a strong working knowledge of Massachusetts municipal law and local government operations. Familiarity with public records law, open meeting law, procurement law, land use and zoning, ethics requirements, administrative law, and litigation management is highly desirable.

Success in this role requires exceptional analytical, oral, and written communication skills, sound legal judgment, and the ability to provide practical solutions to complex legal issues. Candidates should demonstrate strong interpersonal skills and the ability to work effectively with elected officials, department leaders, boards and commissions, Town employees, outside counsel, and members of the public. The ability to manage multiple priorities while handling sensitive and high-profile matters with discretion and professionalism is essential.

Apply Now:

If you're ready to help shape the future of public service in one of Massachusetts' most vibrant and community-focused municipalities please apply today with your confidential letter of interest and resume.

Applications received by November 30, 2026 will be prioritized for consideration.

title: Start Your Career Helping Children with Autism
description:
Psychology Opportunity in Webb City,MO

Seeking candidates who are able to a make a long term commitment (minimum 6 months) | Competitive Pay | Flexible Hours |

Are you a seasoned Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) seeking the ideal organization to join? We're actively seeking enthusiastic and devoted RBTs to become valued members of our team, contributing your expertise to support our clients in achieving their unique goals. As an accomplished professional in the Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) field, your skills and dedication align with our dedication to providing excellence to our clients.

Perks:

  • Same Day Pay! No more waiting for payday — now you can access a portion of your paycheck right after you clock in and out. Whether it’s an emergency or you just need funds sooner, you’ll have the flexibility to get paid immediately.

    Your time. Your money. On your schedule.

  • Elevate your career with job stability and opportunities for professional advancement in the thriving ABA industry.

  • Enjoy the flexibility and autonomy you deserve, catering to your schedule and professional preferences.

  • Receive competitive compensation that reflects your experience.

  • Ideal for those seeking part-time positions.

  • Access career advancement assistance through partnerships with BCBA schooling programs.

  • Benefit from a robust clinical team dedicated to providing the support you deserve.

  • Fellowship and internship opportunities to accumulate both restricted and unrestricted hours.

  • Enjoy the freedom to choose your own cases, without a minimum case requirement.

  • Earn referral bonuses by spreading the word about our opportunities.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide one-on-one ABA services to clients, using evidence-based interventions supporting independence and positive behavior.

  • Serve as an integral member of our clinical team, responsible for the direct implementation of skill-building and care plans.

  • Record session data accurately using electronic devices.

  • Foster a positive learning environment for clients and connect with families.

Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • Willingness to learn and passionate about making a difference for children with Autism.

  • Patience, compassion, and the ability to maintain a calm demeanor in challenging situations.

  • RBT certification is required before working

Need to Know:

  • Services will be provided in clients' homes or in community-based locations.

  • All positions start off part-time.

  • Looking to hire candidates who are willing to make a 6-month commitment to change our clients lives.

Great Fit If You Have Experience In:

  • Education or early childhood development

  • Childcare, babysitting, or youth mentorship

  • Teaching assistant, paraprofessional, or instructional aide roles

  • After-school programs or camp counseling

  • Behavioral health, mental health, or social services

  • ABA therapy or working with individuals with Autism

  • Healthcare support (DSP, CNA, HHA, PCA, caregiver)

  • Supporting a neurodiverse family member or loved one

No experience? No problem — paid training is provided!
If you're compassionate, patient, and passionate about making a difference, we encourage you to apply.

Join our team, contribute your skills to our mission, and continue your journey of making a meaningful difference in the lives of children with Autism. Apply today and be a part of our dynamic and fulfilling community!

title: Family Worker
description:
Reports To: Social Work Supervisor

Location: 503 5th Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11215

Hours: 35 Hours/Week; Non-exempt

Salary: $40,000 - $45,000 per year

Job Summary: The Family Worker provides a variety of home-based supportive services and case management activities for families participating in the Transitions Brooklyn prevention program in order to ensure child safety, well-being, and family stability. The Family Worker also carries administrative and organizational responsibilities to support the overall program operation.

Major Duties:

  • Collaborate closely with and assist the Case Worker/Social Worker to conduct frequent home and office visits with families to monitor child safety and ensure family stability where indicated.
  • Create and maintain linkages to important community resources and assist families in accessing these resources, including medical and mental healthcare, substance abuse treatment, affordable housing, childcare, and public benefits.
  • Accompany participants to designated meetings and appointments for educational, medical, or treatment purposes, and/or to government and other community agencies in order to assist and encourage families in their progress towards meeting goals.
  • Manage basic administrative and organizational tasks for the program including obtaining needed consent forms and medical/educational records to update case records, preparing case tracking lists, and monitoring report submissions to ensure the meeting of time-sensitive milestones.
  • Complete statistical/written reports in required databases (Connections and PROMIS) including accurate and timely progress notes for contacts made with participants and summaries of school and treatment reports received.
  • Greet and welcome visitors and participants and respond to calls while covering the reception area as needed to support program.
  • Attend community-based and funder-provided training and informational sessions and share knowledge and resources with staff and participants.
  • Engage in crisis intervention activities as needed during periods of family instability, helping to de-escalate conflict and ensure safety.
  • Make State Central Register (SCR) reports when required to ensure responsiveness to immediate or impending child safety concerns.
  • Support the use of the Solution-Based Casework and Family Treatment/Rehabilitation models with all families.
  • Attend and participate in program staff meetings, as well as related agency training as appropriate.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualities Sought:

  • Works to create and support a respectful and collegial environment.
  • Handles administrative and clerical tasks with professionalism and competence, ensuring the success and effectiveness of the program at large.
  • Creates, embodies and supports a learning environment, regularly participating in training and professional development to augment case management skills and knowledge.
  • Offers and receives feedback and suggestions in a strength-based and constructive manner.
  • Dedicated to being a team player and active contributor to achieve the vision and mission of the program and agency.
  • Energetic, empathic, honest, genuine, professional, creative, and committed to making a positive contribution to families, the program, the community, and the agency as a whole.

Qualifications:

  • High School diploma is required; some college is preferred.
  • Bilingual in English/Spanish preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Excel, and Word) required.
  • At least one year of related experience working with children or families in a community-based setting is preferred.
  • Familiarity with Connections and PROMIS databases a plus.
  • Must be able to travel and feel comfortable making home visits throughout Brooklyn.
  • Willingness to understand and be sensitive to varied cultures & backgrounds.
  • Must have a proven record of successfully navigating New York City entitlement programs.
  • Must work a maximum of two evenings per week, as needed.
  • Must work with participants from a strength-based, youth and family development, and trauma-informed practice approach.

Benefits/Perks:

  • Tuition Assistance Program
  • Monthly MetroCards or travel reimbursement for use of personal vehicle will be provided to staff conducting home visits to families
  • Generous paid time off (Including 5 Self-Care Days/Floating Holidays, 12 Sick Days, 15 Vacation Days, and 11 Holidays)
  • Healthcare Plans (Medical, Dental, Vision, and Pet Care)
  • 403(b) Plan (GSS contributes 3% of your salary to your 403(b) plan after 3 years of service, with contributions increasing over time)

title: Director of First Impressions
description:
About Us

At Carlton, we are dedicated to enriching the lives of older adults by offering personalized care and fostering a warm and supportive environment. We know it takes a special group of individuals to help our residents live their lives to the fullest, surrounded by love, kindness, and care. We believe happy employees ensure happy residents. With attractive benefits, hands-on training, and opportunities for career advancement, we take great pride in recruiting people who embrace and embody our unique “culture of caring.”

Join our exceptional team at Carlton Senior Living as our Receptionist!

Why work with us:

  • Annual raises
  • Anniversary Bonus
  • Immediate Pay
  • Fitness/Education Reimbursement
  • Complimentary employee meals
  • Holiday pay
  • Sick/Vacation Time
  • Medical, Dental, Vision… and more!

What we are hiring for:

Schedule: Open Availability (7am - 9pm Sun-Sat)

Pay Range: $17.00 - $18.00

What You’ll Do:

  • Serve as the “Director of First Impressions” by greeting visitors, residents, and families with warmth and professionalism while providing accurate information and direction.
  • Answer and direct phone calls, monitor emergency systems, and respond promptly to resident and guest needs with a high level of customer service.
  • Support administrative tasks such as maintaining resident records, handling mail, and coordinating with maintenance or other departments as needed.
  • Assist the Sales and Activities teams by helping with event coordination, guest arrangements, and preparation of marketing materials.
  • Maintain a clean and organized front desk area, present a professional appearance, and stay informed about community events to keep residents and guests engaged.
  • Support safety protocols, emergency plans, and elopement prevention practices.
  • Foster a warm, collaborative atmosphere with residents, families, and team members.

Qualifications:

  • Must be at least eighteen (18) years or older, per Title 22 requirements
  • Prior administrative experience preferred but not required – we will train the right candidate!
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to interact effectively with residents, families, and team members.
  • Proficient in basic computer applications such as Microsoft Office, email, and scheduling systems.

title: Sub-Varsity Baseball Coach
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION.

Second Baptist School is currently seeking a SUB-VARSITYBASEBALL COACH for the 2026-2027 school year.

  • Campus Location: SBS Woodway
  • Reports To: Head Coach/Director of Athletics
  • Compensation: Seasonal, stipend

The goal of the Department of Athletics at Second Baptist School is to provide an environment of competition, cooperation and teamwork for our students that glorifies God and provides valuable life lessons. Winning the contest is important to any competitor, but the lessons learned in the heat of competition are the most important attributes to be gained from the contest.

JOB SUMMARY.

A Second Baptist School coach must be able to plan, organize and implement an appropriate athletic program that guides and encourages students to develop and fulfill their potential as an athlete, but more importantly, as an outstanding citizen. SBS offers a wide variety of teams, and coaches encourage students to try out for any and all sports offered. Coaching work is performed under the supervision of the Director of Athletics. The ideal candidate must:

  • Have a personal and passionate relationship with Jesus Christ and a calling to serve as a positive Christian role model to our students
  • Be a dedicated and loyal team member supporting all school-level activities and school-wide initiatives
  • Possess a strong desire to coach and develop all athletes
  • Have competency in playing and/or coaching baseball
  • Be committed to carrying out the policies and procedures of the SBS athletic handbook and assume responsibilities for all matters assigned by the school and the director of athletics
  • Be committed to Second Baptist Church and be a model of faithfulness in weekly Bible study and worship services
  • Be a responsible steward of the school’s resources

KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS REQUIRED.

To perform this job successfully, candidates must:

  • Hold a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution
  • Have prior experience in coaching and/or significant playing experience
  • Possess the ability to mentor student athletes in their Christian faith, athletic skills and life skills
  • Be adept at engaging with student athletes and families; helpful in making parents confident in their choice of Second Baptist School
  • Understand and embrace Christian education; have a biblical perspective on athletics and competition
  • Be able to establish and maintain cooperative and effective working relationships with others
  • Be personable, energetic and approachable
  • Report to work on a regular and punctual basis
  • Be committed to professional growth
  • Demonstrate excellent communication skills
  • Be willing to collaborate with colleagues
  • Be proficient in technology

Coaching experience, teacher certification and/or prior knowledge of Second Baptist Church and School will be considered a plus.

title: Dealer Solutions Manager
description:
Shaping the Future of Lending

With 30 years of fintech leadership, Origence empowers credit unions with innovative SaaS lending solutions that make lending more accessible, efficient, and competitive. We invest in our people and foster a culture of innovation, ownership, and continuous improvement. As we help shape the future of lending, we're leveraging AI to enhance the way we work and create value for our clients, and we're seeking individuals who are excited by emerging technologies and eager to use them responsibly to solve problems and drive impact.

The Dealer Solutions Manager will enhance, service, and monitor business relationships with existing Dealer clientele. Maintains and develops relationships with dealers in a defined area in order to enhance their overall CUDL experience, increase CUDL Dealer Portal features usage, product penetration, product retention, lender penetration, and market share based on management directed business plans and objectives. Client contact, client retention, product utilization, product penetration, and revenue growth are primary measurables.

***MUST BE LOCATED IN THE FORT WORTH, TEXAS AREA***

The Origence Mindset

At Origence, we are self-aware, adaptable, and relentlessly focused on creating meaningful impact. We think like owners, embrace complexity and ambiguity, challenge conventional thinking, and continuously pursue smarter, more effective ways to solve problems and advance the business. If this mindset reflects who you are, you may be exactly who we're looking for.

How You'll Contribute:

Relationship Management

  • Works to foster and enhance relationships, at multiple levels within the Dealer sales management vertical, through in person visits within an assigned area to create an excellent dealer experience with CUDL.
  • Trains appropriate dealer personnel in gaining better understanding of individual lender programs to increase dealer portal usage and greater lender penetrations.
  • Consults with existing Dealers regarding AutoSMART and various Digital Retail marketing products to assist dealer in better positioning themselves within their market.
  • Encourages a strong partnership between both Dealer and Lender clientele.
  • Works in collaboration with the Client and Product Support team, Lender Experience team, and Internal Dealer Experience team. This may include targeted joint dealer visits with lenders, dealer account servicing needs between internal team and field team, provide dealer/lender market feedback, and field support, etc.

Product Development

  • Sells to existing Dealers to increase or retain business through in person visits within assigned area. Maintains and enhances existing dealer network according to business plans and objectives.
  • Sells all Origence products including CUDL, AutoSMART, Vehicle Inventory Display, DMS, Digital Retail marketing, VERO, GAP, plus all other dealer related products according to business plan and objectives.
  • Identifies vehicle dealers changing ownership via buy/sell arrangement and works with both parties to ensure a smooth transition by collecting accurate information and follow up for contract execution.
  • Responsible for achieving business plan goals for all dealer related Origence products within assigned dealer region.

Product Maintenance

  • Properly trains dealer personnel on CUDL Dealer Portal usage and any other system enhancement or product.
  • Responsible for updating and maintaining accurate Dealer client contact information in CUDC database system.
  • Services and supports assigned CUDL dealers.
  • Works to ensure billing for existing dealer accounts is current or assists in collection of past due dealer revenue.
  • Works with any of the following Fleet, Finance, Marketing, BDC, or Internet dealer client staff to ensure auto related marketing and advertising activities are understood and completed on a regular basis.

Reporting and Documentation

  • Responsible for tracking all client related activity through Salesforce or other related CRM tools weekly or as directed by management.
  • Monitor and report to your Director of Dealer Experience on all relative trends affecting both the dealer retail market and the credit union industry.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

Education

  • BA/BS degree or commensurate experience

Experience

  • Three years successful experience in indirect auto finance industry or automotive digital retail marketing. Previous Salesforce experience a plus.

Your Strengths & Expertise

  • Work independently with a high level of initiative
  • Excellent oral, written, presentation and analytical skills
  • Ability to organize, prioritize work, meet deadlines and established goals.
  • Specialized problem solving and trouble shooting skills in the dealer business model.
  • Excellent internal and external customer service skills
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office programs to include Word, Excel and PowerPoint
  • Proficient in computer skills
  • Ability to travel and work daily in vehicle while visiting and servicing dealer clients. Up to 80% weekly car travel possible. Some overnight travel.
  • Must possess a valid driver’s license

Bring your ideas, your curiosity, and your unique perspective. We'll provide the opportunities, tools, and support to help you succeed.

How We Invest in You:

  • 401(k) with 8% Company Match
  • Flexible Work Environment
  • Competitive Paid Time Off
  • Tuition Reimbursement & Education Benefits
  • Comprehensive Health & Wellness Benefits
  • Microsoft Copilot and AI-Enabled Tools
  • Continuous Learning & Development Opportunities
  • A culture of connection, celebration, and growth through employee-driven programs, company events, holiday celebrations (Star Wars Day), monthly town halls, quarterly company meetings, and team traditions like Bring Your Kid to Work Day

Recognizing Your Impact

The starting salary range for this full-time position is $65000 - $80000 per year in addition to a quarterly incentive opportunity. We offer competitive compensation designed to recognize the value, experience, and contributions each team member brings to Origence. Base pay is determined by factors including experience, geographic location, and internal equity.

Origence is an equal opportunity employer. All recruitment, hiring, training, compensation, benefits, discipline, and other terms and conditions of employment will be based upon an individuals’ qualifications regardless of race, religion, color, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, ancestry, military service, marital status, pregnancy, age, protected medical condition, genetic information, disability or any other category protected by federal, state or local law.

title: Nursery Coordinator - Cypress
description:

Direct Supervisor: Nursery Director

The goal of the SecondKids Ministry is to create an environment that is positive and friendly in order to introduce children and their families to Jesus and God’s Word in a child friendly and age-appropriate way. Our nursery coordinators have the wonderful privilege of helping to lay a solid spiritual foundation and plant seeds for spiritual growth in our nursery ministry area. Qualifications

  • Growing relationship with Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior
  • A desire to minister to children and families

title: Service Desk Lead / Program Manager - VA C&P Help Desk 2.0 (Remote)
description:
Triumph Enterprises, Inc. is recruiting a Service Desk Lead / Program Manager for our proposed support to the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Office of Information and Technology, Compensation and Pension (C&P) Product Line Help Desk Tier 2 and Deployment Support Services 2.0. This position is contingent upon contract award. Remote work from anywhere in the United States.

ABOUT THE WORK

The Service Desk Lead manages Triumph's Tier 2 service desk and release support team for a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) claims-processing product line. You own delivery to the service-level agreements, lead a remote team of analysts across extended hours, and are the contractor's primary point of contact with the VA program office.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Plan, monitor and control all work; maintain the project management plan and bi-weekly progress reports, including workforce staffing data
  • Lead the 60-day transition-in: knowledge transfer, staff onboarding, background investigation tracking and Government-furnished equipment (GFE)
  • Run the Tier 2 service desk: staffing schedules across 102 coverage hours a week, 24/7 on-call rotation, two-senior-analyst review before escalation
  • Notify the VA C&P Service Desk Manager and Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) of high/critical priority incidents within 30 minutes and provide hourly updates
  • Represent the team at daily C&P and Enterprise Operations calls; provide subject matter expert support to C&P managers
  • Lead transition-out if exercised

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

  • U.S. citizenship required
  • Able to read, write, speak and understand English
  • Able to obtain and keep a VA Tier 2 / Moderate Risk background investigation; complete VA privacy and security training and sign the Contractor Rules of Behavior before system access
  • 7+ years in IT service desk or application support, including 3+ years leading Tier 2 teams of 10 or more
  • Experience managing to service-level agreements in ServiceNow
  • Bachelor's degree, or 4 additional years of relevant experience in lieu of a degree
  • Able to travel about once a year (2 days; Charleston, SC or Washington, DC)

PREFERRED CERTIFICATIONS

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) or Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM)
  • ITIL 4 Foundation
  • ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (Triumph will sponsor the exam for the selected candidate)

OTHER PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

Location: 2190 University Avenue, Bronx, NY 10453

  • Provide direct supervision and be accountable for the whereabouts of residents at all times.

  • Responsible for adhering to all pertinent ACS regulations.

  • Promote and model the seven Sanctuary Model commitments to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Integrate the Sanctuary Model SELF (Safety, Emotional Management, Loss and Future) framework into daily practice to ensure quality care and an effective work environment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma/GED required
  • Associate or bachelor's Degree preferred.
  • Valid New York State driver’s license
  • Must be able to complete and pass all components of the program’s designated behavior management/physical intervention training.

title: Records Governance and Legal Services Specialist
description:

The Records Governance and Legal Services Specialist plays a critical role in supporting the firm’s Information Governance function, with a dual focus on global records related initiatives and internal Legal Hold and eDiscovery operations. This position will report to and partner closely with the Records Governance Manager to ensure defensible, efficient, and legally sound handling of data across the information lifecycle.

Microsoft Purview & Technology Utilization

eDiscovery & Legal Hold Management (Preferred Experience)

Required:

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
  • 3–6+ years of experience in Records management or information governance.
  • Familiarity with legal concepts related to Records Retention, litigation, investigations, and regulatory matters.
  • Familiarity with domestic and international records management and retention frameworks.

Preferred:

  • Hands-on experience with eDiscovery review platforms (e.g., Relativity and Everlaw).

Key Competencies:

  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to translate technical concepts for legal audiences.
  • High level of discretion and professionalism when handling sensitive data.
  • Collaborative mindset with a client-service orientation.

title: Assistant Project Manager
description:
Purpose:

The Assistant Project Manager supports the Project Manager or Senior Project Manager in delivering safe, quality projects within budget and on schedule in accordance with Rabren Best Practices. This position manages assigned project processes and scopes, coordinates documentation and procurement, and supports financial management and closeout.

Duties and Responsibilities:

Best Practices & Relationships

  • Manage assigned scopes and project processes under the direction of the PM or SPM; coordinate with field leadership and subcontractors.
  • Build productive relationships with subcontractors, suppliers, owners, and design professionals; communicate issues and follow through on commitments.
  • Review contract documents for assigned work; identify scope gaps, conflicts, and decisions requiring PM or SPM direction.
  • Assist with project setup, planning, budgeting, and startup requirements.

Procurement & Contracts

  • Assist with buyout and subcontracts; coordinate trade partner qualification, approvals, and compliance records before work begins.
  • Track submittal approvals, long-lead items, and deliveries; coordinate with the Superintendent to address delays.

Financial Management

  • Track subcontractor change requests, pricing, approvals, billings, and correspondence; assist with preparing change orders and pay applications.
  • Support weekly and monthly job cost reviews, invoice coding, and cost projections for assigned work; raise potential overruns promptly.

Schedule

  • Assist with schedule updates and progress evaluations; identify constraints affecting assigned work and follow up on resolution.
  • Coordinate submittal reviews, procurement deadlines, and material deliveries with the project schedule; follow up on decisions affecting assigned scopes.

Safety & QA/QC

  • Support the project safety plan and QA/QC requirements; coordinate assigned inspections and follow up on documented deficiencies
  • Coordinate LEED documentation and compliance requirements when applicable to the project.

Daily Reports & Documentation

  • Manage the RFI process and assigned submittals, including review, routing, tracking, and follow-up to meet schedule requirements.
  • Maintain current drawings, specifications, revision logs, and project records in Procore or approved systems.
  • Organize assigned meetings, prepare agendas and minutes for PM review, and track action items; supplement daily reports and progress photos as needed.
  • Coordinate assigned punch list and closeout activities with subcontractors to meet contract deadlines.
  • Collect warranties, operating manuals, record documents, and turnover materials; support final accounting and assigned warranty follow-up.

Other Duties

  • This description does not cover every activity, duty, or responsibility required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Building Science, Construction Management, Civil Engineering, or a related field.
  • 2-5 years of commercial general contractor construction experience.
  • Understanding of building processes and systems for moderately complex construction projects.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office products, including Word and Excel.
  • Valid driver’s license.

Preferred Qualifications

  • LEED AP and/or Certified Construction Manager certification.
  • Experience with construction management software such as Procore and construction ERP accounting software such as Viewpoint.
  • Experience with scheduling software and BIM modeling.
  • OSHA 30 and First Aid/CPR.
  • Ability to communicate in Spanish.

Rabren Success Factors and Team Expectations

  • Drive for Results, Strive for Improvement, Create Trust with Character and Action, Team Up, Solve Complex Problems, and Build People.
  • Humble: Put the team first, welcome feedback, and share credit. Hungry: Take initiative, follow through, and pursue improvement. People Smart: Listen well, communicate respectfully, and consider how your actions affect others.

Supervisory Responsibility

May supervise Project Engineers and Interns as assigned. Follow Rabren policies and processes in supervisory activities. Establish goals and development plans with direct reports and monitor their progress and contribution to Rabren.

Work Environment and Physical Demands

  • Work in office and construction jobsite settings, including time outdoors.
  • Walk or stand for extended periods.
  • Lift or move up to 50 pounds.
  • Navigate areas under construction involving stooping, bending, kneeling, crouching, reaching, and twisting.
  • These duties may be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

Hours and Travel

Full-time position. Standard hours are Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Evening and weekend work is required as job duties demand. Travel to Rabren jobsites and offices is required.

Other Duties

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties, or responsibilities required of the employee. Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice.

title: Workers Compensation Specialist
description:
WHO WE ARE

IMT is proud of our heritage and will never forget where our roots are firmly planted. Locally run from its office in West Des Moines, Iowa, IMT has been a Midwest company since it was founded in Wadena, Iowa in 1884. That’s over 140 years!

Today, IMT continues to offer a strong line of personal and commercial insurance products for which it has always been known, along with exceptional service for a competitive price. Our products are offered through Independent Agents throughout a six-state territory – Iowa, Illinois, Minnesota, Nebraska, South Dakota, and Wisconsin.

WORKERS COMPENSATION SPECIALIST

IMT Insurance is seeking an individual to fill the position of Workers Compensation Specialist. In this position, you will be responsible for managing and overseeing a significant portfolio of claims, requiring advanced knowledge and decision-making skills. Other duties will include high-value or high-complexity claims, where deeper investigative work, negotiation, and coordination with external parties (i.e., legal counsel, medical providers, third-party administrators) are required. You will also play a leadership role, providing guidance and mentorship to junior staff while managing cases independently or with minimal supervision. If you are a detail-oriented, self-starter and interested in growing your knowledge within the Insurance industry, this is the perfect opportunity for you. Apply online today!

A DAY IN THE LIFE

  • Complex Claims Management: Independently manage a high-volume and high-complexity caseload, including severe injury claims, occupational disease claims, litigated claims, and claims involving multiple stakeholders (e.g., insurance carriers, legal teams, medical providers, and third-party administrators).
  • Advanced Case Reserve Management: Set and adjust substantial monetary reserves for large claims, factoring in medical costs, lost wages, future treatment, and potential legal settlements. Provide recommendations on reserve adjustments based on in-depth analysis of claims data.
  • Strategic Claims Oversight: Develop and implement strategies to efficiently manage complex claims, reduce claim costs, and expedite resolution. Work closely with legal counsel, medical experts, and external vendors to manage high-exposure claims.
  • Litigation & Settlement Negotiation: Act as the primary point of contact for complex claims litigation, providing guidance to legal teams, negotiating settlements, and ensuring that claims are resolved in the best interest of the organization while adhering to regulatory guidelines.
  • Leadership & Mentorship: Lead and mentor junior team members, including Work Comp Specialists I–III. Provide training on advanced claims management, legal and medical considerations, and effective negotiation strategies. Support team development and foster a collaborative work environment.
  • Program Development & Process Improvement: Contribute to the continuous improvement of the workers' compensation program by identifying areas for process enhancement, implementing best practices, and optimizing claims handling procedures.
  • Cross-Departmental Collaboration: Work with internal stakeholders to ensure a comprehensive approach to workers’ compensation claims. Participate in safety initiatives and return-to-work programs to reduce claim frequency and severity.
  • Reporting & Strategy: Prepare detailed reports and presentations for management on the performance of the workers' compensation program. Provide strategic recommendations for cost containment, claims management improvements, and risk mitigation.
  • Regulatory Compliance & Industry Leadership: Stay updated on changes to workers' compensation laws, regulations, and industry best practices. Ensure compliance with state and federal workers' compensation regulations, and serve as a subject matter expert on regulatory matters.
  • External Relationships: Manage relationships with external vendors, including third-party administrators (TPAs), medical providers, legal professionals, and insurers. Negotiate contracts and service level agreements (SLAs) to optimize service delivery and cost control.

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5-8 years of experience in Workers’ Compensation Claims Management, including handling complex or high-risk claims. At least 2-3 years of experience handling more complex or high-stake claims.
  • Relevant certifications, such as Certified Workers’ Compensation Professional (CWCP) or Associate in Risk Management (ARM), are preferred.
  • A high school diploma or equivalent is needed to perform normal functions. A Bachelor’s degree in business, insurance, risk management, or related field is preferred.
  • Advanced expertise in workers' compensation laws, claims management strategies, and litigation processes.
  • Strong leadership abilities with experience in mentoring, training, and developing staff.
  • Excellent negotiation skills and the ability to manage difficult claims and stakeholders effectively.
  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to present complex claims information to executive leadership and external partners.
  • Strong financial acumen for managing large claim reserves, budgeting, and cost-control initiatives.
  • Ability to analyze complex claims data and recommend actionable insights to improve claims handling processes.
  • High proficiency in claims management software, Microsoft Office Suite, and other industry-specific tools.

BENEFITS & PERKS

IMT Insurance is committed to our employees and their families. When you work for IMT, you earn far more than just a paycheck. The IMT office was new in 2018 and offers a fitness room, game room and a variety of collaboration areas. This position includes hybrid work arrangements, learning and development opportunities and more! Below is a list of what IMT offers our employees:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance, Life & A D & D insurance, 401K retirement savings accounts, spending accounts, long and short-term disability, profit share, paid vacation & sick time, employee assistant program and additional voluntary benefits.

The salary range for this position is $65,000.00 - $98,000.00

Starting salary and level of position will depend on level of experience.

This position is not eligible for tips or commission but may be eligible for additional bonuses

WHAT DEFINES US

Our vision is to provide peace of mind in the moments that matter.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant based on race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

Our agents and customers come from all walks of life and so do we. Our goal is to hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, because it makes our team stronger. If you share our values and our passion for creating a Worry Free life for others, we want to talk to you!

title: Director of Mentoring and Resource Development
description:
TITLE: DIRECTOR OF MENTORING SERVICES AND RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT

Reports to: Chief Program Officer of Youth and Family Wellbeing

Location: The position will be located at 305 7th Avenue, while requiring regular presence at YFWB locations in Brooklyn, Manhattan, and The Bronx.

Hours: 35 Hours/Week; Exempt

Salary: $80,000-$90,000/Annually (Based on relevant experience)

Job Summary: The Director of Mentoring provides strategic leadership for the design, implementation, and growth of a division-wide mentoring initiative that supports youth and young adults across the Youth & Family Wellbeing (YFWB) Division. This position is responsible for building and sustaining a comprehensive mentoring framework that integrates mentoring into the culture and practices of YFWB programs.

The Director will lead the recruitment, training, engagement, and retention of volunteer mentors while developing systems that prepare youth and staff to participate in meaningful mentoring relationships. Working collaboratively with program leaders, designated mentoring facilitators, and community partners, the Director will create a sustainable mentoring model that promotes positive youth development, educational attainment, career readiness, independent living skills, and social-emotional well-being.

Major Duties:

Strategic Leadership & Program Development

  • Develop and implement a division-wide mentoring strategy aligned with the mission, values, and goals of Youth & Family Wellbeing.
  • Embed mentoring as a core component of YFWB program culture and youth development practices.
  • Assess and refine existing mentoring recruitment, training, onboarding, and support systems.
  • Effectively uses, promotes, and models and practices our Trauma Informed Approach, Solution Based Casework and the Sanctuary Model Tools* to create a supportive, non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture
  • Establish policies, procedures, tools, and quality standards to ensure consistent mentoring practices across programs.
  • Monitor program outcomes and utilize data to strengthen mentoring effectiveness and participant experiences.
  • Track and record mentor/mentee participation and engagement for outcome reporting and continuous feedback to program leadership
  • Prepare reports and presentations for department leadership, funders, and stakeholders.

Mentoring Infrastructure & Facilitator Support

  • Recruit, train, and support designated staff representatives from YFWB programs to serve as Mentoring Facilitators.
  • Develop a facilitator training curriculum and ongoing professional development opportunities.
  • Collaborate with facilitators to identify and prepare youth and young adults for mentoring participation.
  • Support facilitators in conducting regular check-ins with mentees and monitoring mentoring relationships.
  • Convene facilitator meetings and communities of practice to share insights, challenges, and best practices.
  • Leverage facilitators' program expertise to continuously strengthen mentoring strategies and participant engagement.

Mentor Recruitment, Training & Retention

  • Design and implement a comprehensive mentor recruitment strategy utilizing internal staff, volunteers, corporate partners, and community organizations.
  • Build and maintain partnerships with organizations and employers that can serve as sources of volunteer mentors.
  • Recruit mentors whose lived experiences, backgrounds, and professional expertise align with the needs and aspirations of participating youth.
  • Develop and facilitate mentor screening, onboarding, orientation, and training processes.
  • Provide ongoing coaching, technical assistance, and support to mentors throughout their engagement.
  • Implement strategies to recognize, retain, and strengthen mentor participation.

Mentoring Match Development & Support

  • Collaborate with facilitators to assess youth needs, interests, strengths, and goals.
  • Create thoughtful mentor-mentee matches that support positive relationship-building and youth outcomes.
  • Determine appropriate mentoring models, including one-to-one, group, peer, or hybrid approaches.
  • Monitor mentoring relationships and intervene proactively to address challenges or barriers.
  • Ensure mentoring activities are youth-centered, culturally responsive, trauma-informed, and developmentally appropriate.
  • Establish systems for ongoing feedback from mentors, mentees, and staff.

Learning Communities & Professional Development

  • Facilitate monthly virtual peer-learning sessions for mentors and YFWB mentoring facilitators.
  • Create opportunities for participants to share successes, challenges, and effective practices.
  • Develop resources and tools that strengthen mentoring relationships and program quality.
  • Foster a culture of continuous learning and improvement across the mentoring initiative.

Partnership Development & Community Engagement

  • Build and maintain relationships with corporate, community, educational, and nonprofit partners that support mentoring efforts.
  • Collaborate with the External Relations Department to develop community relationships and resources that enhance mentoring opportunities for youth and mentors.
  • Represent the mentoring initiative in internal and external meetings, events, and partnership-building activities.
  • Identify opportunities to expand mentoring resources and funding support.

Preferred

  • Master's degree in a relevant field.
  • Experience managing mentoring programs and/or volunteer management systems.
  • Knowledge of positive youth development, trauma-informed care, restorative practices, and youth mentoring best practices.
  • Experience with data collection, program evaluation, and outcome measurement.
  • Experience building partnerships with corporate, educational, and community organizations.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in social work, Education, Human Services, Youth Development, Psychology, Public Administration, or a related field required.
  • Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible experience in youth development, mentoring, workforce development, education, or related human services programs.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and implementing programs across multiple sites or departments.
  • Experience recruiting, training, supervising, and supporting volunteers.
  • Strong facilitation, training, and relationship-building skills.
  • Experience working with diverse youth populations and communities.
  • Strong project management, organizational, and communication skills.

description:

The ServiceNow Administrator / Architect to lead the administration, configuration, and optimization of our newly implemented ServiceNow platform. The ideal candidate will help drive long-term platform strategy, ensure operational excellence, and become the internal subject matter expert as we scale our use of the platform.

***Please note, this position will follow a Hybrid schedule with a minimum of 3 days in the office/week***

What You’ll Be Doing:

    Module Configuration and Customization:
    • Configure and maintain ServiceNow modules including:
      • ITSM: Incident, Problem, Change, Service Catalog, Knowledge
      • ITOM: CMDB, Discovery
      • ITAM: Hardware and Software Asset Management
      • CSM: Customer Service Management
    • Develop and support custom applications, workflows, UI policies, business rules, and UI actions using ServiceNow Studio and Flow Designer.
    • Create and maintain custom roles, forms, views, and reports to support evolving business needs.
  2. Platform Administration:
    • Oversee all aspects of the ServiceNow platform, including updates, patches, configurations, and daily maintenance.
    • Monitor platform performance, health, and security; identify and remediate operational issues.
    • Manage user roles, access control, data integrity, and compliance with internal IT security policies.
  3. Security and Compliance:
    • Implement role-based access controls, data encryption, and compliance configurations in line with organizational security policies.
    • Support internal and external audits by ensuring configuration and documentation are aligned with compliance requirements.
  4. Integration and Automation:
    • Integrate ServiceNow with external systems and applications via REST/SOAP APIs and other integration tools.
    • Automate manual processes to improve efficiency and reduce operational overhead.
  5. Data Management:
    • Ensure data accuracy and consistency through import sets, transform maps, and regular audits.
    • Design and maintain dashboards, performance analytics, and scheduled reports to support decision-making and operational transparency.
  6. Continuous Improvement:
    • Stay current with ServiceNow releases, features, and industry best practices.
    • Identify and propose enhancements to improve platform performance, user experience, and business outcomes.
    • Participate in planning, testing, and rollout of upgrades and new features.

The Ideal Candidate:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience as a ServiceNow Administrator in a corporate environment.

Certifications (Preferred but not required):

  • ServiceNow Certified System Administrator (CSA) – required
  • ServiceNow Certified Implementation Specialist – preferred
  • ITIL v4 Foundation certification – preferred

Technical Skills:

  • Strong proficiency in JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and other scripting languages used within ServiceNow.
  • Experience with REST, SOAP, LDAP, and other integration technologies.
  • Familiarity with ServiceNow modules: ITSM, ITOM, ITAM, and CSM.
  • Experience with ServiceNow Studio, Flow Designer, and Performance Analytics.
  • Knowledge of cloud platforms and services is a plus.

Specialized Skills:

  • Strong problem-solving skills with keen attention to detail.
  • Effective communicator with the ability to collaborate across technical and non-technical teams.
  • Comfortable working in fast-paced, dynamic environments with shifting priorities.
  • Proficient with MDM tools such as Intune, JAMF, and SCCM.
  • Quick to learn and adapt to emerging technologies and applications.
  • Experienced in automating processes using scripting languages like PowerShell.
  • Capable of translating technical specifications into clear, actionable, non-technical requirements.
  • Contributes to process documentation and provides training support as needed.

Why you should apply:

  • Flexible Working Environment
  • Paid Time Off
  • 401k (8% match)
  • College Tuition Benefits/ Tuition Reimbursement
  • Good Benefits options
  • Company Culture! Cultural and Holiday celebrations, Theme days like Star Wars Day & Bring your Kids to Work Day, Monthly Townhalls and Quarterly Company Meetings that ensure awareness, inclusion, and transparency.

Origence maintains a highly competitive compensation program. Under company guidelines, this position is eligible for an annual bonus to provide an incentive to achieve targeted goals. Bonuses are awarded at company’s discretion on an individual basis.

title: Temp Referral Clerk
company: Community Health Centers of the Central Coast
description:
Job Title: Referral Clerk

Department: Referral Center

Reports To: Director of Utilization Management (UM) and Referrals

FLSA Status: Non-Exempt

Wage Range that the Company Expects to Pay: $26.50 - $29.22 per hour

SUMMARY

Under the direct supervision of the Director of UM and Referrals, the Referral Clerk is responsible for processing specialty referral orders by obtaining insurance authorization, attaching clinical documents, and submitting to specialty offices. The Referral Clerk communicates with patients about referral details and documents in the electronic health record. The Referral Clerk obtains specialist consultation notes and closes referrals.

It is the primary purpose of CHCCC to provide the highest quality of total care possible to the patient population it serves. Such a level of quality depends ultimately on the staff's desire and ability to work together, individually, and as a team. The employee is expected to be professional, punctual, maintain regular attendance, cooperative, motivated, and organized at all times.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES include the following. Additional duties may be assigned with or without prior notice.

Selects referrals from assigned site bucket, reviews referral order, and chart documents for appropriateness and completeness.

Contacts patient to confirm referral and advises patient of referral detail.

Obtains insurance authorization for referral and uploads into the electronic health record.

Collates electronic documents relevant to referral order (chart notes, diagnostic studies, authorization) and submits to specialist.

Documents actions in electronic health record.

Selects follow up from assigned site bucket, reviews referral documentation, and looks for associated consultation notes in electronic health record.

Contacts patient to confirm specialty appointment was made, kept, and notes date in electronic health record.

Contacts specialty office to request consultation report, if indicated.

Answers incoming telephone calls from patients or offices and addresses needs of the caller.

Reviews and responds to patient cases as assigned.

Completes chart processing and RAF requests as assigned from the Utilization Management bucket.

Requests consultation notes and/or prescriptions for 340B claims as assigned.

Demonstrates professionalism and provides quality customer service using AIDET Standards.

Ability to work with high volume of patients, internal/external customers, and deal with frequent changes, delay or unexpected events.

Demonstrates adherence to and observes all safety policies and procedures, inclusive of infection control rules and regulations.

Demonstrates the knowledge and skills necessary to provide care appropriate to the age of the patients served (infants, pediatrics, adolescents, adults or geriatrics).

Demonstrates knowledge of domestic violence, child and dependent abuse protocols.

Demonstrates cultural sensitivity and competence with patients.

Maintains and adheres to HIPAA, employee confidentiality, and privileged communications (patient, employee, and corporation).

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This job has no supervisory responsibilities.

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

COMPETENCIES

To perform the job successfully, an individual should demonstrate the following characteristics: resourceful, independence, detail-oriented, professionalism, problem-solver, multi-tasker, team player, and customer service.

EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

High school diploma or GED required. Graduation from an accredited school in Medical Assisting or a certified or registered medical assistant (CMA/RMA), or other relevant medical experience.

LANGUAGE SKILLS

Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals. Ability to respond effectively to the most sensitive inquires or complaints. Ability to write routine reports and correspondence. Ability to speak effectively before groups of patients or employees of organization.

Bilingual - ability to read, speak, and write in English and another language is strongly preferred.

MATHEMATICAL SKILLS

Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret bar graphs.

REASONING ABILITY

Ability to apply sound judgment in understanding to carry out instructions in written or oral form. Ability to make appropriate job decisions following standard office policies and past precedents.

COMPUTER SKILLS

Experience with word processing, spreadsheets, email, and keyboarding required. Microsoft Office and Google Suite skills required. Working knowledge of EHR required.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

Possession of current, valid, unrestricted California Driver's License (Class C) required.

OTHER REQUIREMENTS

Required to pass a criminal history background check and drug screen upon hire.

Annual health examination; annual Tuberculosis skin test clearance or chest x-ray; proof of immunity to MMR, Varicella, and Hepatitis B; proof of Tdap vaccine; during current flu season, must provide proof of influenza vaccine or a signed declination form. If declined, a flu mask is mandatory during flu season.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

This job is largely sedentary. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. The employee will have repetitive finger and hand motions when typing. The employee will regularly need to operate a computer, keyboard, and telephone. The employee is regularly required to sit for an extended period of time however, may be frequently required to stand and walk. The employee may need to lift and/or move up to 25 pounds of supplies. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is occasionally exposed to risk of electrical shock. The noise level in the work environment is moderate (i.e. office setting with computers, phones, and printers). Must be able to work in a cubicle setting and work in a fast-paced environment consisting of inbound and outbound calls.

Must be willing to have a flexible work schedule that may include evenings/weekends, and travel as needed.
