title: Youth Ministry Director at Fort Belvoir, Virginia
description:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.

Salary:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Location:

Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:

title: Case Planner (EFFC)
description:
We are looking for a dynamic and compassionate Case Planner to join our team. In this role you will work towards timely permanency planning for children and youth in foster care.

Reports to: Foster Care Supervisor

Location: 7 West Burnside Avenue, Bronx, New York 10453

Hours: 35 Hours / Week; Non-Exempt - Position requires in office hours and field visits. Hybrid schedules are based on program needs and leadership discretion.

Salary Range: 50k-55K based on relevant experience and education.

Major Duties:

  • Assess and monitor for safety and risk.
  • Establish immediate contact with families of the children who are placed into our care, and with their foster families.
  • Conduct required casework contacts with the child, parent, foster parent and collateral contacts (schools, service providers, medical personnel, mental health practitioners, and substance abuse counselors). Make assessment-based referrals as necessary to meet the needs of the child and/or parent.
  • Visit family and child, as often as mandated and/or necessary to gather social history, to assess family strengths and concerns, and to assess existing problems in relation to the reason for placement.
  • Coordinate and supervise all visits between the family and child along with separate sibling visits.
  • Share responsibilities with agency team for the permanency planning of each child.
  • Locate resources and make referrals to any resource that would provide aid to the family and child.
  • Evaluate child’s adjustment in foster home and monitor educational and behavioral performance at home and in school.
  • Monitor foster parents in terms of their ability to meet the needs of the child in their home, and make recommendations regarding future use of the home, in conjunction with the Home finding Department.
  • Adherence to the KEEP (Keeping Foster and Kinship Parents Supported and Trained), PTC (Parenting Through Change) and YDSC (Youth Development Skills Coaching) manuals.
  • Make efficient and creative use of training manuals.
  • Capacity to work within the fidelity guidelines of the KEEP/PTC interventions while delivering the material in the manner that appeals to the needs of individual parents and youth.
  • Support and counsel foster parents in their efforts to care for the child and include them in the development of the goals and tasks.
  • Keep case records up to date within agency standards and complete all necessary ACS/Agency documentation including FASPs, Progress notes, Permanency Hearing reports and all other reports necessary to fulfill the function of the work.
  • Make all court appearances and testimony including permanency hearings.
  • Participate in Family Team Conferences, including but not limited to the placement preservation, reunification/discharge, goal changes and permanency planning conferences. Attend all necessary meetings, functions, workshop, etc. as required by the agency.
  • Keep case records up to date within agency standards and complete all necessary ACS/Agency documentation including FASPs, Progress notes, Permanency Hearing reports and all other reports necessary to fulfill the function of the work.
  • Progress notes are to be completed and submitted preferably within one day of the event but no later than the end of the given week of the event.
  • FASP and Permanency Hearing Report will be submitted on the internal date for review provided by the agency's compliance department.
  • Collaborate closely with team members.
  • Conduct Group facilitation of Keep and PTC groups with parents and foster parents.
  • Ability to enhance communication among parent group members to promote skill development and social networking.
  • Review KEEP/PTC feedback and practice strategies with families.
  • Collaborate closely with Youth Skill Trainers, monitor their interactions with youth.
  • Documents according to developer’s standards, each interaction and visit.
  • Effectively use and practice the Sanctuary Model tools: safety plans, community meetings, psycho-educational groups, team meetings, red flag reviews, treatment planning conferences (or similar), and self-care, when applicable, in the department/program to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Promote and model the seven Sanctuary Model commitments to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Integrate the Sanctuary Model SELF (Safety, Emotional Management, Loss and Future) framework into daily practice to ensure quality care and an effective work environment
  • Utilize Solution Based Casework in casework practice.
  • Implement Solution Based Casework model of casework practice within the department/program.
  • Implement and integrate the principles and procedures of Solution Based Casework: assessment, family and individual level outcomes, action plans and documentation and celebration.
  • Actively participate in case consultation, continued SBC training and the SBC certification process.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in related field required;
  • MSW or at least one year related experience preferred.
  • Must be able to establish working relationships with clients in need of counseling and supportive services.
  • Must be able to effectively engage parents.
  • Ability to apply theory of change.
  • Willingness to facilitate groups with parents and foster parents.
  • Ability to work cooperatively with their agency supervisor(s), KEEP, PTC, and YDSC consultants, ACS and other team members.
  • Excellent written and verbal skills necessary.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred.
  • Some evenings may be required
  • Must have a commitment to work from a strength based and/or youth development perspective.

title: In-Home Personal Care Attendant (PCA)
description:
Job Title: In-Home Personal Care Attendant (PCA)
Department: In-Home PCA
Reports To: Program Manager- In Home Services
FLSA: Non-Exempt

For the Maryville, MO Area


SUMMARY
The position involves providing caregiving and personal care services to individuals who have disabilities within the comfort of their homes.


BASIC FUNCTIONS AND GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Provide cleaning services including but not limited to vacuuming, dusting, washing dishes, appliance care, running errands and laundering clothing, reading, and writing essential correspondence for blind, illiterate or physically impaired individuals.
• Provide personal care services including but not limited to hair care, assistance with bathing and meal preparation.
• Maintain records of service delivery including time sheets, calendars, and incident documentation
• Report any problems related to a participant or plan of care to supervisor.
• Complete required hours of continued training annually to meet state eligibility guidelines.
• Effectively and efficiently use computers or mobile devices to input, access, modify, or output information. This includes the ability to quickly access, store and retrieve data.
• All Other Duties as Assigned


Physical Expectations
• This position requires extended periods of walking and standing with some periods of sitting which are dependent upon the needs and activities of the individuals supported. It may require light to heavy lifting, up to fifty pounds independently, and occasional stooping, kneeling, bending, and/or climbing stairs depending on the needs of the individual supported.
• The position will require occasional physical intervention if confronted by a person displaying combative or potentially dangerous behavior.


Working Conditions
Office/home environment with noises from appliances, telephones, and occasional small machinery (lawn mower, etc.). May be exposed to bloodborne pathogens and/or infectious diseases. Occasionally, prolonged hours or unusual chores to meet the unexpected needs of the individuals (i.e., medical and/or behavioral).


QUALIFICATIONS
• High School Diploma or commitment to obtain HiSet or GED.
• Six months of experience as a care provider, CNA, housekeeper, or household worker, or one year of experience caring for children, sick or elderly individuals
• Ability to perform a variety of cleaning tasks and mobility to negotiate a variety of obstacles in client homes.

• Must not have been convicted of any disqualifying misdemeanor or felony and must not have been substantiated for abuse or neglect in the state of Missouri, as recorded by the Department of Mental Health’s Employee Disqualification List.

title: Case Manager - BRAG Restore
description:
The Case Manager (Credible Messenger) provides intensive, trauma-informed case management and supportive services to young adults (ages 16–25) at elevated risk of engaging in serious violence. Grounded in the Cure Violence Global model, the Sanctuary Model, and Trauma-Informed Care, the Case Manager serves as the participant's primary point of support by building trusting relationships, coordinating services, providing crisis intervention, and promoting long-term stability. Working collaboratively with the Program Director and Educational/Vocational Specialist, the Case Manager develops individualized Sustainable Growth Plans, monitors participant progress, connects participants to community resources, and supports positive youth development through strength-based and restorative practices

TITLE: Case Manager (CREDIBLE MESSENGER) – B.R.A.G. Restore

REPORTS TO: PROGRAM DIRECTOR, B.R.A.G. WEST/RESTORE

LOCATION: 1995 Jerome Ave., Bronx, NY & 1 East Fordham Rd. Bronx NY

HOURS: 35 Hours/Week, Non-Exempt

SALARY: $48,000 - $53,000

MAJOR DUTIES:

Participant Engagement & Case Management

  • Maintain a caseload of approximately 7–8 participants.
  • Complete trauma-informed intake assessments using the At-Risk Criteria (ARC) screening tool.
  • Develop and update individualized Sustainable Growth Plans based on participant strengths, needs, and goals.
  • Conduct weekly case management sessions and maintain consistent participant engagement through office, home, hospital, and community visits.
  • Build trusting relationships through mentorship, advocacy, and participant-centered support.
  • Engage families and natural supports when appropriate.
  • Monitor participant progress and adjust service plans as needed.

Crisis Intervention & Violence Prevention

  • Assess participant safety and develop individualized safety plans.
  • Respond to crises involving violence, victimization, housing instability, behavioral health, family conflict, or legal involvement.
  • Utilize trauma-informed interventions, motivational interviewing, restorative practices, and de-escalation strategies.
  • Collaborate with outreach staff during conflict mediation and community violence response efforts.

Service Coordination & Advocacy

  • Coordinate referrals and ongoing service connections for behavioral health, substance use treatment, housing, healthcare, legal services, food assistance, public benefits, domestic violence services, and family supports.
  • Advocate for participants with community agencies, healthcare providers, schools, courts, and other service systems.
  • Monitor service engagement and assist participants in overcoming barriers to accessing care.

Mentorship & Group Facilitation

  • Provide individual mentoring and supportive counseling that promotes healthy decision-making, emotional regulation, conflict resolution, accountability, resilience, and self-advocacy.
  • Plan, coordinate, and facilitate workshops, ensuring engaging and effective delivery of training and learning sessions.
  • Facilitate or co-facilitate psychoeducational groups focused on violence prevention, trauma recovery, restorative practices, emotional wellness, healthy relationships, stress management, and personal growth.
  • Encourage participation in program activities that support individual goals.

Documentation & Compliance

  • Maintain accurate and timely participant records, including assessments, case notes, progress notes, safety plans, referrals, and incident reports.
  • Enter participant information into Salesforce and other required databases within established timelines.
  • Maintain confidentiality and comply with agency policies and applicable regulations.
  • Review, complete, and approve participant timesheets to ensure accuracy, compliance, and timely payroll processing.
  • Manage and facilitate the participant onboarding process within ADP(Payroll System), ensuring accurate and timely completion of required documentation and system setup.

Team Collaboration

  • Participate in supervision, case conferences, staff meetings, training, and community meetings.
  • Collaborate with program staff while maintaining clear professional roles.
  • Support program events, quality improvement efforts, and other duties as assigned.

Practice Framework - Provide services consistent with:

  • Cure Violence Global
  • Sanctuary Model
  • Trauma-Informed Care
  • Positive Youth Development
  • • Restorative Practices
  • Strength-Based Case Management
  • Integrate the Sanctuary SELF Framework to promote safety, healing, resilience, and participant empowerment.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Required: High School Diploma/GED & a minimum of six years' experience providing case management, counseling, youth development, or related services.
  • Preferred: Bachelor’s degree in Social Work, Human Services, Psychology, Criminal Justice, Sociology, or a related field & a minimum of two years' experience providing case management, counseling, youth development, or related services.
  • Experience working with justice-involved, violence-impacted, or high-risk youth and young adults preferred.
  • Knowledge of trauma-informed care, crisis intervention, community resources, and case management practices.
  • Strong assessment, organizational, documentation, and communication skills.
  • Ability to establish effective relationships with participants and collaborate within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and electronic case management systems.
  • Ability to travel throughout New York City and work flexible evening and weekend hours.
  • Credible Messenger with relevant lived experience is strongly preferred.
  • Experience with Motivational Interviewing and restorative practices.
  • Familiarity with the Bronx and surrounding communities.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.

Salary:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Location:

Club Beyond works on military installations all over the world. We currently have openings at:

title: QIDP
description:
Job Overview:

As a Qualified Intellectual Disabilities Professional (QIDP) at Glenkirk, you will assume a pivotal role in coordinating and overseeing services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities. You will be responsible for ensuring the development, implementation, and evaluation of individualized service plans, with a focus on enhancing the quality of life and promoting independence. The successful candidate will demonstrate expertise in program coordination, regulatory compliance, and a commitment to person-centered care.

Key Responsibilities:

  1. Individualized Service Planning:
    • Develop, implement, and regularly review individualized service plans (ISP) in collaboration with clients, their families, and interdisciplinary teams.
    • Ensure that ISP goals align with clients' preferences, needs, and overall well-being.
  2. Regulatory Compliance:
    • Stay informed about and ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations governing services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
    • Prepare for and participate in regulatory inspections and audits.
  3. Client Advocacy:
    • Advocate for the rights and preferences of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
    • Collaborate with clients and their families to address concerns and facilitate communication with the interdisciplinary team.
  4. Program Coordination:
    • Coordinate and oversee the delivery of services, ensuring that they are consistent with individualized service plans and regulatory requirements.
    • Monitor program outcomes and make recommendations for improvement.
  5. Staff Supervision:
    • Supervise and provide guidance to direct support professionals and other relevant staff.
    • Facilitate training sessions to ensure staff competency and adherence to established standards.
  6. Quality Assurance:
    • Implement quality assurance measures, including regular assessments, audits, and outcome evaluations.
    • Identify opportunities for improvement and implement corrective actions as needed.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in a related field (Social Work, Human Services, Psychology, etc.) required.
  • Certification as a QIDP or eligibility for QIDP certification.
  • Previous experience in a similar role, preferably in services for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
  • Strong organizational and leadership skills.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities.

Benefits:

  • Annual salary of $45,000.
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance options.
  • Retirement savings plan.
  • Professional development opportunities.
  • A collaborative and inclusive work environment committed to the well-being and empowerment of individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

title: Youth Development Counselor (Euphrasian) - Overnight Shift ONLY
description:
Are you looking to make a difference in a child’s life? Do you love helping people reach their full potential? Do you want to feel good about the job you are doing? If you answered yes to all these questions, then we want you to join our team! We are looking for a dynamic and compassionate Youth Development Counselor to work alongside other team members to provide 24 hours supervision, structure and guidance to the residents of a 10-bed female adolescent Youth Reception Center. The Youth Development Counselor works with participants and their families to create a therapeutic milieu in which each participant is able to reach their potential and learn socially appropriate behavior, homemaking skills and develop their individual skills and abilities.

Job Title: Youth Development Counselor - Overnight Shift ONLY

Reports to: Residential Life Supervisor; Euphrasian Diagnostic Center

Location: 479 Jersey Avenue, Brooklyn, New York 11207

Hours: 40/hours non-exempt. Position requires staff to be onsite. Must be available full time for Day; Evening and/or Overnight Shift. Some weekend shifts will be required.

Salary Range: $20-$22 per hour

Major Duties:

  • Ensure the whereabouts and safety of participants at all times.
  • Plan, lead and engage participants in a range of program activities including recreational activities, family activities, tutoring, cultural events, and special activities for evenings or weekends.
  • Escort participants to and from court, school, medical, pre-placement visits to other agencies, family/sibling visits, and other various appointments.
  • Monitor participants’ school performance, including homework assistance and tutoring.
  • Supervise and record participant medical needs and follow-up on recommendations.
  • Attend teacher/social worker update meetings.
  • Maintain documentation logs of daily activities, progress notes and critical events.
  • Complete assessments and reports for presentation at team meetings.
  • Attend all mandatory meetings and trainings.
  • Participate in multi-disciplinary meetings.
  • Effectively use and practice the Sanctuary Model tools: safety plans, community meetings, psycho-educational groups, team meetings, red flag reviews, treatment planning conferences (or similar), and self-care in the department/program to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Promote and model the seven Sanctuary Model commitments to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Integrate the Sanctuary Model SELF (Safety, Emotional Management, Loss and Future) framework into daily practice to ensure quality care and an effective work environment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or GED required;
  • Associate or bachelor’s degree preferred.
  • Must have excellent written, organizational, and prioritization skills.
  • Ability to transition easily between working independently with a high degree of self-initiative and contributing as part of a team.
  • Valid Driver's License required; comfortable driving in the New York Metro areas including the five boroughs and Long Island.
  • Participate in creating a safe and therapeutic milieu.
  • Effective in conflict resolution and crisis intervention techniques and practices.
  • Must be able to successfully complete state mandated crisis intervention training and perform physical restraint of a resident.
  • Must be able to successfully complete state mandated medication administration training.
  • Must be flexible to work evening, overnight, weekend and holiday hours.
  • Must have a commitment to work from a strength-based, youth and family development and trauma-informed perspective.
  • Bilingual – Spanish preferred.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Must be able to successfully complete state mandated crisis intervention training within two months of hire
  • Must successfully complete a pre-hire physical ability test.
  • Ability to perform physical restraint of youth using approved restraint procedures.
  • Must be capable of sustained physical exertion and have no limitations on ability to engage in necessary physical intervention activities including but not limited to standing, twisting, turning, kneeling, and supporting a participant’s body weight.

title: Temp Case Planner (EFFC)
description:
We are looking for a dynamic and compassionate Case Planner to join our team. In this role you will work towards timely permanency planning for children and youth in foster care.

Reports to: Foster Care Supervisor

Location: 7 West Burnside Avenue, Bronx, New York 10453

Hours: 35 Hours / Week; Non-Exempt - Position requires in office hours and field visits. Hybrid schedules are based on program needs and leadership discretion.

Salary Range: 50k-55K based on relevant experience and education.

Major Duties:

  • Assess and monitor for safety and risk.
  • Establish immediate contact with families of the children who are placed into our care, and with their foster families.
  • Conduct required casework contacts with the child, parent, foster parent and collateral contacts (schools, service providers, medical personnel, mental health practitioners, and substance abuse counselors). Make assessment-based referrals as necessary to meet the needs of the child and/or parent.
  • Visit family and child, as often as mandated and/or necessary to gather social history, to assess family strengths and concerns, and to assess existing problems in relation to the reason for placement.
  • Coordinate and supervise all visits between the family and child along with separate sibling visits.
  • Share responsibilities with agency team for the permanency planning of each child.
  • Locate resources and make referrals to any resource that would provide aid to the family and child.
  • Evaluate child’s adjustment in foster home and monitor educational and behavioral performance at home and in school.
  • Monitor foster parents in terms of their ability to meet the needs of the child in their home, and make recommendations regarding future use of the home, in conjunction with the Home finding Department.
  • Adherence to the KEEP (Keeping Foster and Kinship Parents Supported and Trained), PTC (Parenting Through Change) and YDSC (Youth Development Skills Coaching) manuals.
  • Make efficient and creative use of training manuals.
  • Capacity to work within the fidelity guidelines of the KEEP/PTC interventions while delivering the material in the manner that appeals to the needs of individual parents and youth.
  • Support and counsel foster parents in their efforts to care for the child and include them in the development of the goals and tasks.
  • Keep case records up to date within agency standards and complete all necessary ACS/Agency documentation including FASPs, Progress notes, Permanency Hearing reports and all other reports necessary to fulfill the function of the work.
  • Make all court appearances and testimony including permanency hearings.
  • Participate in Family Team Conferences, including but not limited to the placement preservation, reunification/discharge, goal changes and permanency planning conferences. Attend all necessary meetings, functions, workshop, etc. as required by the agency.
  • Keep case records up to date within agency standards and complete all necessary ACS/Agency documentation including FASPs, Progress notes, Permanency Hearing reports and all other reports necessary to fulfill the function of the work.
  • Progress notes are to be completed and submitted preferably within one day of the event but no later than the end of the given week of the event.
  • FASP and Permanency Hearing Report will be submitted on the internal date for review provided by the agency's compliance department.
  • Collaborate closely with team members.
  • Conduct Group facilitation of Keep and PTC groups with parents and foster parents.
  • Ability to enhance communication among parent group members to promote skill development and social networking.
  • Review KEEP/PTC feedback and practice strategies with families.
  • Collaborate closely with Youth Skill Trainers, monitor their interactions with youth.
  • Documents according to developer’s standards, each interaction and visit.
  • Effectively use and practice the Sanctuary Model tools: safety plans, community meetings, psycho-educational groups, team meetings, red flag reviews, treatment planning conferences (or similar), and self-care, when applicable, in the department/program to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Promote and model the seven Sanctuary Model commitments to create a non-violent and trauma-sensitive culture.
  • Integrate the Sanctuary Model SELF (Safety, Emotional Management, Loss and Future) framework into daily practice to ensure quality care and an effective work environment
  • Utilize Solution Based Casework in casework practice.
  • Implement Solution Based Casework model of casework practice within the department/program.
  • Implement and integrate the principles and procedures of Solution Based Casework: assessment, family and individual level outcomes, action plans and documentation and celebration.
  • Actively participate in case consultation, continued SBC training and the SBC certification process.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in related field required;
  • MSW or at least one year related experience preferred.
  • Must be able to establish working relationships with clients in need of counseling and supportive services.
  • Must be able to effectively engage parents.
  • Ability to apply theory of change.
  • Willingness to facilitate groups with parents and foster parents.
  • Ability to work cooperatively with their agency supervisor(s), KEEP, PTC, and YDSC consultants, ACS and other team members.
  • Excellent written and verbal skills necessary.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish preferred.
  • Some evenings may be required
  • Must have a commitment to work from a strength based and/or youth development perspective.

title: Cleanroom Technician, Fresenius Kabi Canada
description:
As a global healthcare company, Fresenius Kabi is Committed to Life. The company’s products, technologies, and services are used for the therapy and care of critically and chronically ill patients. With more than 41,000 employees and presence in over 100 countries, Fresenius Kabi’s expansive product portfolio focuses on providing access to high-quality and lifesaving medicines and technologies.

WHAT WE OFFER!
At Fresenius Kabi Canada we foster a collaborative environment where employees are encouraged to share ideas and contribute to meaningful work.   • Company matched RRSP program
  • Generous vacation plan with one extra day accrual for each year of service
  • Paid float days and paid sick days
  • Employee assistance program
  • Casual office dress code
  • Employee recognition program
  • Perkopolis & Goodlife Discounts
  • Professional growth and development opportunities

We are currently seeking a Cleanroom Technician to join our team!

On-site requirement 5 days/week

Location: 2400 Skymark Avenue, Unit 4, Mississauga, ON, L4W 5K5

The pay rate for this role is: $27 - $28.50.

Placement within the range will be determined based on relevant skills, experience, qualifications, and internal equity. The final offer will reflect the successful candidate's background and demonstrated capabilities.

This position is an existing vacancy within the organization

POSITION SUMMARY
The Cleanroom Technician reports to the Pharmacy Production Supervisor and operates within the Production department at Fresenius Kabi Canada’s Hospital Compounding facility. Under the direction of the Supervisor, Cleanroom Team Lead, Manager of Cleanroom Operations, and/or Pharmacist in Charge, the technician is responsible for the aseptic preparation of sterile admixtures in accordance with company guidelines and master batch records.

In addition to compounding activities, the role supports staging, picking, decontamination, labeling, inspection, and packaging of all compounded batches.

KEY RESPONSIILITIES

  • Prepare sterile products using proper aseptic techniques in compliance with established procedures
  • Adhere to GMP standards, SOPs, and all quality and safety requirements
  • Perform staging, decontamination, labeling, inspection, and packaging activities
  • Maintain proper line clearance and ensure accuracy during all production steps
  • Operate and maintain production equipment safely and effectively
  • Ensure adequate availability of cleanroom supplies to meet production needs
  • Complete all required in-process checks to maintain compliance and product quality
  • Participate in inventory counts, validations, calibration, and environmental monitoring
  • Maintain cleanliness, organization, and proper waste handling in cleanroom areas
  • Support training of new employees and continuous improvement initiatives
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and other departments
  • Maintain up-to-date training and comply with all company policies and procedures


WORKING CONDITIONS

  • Extended periods of standing and repetitive motions

Company: Interstate Power Systems
Locations: Kearney, NE • Grand Island, NE • Norfolk, NE • Fremont, NE •

Interstate Power Systems location in Omaha is expanding across Nebraska and Iowa and is seeking experienced Field Power Generation Technicians/Mechanics to support our growing customer base. This role focuses on generator service, maintenance, and repair, with opportunities available in multiple locations. We offer highly competitive wages and a dynamic field-based work environment.

As a Field Power Generation Technician/Mechanic, you will be responsible for diagnosing, maintaining, and repairing power generation systems—primarily, diesel-driven generators—to ensure reliable and efficient operation. You’ll work directly in the field, responding to customer needs, performing preventative maintenance, troubleshooting complex mechanical and electrical issues, and completing repairs safely and efficiently.

Key responsibilities include monitoring generator performance, conducting routine inspections and maintenance, identifying and resolving technical issues, and supporting system upgrades to improve performance and reliability. You will also play an important role in maintaining safety standards and helping implement best practices while working in a variety of field conditions.

This position is ideal for a technician who brings strong technical skills, attention to detail, and flexibility, along with the ability to work independently while representing Interstate Power Systems in a professional manner with customers.

If this describes you, Interstate Power Systems is eager for you to apply today and join our expanding team in one of these Nebraska or Iowa locations!

Interstate Power Systems is a proud distributor for Volvo Penta, Detroit Diesel Engines, Allison Transmissions, Deutz Engines, and Generators.

Interstate Companies, Inc. is a dynamic organization providing rewarding careers for more than 1,700 employees across its corporate office and five operating units: Interstate Assembly Systems, Interstate Bearing Systems, Interstate Energy Systems, Interstate Power Systems, and I-State Truck Center. Interstate is also a leader in Heavy Diesel Construction Equipment, Off-Highway Equipment, and Agriculture Equipment.

At Interstate, we take personal pride in our work and customer relationships, that's why we deliver Pride in Service in every interaction, every single day!

  • Troubleshoot, maintain, and repair all makers of generators.
  • Demonstrate basic-level knowledge of and/or experience with power generation products.
  • Complete preventative maintenance and repairs on generators or components at customer sites with minimal supervision.
  • Diagnose, repair, adjust, and modify components of the generator, engine, and switchgear.

  • Meet certification requirements.
  • Perform administrative duties related to the role.

title: JNTC Exercise Designer (MAWTS-1)
description:
JNTC Exercise Designer (MAWTS-1)


Location: Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Yuma, Arizona
Employment Type: Full-Time
Work Arrangement: On-Site
Annual Salary Range: $105,000 to $110,000
Security Clearance: Active Secret Required

Application Instructions

All interested candidates should apply directly through Green Cell Consulting's official career page to be considered for this position.

Apply at:

Please locate the JNTC Exercise Designer (MAWTS-1) position and complete the online application process.

Applicants with military experience are encouraged to submit a resume that accurately reflects their military duties, responsibilities, qualifications, and accomplishments. Do not civilianize your military resume. Retain your military rank, occupational specialty (MOS), duty titles, unit assignments, and relevant military terminology. This information allows Green Cell Consulting to properly evaluate your experience and qualifications against the position requirements.

Position Overview

Green Cell Consulting (GCC) is seeking a qualified MAWTS-1 JNTC Exercise Designer to support Marine Aviation Weapons and Tactics Squadron One (MAWTS-1) at MCAS Yuma, Arizona.

This position supports the Joint National Training Capability (JNTC) accredited program, including the Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) Course and associated joint training exercises.

The Exercise Designer is responsible for planning, coordinating, and integrating joint military capabilities into MAWTS-1 training events. The successful candidate will work closely with Marine Corps personnel, other military services, government organizations, and exercise participants to ensure training objectives and JNTC requirements are effectively supported.

We are seeking a professional with a strong understanding of military operations, excellent communication skills, and the ability to independently coordinate complex exercise requirements in a dynamic operational environment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Exercise Planning and Integration

  • Develop, coordinate, and manage joint integration plans and supporting requirements for MAWTS-1 JNTC-accredited training events.

  • Identify and coordinate joint enablers, participating organizations, and tactical and operational capabilities throughout the exercise planning and execution cycle.

  • Coordinate joint, other-Service, and interagency participation to support established training objectives.

  • Manage exercise integration activities and adjust participating support as necessary within approved program requirements.

Funding and Resource Coordination

  • Prepare, submit, and track JNTC funding requirements, supporting documentation, and exercise-related funding actions.

  • Develop funding justifications and budget recommendations for submission to the TECOM JNTC section.

  • Identify changes to funding requirements and coordinate requested adjustments through appropriate channels.

JNTC Accreditation and Assessment

  • Coordinate JNTC accreditation, certification, and mitigation activities with appropriate government and civilian personnel.

  • Support JNTC assessments, including the collection and analysis of exercise data.

  • Assist with pre-event and post-event assessments and preparation of Service Lessons Learned documentation.

  • Develop, update, and report other-Service and interagency exercise requirements.

Program Coordination and Reporting

  • Coordinate classified network access requirements and maintain necessary system access.

  • Provide weekly activity reports to the JNTC Contract Project Manager documenting accomplishments, upcoming events, coordination activities, funding requirements, and potential program risks.

  • Perform other related duties consistent with the position and applicable contract requirements.

Required Qualifications

  • Relevant experience in military operations, joint training, exercise planning, operational planning, or a related field.

  • Must possess a military aviation pilot or Weapons Systems Officer (WTI) background, or a military aviation Command and Control background.

  • Experience coordinating requirements, resources, and supporting organizations in a military or government environment.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop, coordinate, and manage exercise plans and supporting requirements.

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

  • Effective written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to coordinate effectively with military, government, and civilian stakeholders.

  • Proficiency with common office software and information management systems.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and meet established deadlines.

  • Must be eligible or have an active clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Marine Corps aviation operations, joint operations, military training, or exercise planning.

  • Familiarity with MAWTS-1, the Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) Course, JNTC, or the Joint Training, Exercise, and Evaluation Program (JTEEP).

  • Bachelor's degree or relevant professional military education.

Compensation

The anticipated annual salary range for this position is $105,000 to $110,000.

Compensation within the advertised range will be determined based on relevant experience, qualifications, and job-related skills.

Additional Position Requirements

  • This position requires on-site work at MCAS Yuma, Arizona.

  • Travel may be required to support JNTC-accredited exercises, planning conferences, coordination meetings, and other contract-related activities.

  • Local travel during the workday may be required, including the use of a personal vehicle.

  • The position involves extended periods of computer-based work, sustained attention, and occasional lifting of materials weighing up to 15 pounds.

  • Qualified individuals must be able to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Must comply with applicable contract security requirements, installation access procedures, and company policies.

Why Join Green Cell Consulting?

Green Cell Consulting is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) committed to supporting military readiness, operational excellence, and mission success.

Our team consists of experienced military veterans and civilian professionals who understand the importance of delivering quality support to the warfighter.

Our company is guided by three core values:

Trust. Service. Value.

At GCC, you will have the opportunity to apply your military and operational experience in a mission-focused environment while directly contributing to the training and readiness of Marine Corps aviation forces.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Reasonable accommodations are available to qualified applicants and employees in accordance with applicable law.

title: Internship - Audio data collection and acoustic measurement
description:
We are seeking an intern interested in audio data collection, acoustic measurement, and immersive audio systems. The intern will collaborate with MERL researchers to design and conduct acoustic measurement experiments, record room impulse responses, configure multichannel audio recording and playback systems, and develop tools for data acquisition and analysis. Projects may involve microphone and loudspeaker arrays, spatial audio recording and reproduction, Dante audio networking, and the development of automated measurement and data collection workflows. The collected datasets will support ongoing research in spatial audio processing, room acoustics, and machine learning.

The ideal candidate is an undergraduate or graduate student with experience in some of the following: audio signal processing, acoustic measurements, impulse response measurement techniques, microphone and loudspeaker arrays, multichannel audio systems, Dante audio networking, and immersive audio technologies. Hands-on experience with audio recording equipment and experimental setups is particularly desirable.

Flexible start dates, durations (typically 3–6 months), and full-time or part-time arrangements are available.

The pay range for this internship position will be 4-8K per month.

title: Youth Ministry Director at Fort Benning, Georgia
description:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

title: Fiber Engineer II
description:
Fiber Engineer II

About the Job

Cityside Fiber is seeking an experienced Fiber Engineer II to join our OSP team. This role is responsible for leading complex fiber optic network projects, mentoring junior engineers, optimizing network performance, and solving technical challenges. Fiber Engineer II plays a key part in expanding reliable connectivity to our communities while maintaining the highest standards of quality and safety. Success in this position requires strong technical expertise, leadership ability, project management skills, and the capacity to work independently on complex problems in a fast-paced environment.

Responsibilities

  • Lead design and planning of complex fiber optic network installations, including route optimization, capacity planning, and resource allocation
  • Oversee and coordinate fiber deployment projects from initial planning through completion and testing
  • Mentor and train junior Fiber Engineers, providing technical guidance and performance feedback
  • Work with splicers and NOC on advanced fiber optic installation, splicing, testing, and termination in accordance with industry standards and company specifications
  • Identify root causes of network issues and develop solutions to minimize service disruptions and improve network reliability
  • Maintain detailed technical documentation of network designs, installations, testing results, testing protocols, and maintenance activities
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams including construction, operations, and network engineering to coordinate successful fiber deployments
  • Perform network performance analysis and recommend upgrades or optimization strategies
  • Ensure compliance with all safety protocols, industry regulations, and company policies regarding fiber installation and network access
  • Conduct field surveys along public right-of-way and utility easements to validate viable, cost-effective network routes — including aerial attachment assessment, clearance checks, pole inspection, and substructure condition review
  • Document field findings through photographs, hand sketches, and field notes to support accurate engineering design and smooth construction handoff
  • Apply value engineering judgment in the field, considering construction impact, installation efficiency, and long-term maintenance when identifying routes and facility placement
  • Participate in technical training and stay current with emerging fiber optic technologies and industry standards
  • Contribute to a culture of trust, integrity, and collaboration
  • Understand and uphold Cityside Fiber's core purpose and values and be passionate about what we do

This job description is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications associated with the position. Management reserves the right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities as business needs evolve.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent; Associate degree in telecommunications, fiber engineering, or related field required
  • 5+ years of experience in fiber optic installation, network engineering, or related telecommunications field
  • 2+ years in a leadership or mentoring role within a technical environment
  • Advanced technical knowledge of fiber optic systems, splicing techniques, network architecture, and testing methodologies
  • Experience with OSP field data collection, including aerial and underground infrastructure assessment, pole classification, and make-ready evaluation
  • Proficiency with network design software and tools (AutoCAD, optical modeling software, or equivalent)
  • Strong project management and organizational skills with ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with ability to mentor and lead technical teams
  • Demonstrated problem-solving ability and technical troubleshooting expertise
  • Valid driver's license with acceptable driving record
  • Ability to work outdoors in various weather conditions and travel to field sites as needed
  • Willingness to work on-call for emergency network repairs and critical issues
  • Physical ability to climb ladders, work at heights, and lift to 25 lbs. occasionally
  • Industry certifications such as CFOT, CFNT, or equivalent strongly preferred

About Cityside Fiber

Cityside Fiber is on a mission to deliver high-quality, reliable internet to communities through innovation and a people-first approach. Headquartered in Irvine, CA, we are an emerging telecommunications provider expanding rapidly due to high demand. Our culture is built on innovation, accountability, and trust, and we seek independent thinkers who want to contribute to something big.

Location

Headquarters in Irvine, CA. [May require travel depending on role.]

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive salary: $90,000 annually (dependent on experience) (exempt)
  • Company-sponsored medical & dental for employees (Subsidized for dependents)
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid Time Off (PTO), sick leave, and holidays
  • Growth opportunities & career development programs

Why Cityside Fiber?

Cityside Fiber believes that we all deserve amazing internet! Our core purpose is to create networks that better enable life-changing connectivity in our communities by daring to be different and having our team members put people first all while having fun. We’re building a next-generation internet provider with a focus on innovation, accountability, and trust. At Cityside Fiber, you’ll work with a passionate team, have room for growth, and make a real impact.

How to Apply

For immediate consideration, submit your resume through our careers site. No phone inquiries, please.

Visit our website at www.citysidefiber.com

Cityside Fiber is an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to diversity and inclusion.

title: Director of Pharmacy
description:
CompleteRx is seeking a results-driven and visionary Director of Pharmacy to lead pharmacy operations at Tallahassee Memorial Healthcare, a 772-bed located in Tallahassee, FL. This leadership role oversees six direct reports and a team of 100+ pharmacy employees, including full-time, part-time, and PRN staff.

Sign on Bonus: $10,000

Location: Tallahassee, Florida

The Director of Pharmacy provides leadership and strategic direction at our partnered hospital while having the support and expertise of CompleteRx’s operations team as a resource. Your positive leadership and innovation will enable the hospital to provide the best services to the local communities.

Hospital Overview:

Founded in 1948, Tallahassee Memorial HealthCare (TMH) is a private, nonprofit healthcare system serving North Florida and South Georgia. At the center of the system is a 772-bed acute care hospital providing advanced and specialized services, including the region’s only Level II Trauma Center, Primary Stroke Center, Level III Neonatal Intensive Care Unit and Pediatric Intensive Care Unit. TMH also provides comprehensive cancer care through its Cancer Center and includes a psychiatric hospital, multiple specialty care centers, residency programs and more than 50 affiliated physician practices.

Why Join CompleteRx?

At CompleteRx, we believe healthcare should be about serving others. That's why our mission is to deliver better care and better service, through innovation. The goal of our exceptional teams is to perform like champions. This means we are committed to being the best at delivering quality care to the patients we serve. Each team member's dedication is essential to meeting and exceeding the needs of our patients and families.

What You Will Do

Evaluates operations on an ongoing basis to ensure safe, appropriate, cost-effective care delivery

  • Develops, enforces, and maintains policies and procedures that promote cost-effective, appropriate, and safe drug use.
  • Evaluates operations on an ongoing basis using principles of continuous process improvement.
  • Develops, implements, checks, and retools action plans to address variances and improve efficiency.
  • Participates in select Hospital committees.
  • Leads the Antibiotic Stewardship Committee in conjunction with the Hospital's Infection Control leader.
  • Develops and maintains a medical-staff-approved formulary.
  • Supervises drug storage and preparation areas throughout the hospital.
  • Provides for the educational needs of healthcare professionals and patients and their families.
  • Ensures maintenance of an adequate drug supply. Ensures the integrity of the drug supply. Establishes specifications for the procurement of drugs, chemicals, and biologicals.
  • Ensures strict control and accountability for drugs dispensed to patients or distributed to floor stock.
  • Assures adequate control and documentation of controlled substances.
  • Maintains a quality improvement plan for the department
  • Ensures the pharmacy is in compliance with all federal, state, and other regulatory agency laws and standards.

Supervises, trains, mentors, and evaluates staff.

  • Supervises pharmacy personnel.
  • Recruits, promotes, disciplines, and terminates pharmacy staff.
  • Develops job descriptions, performance standards, and performance goals.
  • Evaluates and counsels staff on their performance.
  • Prepares work schedules and monitors workload statistics. Maintains an appropriate staffing level.
  • Provides for the educational needs of the pharmacy staff.
  • Acts as a positive role model, mentor, and preceptor.
  • Promotes individual professional growth.
  • Communicates with staff and promotes staff ownership in problem-solving and participation in operational decision-making.

Prepares annual budget, controls and reduces costs, forecasts operational needs, and reviews expenditures to ensure budget limits are not exceeded.

  • Prepares a pharmacy budget annually.
  • Reviews monthly financial statistics and plans expenditures within budget guidelines.
  • Monitors and justifies all expenses exceeding budgeted targets.
  • Administers reports, documents, payroll records, employee surveys, and other required data.
  • Ensures preparation and submission of patient charges and financial reports to administration in accordance with hospital policy.
  • Ensures applicable training records, current licensures, and other records required required to document compliance are maintained in secure department files.
  • Ensures compliance with hospital policies and procedures that apply to pharmacy services.
  • Ensures compliance with all applicable Federal, State, and local laws, rules, and regulations.

Establishes the scope of services and develops annual implementation plans which contribute to the organizational strategic objectives.

  • Develop and implement a strategic plan for the pharmacy that supports the mission and goals of the organization.
  • Develop and implement pharmacy services in collaboration with associated department services.
  • Develop, implement, and maintain a program that improves the quality of pharmacy services and supports the quality improvement plan of the organization.
  • Participate in all committees/functions required by the organization including the Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee.
  • Establish productive collaborative relationships with physicians, nursing, administration, and other hospital staff.
  • Meet customers' needs and expectations.

What You Will Need

  • Bachelor of Science or PharmD degree required.
  • Current Florida pharmacist license in good standing, or obtain a license prior to your date of hire.
  • Current Florida consultant pharmacist license in good standing, or obtain a license prior to your date of hire.
  • 3 years of inpatient hospital pharmacy management experience.
  • 3-5 years of inpatient hospital pharmacy experience is required.

Compensation & Benefits:

As an employee of CompleteRx, your commitment to learning will be encouraged and supported through ongoing training and professional development. We nurture a collaborative, high-performance culture and offer a challenging career along with a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Medical, dental, and vision
  • Flexible Spending Account or Health Savings Account
  • Vacation and sick time
  • Continuing education: Eligible employees have access to a full complement of continuing-education courses as well as a wide variety of career development opportunities.
  • 401(k) plans: CompleteRx offers a 401(k) plan with a company match.
  • License Reimbursement
  • Short and Long-Term Disability

Company Description:

Founded in 1998 as a service-driven organization with a strong sense of community, CompleteRx embarked on a strategy to become the employer of choice in hospital pharmacy management and consulting. Since our founding, we believe our success has been driven by our employees who are our most valuable resources. We believe the very best outcomes are accomplished when all employees share a sense of mutual ownership for successful results and where each employee accepts personal accountability for their individual contributions. These beliefs are the core of our Team Covenant which guides all of our actions to the patients we care for, hospitals we support, and fellow employees we work alongside.

CompleteRx is an Equal Opportunity Employer by choice.

Restore Educational/Vocational Specialist works as a member of an interdisciplinary team to provide educational, vocational, workforce development, and life-skills support to young adults ages 16–25 who have been identified as being at high risk of engaging in serious violence. The Educational/Vocational Specialist will work closely with Case Managers, the Program Director, community partners, employers, workforce providers, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to help participants identify and achieve short- and long-term educational and career goals. The Specialist will help participants reconnect to education, secure employment and internship opportunities, develop job-readiness skills, explore career pathways, obtain credentials, and build the skills and professional relationships needed for long-term self-sufficiency.

The Specialist will contribute to developing and implementing each participant’s Sustainable Growth Plan, ensuring educational and vocational goals connect to the participant’s interests, strengths, needs, and long-term aspirations.

Grounded in Good Shepherd Services’ trauma-informed and strength-based approach, the Educational/Vocational Specialist will support participants in developing protective factors, increasing stability, strengthening positive relationships, and building pathways toward education, employment, and healthy adulthood. title: Youth Ministry Director at Fort Bragg, North Carolina
description:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.

  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

title: Internship - Vision-Language-Action (VLA) Models for Robotic Manipulation
description:
MERL is seeking a highly motivated Ph.D. student to conduct research on Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotic manipulation. Recent VLA models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in general-purpose robotic manipulation. This internship will investigate new methods for improving the reliability and effectiveness of VLA policies in real-world manipulation tasks. Potential research directions include exploring VLA-based approaches, multi-arm coordination, and adaptive behaviors for industrial manipulation tasks, with particular emphasis on reliability assessment, policy intervention, and corrective-action strategies.

The selected intern will work closely with MERL researchers to develop and implement novel algorithms, deploy and evaluate learning-based policies on robotic platforms, and conduct both simulation and real-world experiments. The intern will also disseminate research findings at leading robotics conferences, including ICRA, RSS, CoRL, and IROS. The internship start date and duration are flexible. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply with an updated CV and a list of relevant publications.

Required Specific Experience

  • Current enrollment in a Ph.D. program
  • Strong background in robot learning for manipulation
  • Hands-on experience with Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models for robotics, such as pi0, OpenVLA, Octo, GR00T N1, or related state-of-the-art models
  • Proficiency with ROS, Python, and deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch
  • Experience with robotic simulation environments and sim-to-real transfer
  • Experience deploying and evaluating learning-based policies on physical robotic platforms
  • A strong publication record or demonstrated research potential

The pay range for this internship position will be 6-8K per month.

Remote within the United States; shifts within 6:30 am-12:30 am ET Monday-Friday and Saturday; Sunday deployment testing as scheduled.

  • Maintain supporting documentation and accurate change records, follow current SOPs, recommend process improvements, and provide backup support for Purchasing data activities as assigned.

  • Associate degree or relevant coursework in business, supply chain, information systems, or a related field, preferred.
  • Two or more years of experience in purchasing support, inventory administration, ERP data maintenance, part setup, or a related administrative role, preferred.
  • Experience creating, maintaining, or reviewing records in an ERP system; Epicor experience strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with part numbers, supplier records, manufacturer information, units of measure,

Why CSI

  • Collaborative team environment focused on continuous improvement

Benefits & Perks

title: Parts Counter Representative
description:
Job Title: Parts Counter Representative
Location: Sioux Falls South Dakota
Company: Interstate Power Systems

We are seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Parts Counter Representative to join our team in Sioux Falls South Dakota. The Parts Counter Representative will be responsible for assisting customers, managing parts inventory, and providing exceptional service to support our clients’ needs in the diesel truck and equipment industry. The ideal candidate will have strong communication skills, a passion for customer service, and knowledge of heavy-duty vehicle parts.

As a Parts Counter Representative, you will play a crucial role in assisting customers and technicians with their heavy-duty truck and or off-highway equipment parts needs. You will be responsible for providing exceptional customer service, identifying, and locating the correct parts, processing transactions accurately, and maintaining inventory levels. The ideal candidate will possess excellent communication skills, a strong attention to detail, and a passion for delivering top-notch service to our valued customers.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Customer Service: Greet and assist customers (in-person, over the phone, and via email) with parts inquiries, identifying their needs, and recommending appropriate parts and accessories for heavy-duty diesel trucks and equipment.
  • Parts Lookup and Sales: Utilize parts catalogs, digital systems, and inventory databases to locate and provide accurate parts information, process sales, and issue invoices.
  • Inventory Management: Assist with inventory control, including receiving, stocking, and organizing parts, ensuring accurate stock levels, and conducting periodic inventory counts.
  • Order Processing: Place special orders for non-stocked items, coordinate with suppliers, and communicate delivery timelines to customers.
  • Technical Support: Provide basic technical guidance to customers regarding parts compatibility and installation, collaborating with service technicians as needed.
  • Documentation: Maintain accurate records of sales, returns, and inventory transactions, ensuring compliance with company policies and procedures.
  • Team Collaboration: Work closely with service and sales teams to ensure seamless operations and customer satisfaction.
  • Shop Maintenance: Keep the parts counter and surrounding area clean, organized, and presentable.

Qualifications:

  • Education: High school diploma or equivalent; additional training or certification in automotive or diesel technology is a plus.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a parts department, automotive, or heavy-duty equipment industry preferred but not required.
  • Skills:
    • Strong customer service and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport with clients.
    • Basic knowledge of heavy-duty diesel truck and equipment parts or willingness to learn.
    • Proficiency with computers, including inventory management software and parts lookup systems.
    • Ability to multitask and work in a fast-paced environment.
    • Detail-oriented with strong organizational skills.
  • Physical Requirements: Ability to lift to 50 pounds, stand for extended periods, and occasionally work in a warehouse environment.
  • Other Requirements: Valid driver’s license preferred; must be able to pass a background check.

Work Environment:

  • The position is based in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, at our heavy-duty diesel truck and equipment shop.
  • Work hours may include occasional weekends and rotating after-hours shifts as required.
  • The role involves interaction with customers, technicians, and vendors in a dynamic shop environment.

Employee Benefits:

  • Competitive Wages – Be paid your worth!
  • Tuition assistance - for educational and ongoing career growth
  • Health, dental and vision coverage - begins on the first day of the following month.
  • Paid Time Off - (PTO) starts accruing day one of your full-time employment.
  • Holidays - 6 Holidays and 2 Floating Holidays per year
  • 401(K) - with company matching.
  • Long Term Disability - Supplied
  • Short Term Disability - Supplied
  • Life Insurance - Supplied

  • PPE Reimbursement- Safety Glasses and Safety Boot Reimbursement
  • Pet Insurance – We care about our furry friends!
  • Employee Discounts - available on products and services
  • Paid Employee Assistance Program - Free 24/7 Access to a guidance consultant regarding life challenges you or family member may face.
  • Paid Health and Well-being screening - for employees and their spouse

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Interstate Companies is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and we encourage all qualified and interested persons to apply for this position by submitting a resume for consideration.
