title: Senior Software Engineer, AI-Augmented Development
description:
At ACT, Your Work Makes a Difference

Education has power – a power that changes lives forever. It creates opportunities that lift up individuals, their families, and sparks societal change that echoes through generations to come. From our grassroots we have fought the good fight for inclusivity in education, and we remain devoted to helping anyone who struggles to access that power. This is what matters to us and we must do better -- we’ve never been more sure of our purpose.

ACT team members are part of an organization dedicated to a mission that has never been more important: Helping people achieve education and workplace success. Advancing that mission within our organization, by helping our team members achieve education and workplace success of their own, is core to our values. ACT values a diverse workplace and is committed to fostering an inclusive environment in which every team member has an equal opportunity to grow.

We want our team members to have the well-being and confidence they need to do their best work, in an environment where both they and ACT thrive. To support this, our total rewards include company paid life insurance, medical, dental, vision, flexible health and dependent spending accounts, 401(k) retirement savings with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and so much more. You can find a comprehensive list of our benefits here.

We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer, to help us fulfill that mission.

The Senior Software Engineer applies advanced knowledge, skill, and expertise to software delivery. Work is both independent and collaborative in nature. This role emphasizes using AI coding tools to develop software efficiently, while owning the judgment calls AI can't make, including reviewing, testing, and correcting AI-generated work, and taking end-to-end ownership of delivery from specification through production. Beyond using AI tools well, this role is expected to actively drive how the team adopts new AI-assisted development practices by piloting new tools and techniques, and championing what actually works. This is primarily a hands-on senior engineering role within the team, with the opportunity to grow into a cross-team responsibility for advancing how the broader engineering organization uses AI-assisted development tools as the role matures.

The finalist will be hired at the salary and level commensurate with their qualifications. For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary between $110,000 and $135,000. ACT manages salaries within this range based on relevant factors, including skills, experience, and internal equity. This position is not incentive eligible.

Location: This is a remote position, based in the United States.

Visa: Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship.

What you will be working on:

  • Technical Leadership & Complex Problem-Solving
    • Solve complex technical problems across the team's core systems, using AI-assisted approaches to move faster, including integrations with related platforms.
    • Contribute senior-level technical judgment to active modernization initiatives within the team, using AI tools to accelerate legacy-to-modern platform migrations.
  • AI Tooling Strategy & Adoption
    • Pilot new AI-assisted development tools, models, and techniques within the team (e.g., new agentic coding workflows, MCP integrations, updated model versions), evaluating them against real delivery work rather than vendor claims.
    • Propose and champion new use cases for AI in the team's engineering practice, backed by a measured before/after comparison — time saved, defect rate, or review burden.
    • Feed adoption learnings back into team practice, updating norms, playbooks, or tooling recommendations as new approaches prove out (or don't).
  • Deep Domain Knowledge
    • Apply deep familiarity with the team's platform architecture, history, and constraints to guide technical decisions, including where AI-assisted approaches can speed modernization work.
  • AI-Directed Development & Delivery Ownership
    • Direct AI coding tools and agents to implement features from specs, tickets, or requirements, and own end-to-end delivery of the feature from specification through production.
    • Review, test, and correct AI-generated code for correctness, security, and architectural fit; catch both subtle errors (a plausible-but-wrong calculation, an approach that won't scale) and obvious ones.
    • Act as a steward against AI-specific security and supply-chain risk, scrutinizing AI-suggested dependencies, flagging unfamiliar or unverified packages before they're accepted, and treating AI-generated code that touches auth, data access, or external integrations with elevated review.
    • Write specs detailed enough for an AI tool to implement correctly on the first or second pass; for ambiguous problems, exercise judgment on whether to escalate or proceed independently.
    • Maintain and extend the team's eval and guardrail practices that catch AI-introduced regressions before they reach production.
  • Analysis, Recommendations & Autonomy
    • Independently evaluate where AI-assisted development tools, primarily Claude Code, alongside comparable tools as needed, add genuine value, for example, scaffolding and legacy code comprehension, while applying extra human scrutiny to auth-adjacent or compliance-sensitive logic.
    • Recommend and refine engineering practices with a high degree of autonomy, guided by high-level direction and using independent judgment to accomplish goals.
  • Acts as a Resource for Colleagues
    • Proactively share and teach AI-assisted development practices with the team (code review norms, prompt approaches, and verification habits for AI-generated output)with the opportunity to extend this to other engineering teams as the role grows.
    • Operate as an individual-contributor role, building credibility and driving adoption of good practice through technical expertise and collaboration.
  • Program & Initiative Leadership (Growth Path)
    • As the role matures, lead or contribute to a cross-team initiative establishing shared, practical standards for responsible AI tool usage in engineering, including guidance on what's safe to share with external AI tools, and when AI-generated code warrants elevated review.
    • Participate in the engineering support rotation per the team's standard model.

Role Progression:

The following outlines key milestones and expectations for the first year in this role.

3-Month Mark

  • Completed onboarding on the team's platform architecture and AI tooling conventions; has shipped a few small features or fixes through AI-directed development, with work reviewed and merged at the team's normal quality bar.
  • Is closely working with other team members to understand production issues and system configurations, and has demonstrated at least one concrete instance of catching an AI-generated error or gap before it shipped.

6-Month Mark

  • Owns a feature or workstream end-to-end — writing the spec, directing AI-assisted implementation, and handling review and testing — with minimal day-to-day oversight from the lead.
  • Has contributed a concrete improvement to the team's AI-assisted development practice (a new guardrail, a refined spec template, a prompt pattern) that at least one other engineer has adopted.
  • Demonstrates a working understanding of the end-to-end architecture of the platforms they support, including how those platforms integrate with other systems across the broader technology ecosystem, and the underlying infrastructure architecture beneath them.

12-Month Mark

  • Has led a modernization effort or comparable initiative to completion, with AI-directed development visibly accelerating delivery versus a traditional approach.
  • Is beginning to extend influence beyond the team, if the opportunity has arisen — through early contributions to the cross-team AI standards initiative, informal mentoring, or a guardrail others have started using.

This could be the job for you if you have (minimum requirements):

  • Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible software engineering experience.
  • Engineering Fundamentals
    • Object-oriented and/or functional programming fundamentals.
    • Data modeling and query performance reasoning, across relational and/or schema-driven data layers.
    • API design fundamentals: contracts, versioning, and backward compatibility, whether REST or schema-first (e.g., GraphQL).
    • Security fundamentals: authentication/authorization flows, common injection classes, and dependency risk.
    • Distributed systems fundamentals: failure modes, statelessness, and behavior under concurrent load.
  • Representative Technologies
    • A backend language/runtime, such as Node.js (NestJS), Java, or a comparable OOP/functional stack.
    • An API paradigm, such as GraphQL or REST, including schema design and versioning.
    • A modern frontend framework, such as React or a comparable component-based framework.
    • A relational database, such as PostgreSQL, or a comparable RDBMS.
    • Cloud/container infrastructure, such as AWS and Kubernetes, or comparable cloud-native infrastructure.
    • Claude Code, or a comparable AI-assisted coding tool, used in production.
  • Demonstrated, hands-on production use of Claude Code or a comparable AI-assisted coding tool — candidates should be able to describe specific instances where these tools materially changed their approach to a problem.
  • Track record of piloting a new AI-assisted development tool or technique and measuring its actual impact (time saved, defect rate change, or review burden) rather than just using it because it's available.
  • Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate AI-generated code before accepting it, with a specific example of catching an AI-generated error before it shipped.
  • Working knowledge of AI-specific security risk, e.g., unverified or malicious dependencies suggested by AI tools, injected logic in auto-accepted code; and habits for catching it before it reaches production.
  • Strong engineering fundamentals (programming, data modeling, API design, security, and distributed systems) that hold up independent of AI tooling; treats AI tools as an amplifier of skill.
  • Demonstrated ability to work from ambiguous specs, with sound judgment for when to escalate and when to proceed independently.
  • Experience working (or ability to work) across a mixed legacy and modern technology stack.
  • Experience owning delivery end to end, from specification through production, including writing specs clear enough for an AI tool to implement correctly.
  • Bachelor's degree in computer or data science, software engineering, artificial intelligence, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge and abilities can be acquired.

It’s a plus if you have:

  • Demonstrated ability to influence engineering practices and colleagues outside of a direct reporting relationship, or interest in growing into this scope.
  • Experience evaluating or comparing multiple AI coding tools or models for team fit.
  • Familiarity with test administration or assessment delivery systems, or a comparable domain is valued as a plus alongside strong engineering fundamentals and AI-directed development skill.
  • Experience mentoring or setting technical standards across multiple teams.
  • Background in education technology or a similarly regulated, integration-heavy domain.
  • Experience building or extending eval or guardrail frameworks for AI-generated code.

About ACT

When ACT was founded in 1959, it disrupted the assessment industry with a new approach to helping students better understand their readiness so they could take steps to improve it. By leveraging our expertise and authority in assessment and research, we will again disrupt the industry—helping more people learn, better measure their progress, and improve their navigation through life’s transitions.

More than ever before, ACT is fulfilling its mission of helping people achieve education and workplace success. We’re doing it by pushing the boundaries of learning innovation through the work of our people, who we call team members because we’re all in this together.

We know transformation does not come without challenge. That’s why ACT invests in a variety of experiences for team members to strengthen their connections, explore ideas, learn from customers, and celebrate success.

Learn more about working at ACT at act.org!

ACT is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. ACT participates in E-verify. ACT's online position announcements are intended only to provide general descriptions of employment opportunities; none of the information provided for any position should be interpreted as a commitment by ACT to specific terms and conditions for employment.

Completion of the ACT National Career Readiness Certificate is recommended. Find a testing site near you to register for the WorkKeys assessments. Finalists for this position will be subject to a criminal background check as a condition of employment.

Instead, reach out to us at careers@act.org with the details. title: Service Desk Technician I
description:
Are you passionate about technology and helping clients solve problems? AbeTech is looking for a Service Desk Technician I to join our Managed Services team and serve as the first point of contact for our clients' technical support needs.

In this role, you'll provide front-line technical support, troubleshoot hardware and software issues, and help keep our clients' operations running smoothly. You'll manage support tickets from intake through resolution, assist with device and printer support, provide software assistance, maintain accurate documentation, and deliver exceptional client service throughout the support process.


As a Service Desk Technician I, you'll play a key role in maintaining client production environments by resolving routine technical issues, gathering and documenting critical information, communicating effectively with clients, and escalating more complex issues when needed. Success in this role requires strong problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and a commitment to providing responsive, professional support that meets service level expectations.


Deliver Exceptional Client Support

  • Serve as the first point of contact for client support requests via phone, email, and ticketing systems.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve common issues involving mobile computers, barcode scanners, vehicle-mounted computers, printers, labeling software, and mobile device management (MDM) platforms.
  • Provide timely updates and maintain clear communication throughout the support process.
  • Take ownership of support requests and drive issues to resolution.

Manage and Prioritize Support Requests

  • Review incoming tickets and gather the information needed to diagnose issues effectively.
  • Determine the appropriate support path and escalate issues when additional technical expertise is required.
  • Monitor ticket queues to ensure service levels and response expectations are met.
  • Accurately document troubleshooting steps, updates, and resolutions.

Support Device Deployments and Evaluations

  • Assist with device preparation, staging, configuration, and deployment activities.
  • Perform basic device evaluations, including connectivity, scanning, touchscreen, and hardware functionality testing.
  • Support repair and replacement processes as needed.

Contribute to Team Success

  • Collaborate with Tier II technicians by providing detailed troubleshooting information and documentation.
  • Participate in ongoing process improvements and knowledge-sharing initiatives.
  • Continue developing technical skills through training and hands-on learning opportunities.

title: First-Line Supervisor of Production and Operating Workers
description:
First-Line Supervisor of Production and Operating Workers

Position Availability: This position is contingent upon contract award. Hiring is anticipated to begin upon contract award.

Location: St. Inigoes, MD – NAWCAD Webster Outlying Field (WOLF)
Shift: Day Shift, Monday–Friday
Remote Type: No Remote

Certification: Not specified
Education: Bachelor’s degree in an engineering, technical, or business discipline, or qualifying substitution
Years of Experience: Minimum 3 years, including at least 2 years of production facility management experience

Description

Altus Technology Solutions is seeking a First-Line Supervisor of Production and Operating Workers to support production and fabrication operations at Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD) Webster Outlying Field (WOLF).

This position is responsible for directly supervising and coordinating production workers and fabricators, managing incoming work, coordinating personnel and equipment, and ensuring production activities are completed safely, efficiently, and according to established schedules and requirements.

The Supervisor will work closely with production, engineering, logistics, and management personnel to ensure materials, equipment, personnel, and schedules are properly coordinated to support mission requirements.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Directly supervise and coordinate the daily activities of production workers and fabricators.
  • Manage incoming work schedules and allocate personnel, equipment, and other resources to support successful completion of assigned work.
  • Plan, prepare, issue, and control production schedules.
  • Coordinate the flow of materials to meet production requirements and established schedules.
  • Coordinate personnel and equipment schedules with material procurements and availability.
  • Identify material shortages, resource constraints, and potential impacts to production schedules.
  • Monitor work in progress and communicate production status to management.
  • Identify potential production problems and assist in developing solutions.
  • Coordinate with engineering, logistics, procurement, and other functional teams to resolve production issues.
  • Ensure personnel follow established production procedures, safety requirements, quality standards, and applicable technical requirements.
  • Support the efficient use of production equipment, tools, materials, and personnel.
  • Review work requirements and ensure resources are available to meet established schedules.
  • Maintain accurate production records, schedules, and status information.
  • Provide recommendations to management regarding production resources, scheduling, staffing, and potential process improvements.
  • Support continuous improvement of production processes and procedures.

Qualifications

  • Active DoD Secret clearance or the ability to meet applicable clearance requirements.
  • Bachelor’s degree in an engineering, technical, or business discipline, or a qualifying substitution.
  • Minimum of 3 years of relevant experience, with at least 2 years of experience in production facility management.
  • Experience supervising production personnel, fabricators, technicians, or similar manufacturing/production employees.
  • Experience coordinating personnel, equipment, materials, and production schedules.
  • Ability to identify and resolve production scheduling, material, staffing, and resource issues.
  • Ability to read and understand technical documentation, work requirements, and production schedules.
  • Strong organizational and communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with engineering, production, logistics, and management personnel.
  • Ability to work onsite in a production environment and support mission requirements.
  • Must be able to comply with applicable DoD security, safety, quality, and operational requirements.

  • Microsoft Power BI Data Analyst (PL-300) or Tableau certification
  • ITIL 4 Foundation
  • ServiceNow Performance Analytics training

OTHER PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Federal or VA reporting experience
  • Experience presenting findings to program leadership

Remote within the United States; core hours Eastern.

title: Pipeline Operator - Journey
description:
Headquartered in Houston, Texas, Summit Midstream Corporation (NYSE: SMC) is a value-driven corporation focused on developing, owning and operating midstream energy infrastructure assets that are strategically located in unconventional resource basins, primarily shale formations, in the continental United States.

We currently operate natural gas, crude oil and produced water gathering systems in four unconventional resource basins:

  • the Williston Basin in North Dakota, which includes the Bakken and Three Forks shale formations;
  • the Denver-Julesburg Basin, which includes the Niobrara and Codell shale formations in Colorado and Wyoming;
  • the Fort Worth Basin in Texas, which includes the Barnett Shale formation; and
  • the Piceance Basin in Colorado, which includes the liquids-rich Mesaverde formation as well as the emerging Mancos and Niobrara Shale formations.

Our systems and the basins they serve are as follows:

  • the Polar & Divide system, which serves the Williston Basin;
  • the DFW Midstream system, which serves the Fort Worth Basin;
  • the Grand River system, which serves the Piceance Basin; and
  • the Niobrara G&P system, which serves the DJ Basin.

SMC has an equity investment in and operates Double E Pipeline, LLC, which is natural gas transmission infrastructure that provides transportation service from multiple receipt points in the Delaware Basin to various delivery points in and around the Waha Hub in Texas.

We generate a substantial majority of our revenue under primarily long-term and fee-based gathering agreements with our customers. The majority of our gathering agreements are underpinned by areas of mutual interest (“AMIs”) and minimum volume commitments (“MVCs”). Our AMIs provide that any production drilled by our customers within the AMIs will be shipped on our gathering systems. The MVCs are designed to ensure that we will generate a minimum amount of gathering revenue over the life of each respective gathering agreement. The fee-based nature of the majority of the gathering agreements enhances the stability of our cash flows and limits our direct commodity price exposure.

Since our formation in 2009, our management team has established a track record of executing this strategy through the acquisition and subsequent development of DFW Midstream, Grand River, Polar & Divide, Niobrara G&P, and Double E Pipeline.

Summit Midstream is proudly committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse and inclusive workforce. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical condition), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Relocation: No Relocation assistance provided.

Work Sponsorship: Summit Midstream will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. Any offer of employment is contingent upon the Company receiving satisfactory results from a pre-employment drug screening, a criminal background check, and reference checks and your satisfaction of all other applicable fitness for duty requirements.

DOT Compliance: Responsibilities may include Department of Transportation (DOT) covered functions per PHMSA or FMSCA. Job duties also require the employee to be alert and respond immediately to dangerous or hazardous conditions, and where impaired performance, or failure to follow safety precautions, could result in serious injury or property damage. Maintain working knowledge of regulatory requirements, perform required tasks, and complete associated documentation (OSHA, DOT, EPA, etc.)

Competitive salary range of: $39.76 to $47.69

Summit Midstream offers a comprehensive benefits package including:

  • Company Paid Holidays
  • Discretionary Performance Bonus
  • Medical Insurance
  • Dental Insurance
  • Vision Insurance
  • Employer supplemented Health Savings Account
  • Flexible Benefit Plan
  • Basic Term Life Insurance
  • Voluntary Term Life and AD&D Insurance
  • Employer Short & Long-Term Disability Insurance
  • Employee Assistance Plan (EAP)
  • Hospital Indemnity, Critical Illness and Accident Insurance
  • Wellness Incentive Program
  • 6% Retirement Plan Match

Summary

Pipeline Operator operates, Inspects, maintains, and repairs pipelines, compression and measurement facilities, with the ability to direct and lead teams, projects and processes involved in natural gas pipelines and compression facilities.

Principle Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Maintain scheduled pigging operations, launcher/receiver maintenance and equipment inventory.
  • Inspect, maintain and repair as needed all facilities as assigned, including but not limited to pipelines, compression, and measurement facilities
  • On-call responsibility for areas of responsibility as needed
  • Maintain working knowledge of regulatory requirements, (OSHA, DOT, etc) and document required regulatory activities
  • Plan, organize and prioritize assigned responsibilities and assign responsibilities to others
  • Work independently as liaison between Summit Midstream and outside entities, i.e. landowners, emergency response agencies, contractors and other pipeline companies
  • Operate and assist in maintenance activities at compressor facilities
  • Perform pipeline patrols and inspect lines throughout the area and coordinate the activities of crews at other locations
  • Utilize hand tools to remove or replace valves, and have a basic understanding of riser locations and underground valves
  • Perform Lock-out/Tag-out procedures and write Safe Work Permits, as well as performing emergency shut-downs and operations control center protocol
  • Manage all activities with a focus on safety and compliance
  • Use proper tools and equipment to perform integrity management and regulatory tasks on natural gas pipelines
  • Monitor activity in and around pipeline and facilities and respond as necessary to protect system integrity, with an understanding of what to do in case of an emergency and/or spill
  • Put in work orders in Maximo, and be able to utilize CYGNET
  • Maintain required forms, records, and reports
  • Respond to pipeline emergencies; perform cleanup associated with field ops and corrosion control activities
  • Other duties as assigned

Education & Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 2 to 5 or more years of general pipeline experience in the natural gas industry or related experience in similar industry

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Can manage and control specific projects given to them, i.e. pigging programs, responding to emergency situations, incident commands, etc., as needed when the Supervisor is absent
  • Proven knowledge and experience with line location equipment and techniques
  • Ability to read and utilize drawings, schematics, alignment sheets
  • Ability to identify pipes and valves and what they do
  • Proven knowledge and understanding of procedures used to safely pig pipeline, i.e. launching, receiving and inspection
  • Knowledge to conduct pressure surveys on gathering lines and central delivery points
  • Experienced in monitoring natural gas quality using sampling equipment
  • Ability to direct employees to tasks that need completion and ability to follow up after completion
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills required
  • Must have a valid driver license with acceptable driving record
  • Demonstrate the ability to operate off-road vehicles safely
  • On-call responsibility for areas as assigned

Physical Demands and Working Conditions

  • Above average physical mobility to enable access to elevated height areas via stairs or ladders, as well as movement from place to place on the job, taking distance and speed into account
  • Strenuous physical activity-pushing, pulling and lifting requirements up to 50 lbs. manually transport a load up to 75 lbs. and apply up to 100 ft. lbs. of torque
  • Must be able to work out of doors in extreme weather conditions and perform heavy physical labor operating equipment in a safe manner
  • Work indoors and outdoors in and around industrial and electrical equipment

title: ISNP Clinical Coordinator
description:
*** THIS POSITION MAY BE ELIGIBLE FOR UP TO A $15,000 SIGN-ON BONUS (restrictions may apply) ***

This position is Full-Time, Monday through Friday, 8 am-4:30 pm working on-site at a designated SNF in Roscoe. NY. Ideal candidates live in Sullivan County.

The Institutional Special Needs Plan (ISNP) Clinical Coordinator is a health plan-employed registered nurse assigned on-site to a designated skilled nursing facility (SNF). The position serves as the clinical integration link among the member, the SNF care team, the Medical Provider or other treating practitioner(s), and the health plan. The coordinator supports implementation of the ISNP Model of Care through daily clinical surveillance, timely escalation of changes in condition, facilitation of practitioner services, interdisciplinary care coordination, transition follow-up, quality improvement, and utilization management support. The role promotes person-centered care, skilled-in-place treatment when clinically appropriate, closure of quality gaps, and prevention of avoidable emergency department visits and hospitalizations.

The ISNP Clinical Coordinator is assigned to Nascentia Health Members for the purpose of executing the Institutional Special Needs Model of Care within a Skilled Nursing Facility. The coordinator is responsible for supporting on site continuity of care, data gathering and facilitation of effective onboarding of new health plan members. The coordinator will work with the local clinical and administrative staff to educate and train the nursing facility on the ISNP model of care, will access facility and Nascentia EMR data to ensure the Nascentia clinical team understands member transition needs and communicates any need for network status or other provider support. Additionally, the coordinator will update member information for provider review, facilitate initial and ongoing provider visits, and perform care coordination activities. The coordinator will also assist in Utilization Review processes including data collection of demographics, claims, and medical information; analysis; and outcomes reporting. Utilize standards of care, evidence-based practices, CMS and organizational coverage guidelines to assure members receive high-quality, cost-efficient health care and services to meet their long-term home and community-based needs. Performs utilization review in accordance with all state-mandated regulations.

Performance Responsibilities and Standards:

  1. Performs facilitated Telehealth visits with provider and patients with acute or on-going needs
  2. Coordinates Plan of Care services with facility staff, patient, families and providers
  3. Communicate with physicians, medical directors, and the interdisciplinary team to address symptoms and improve care
  4. Monitor 24-hour reports and prepare daily reports with report out at huddles
  5. Assessment & Planning: Evaluate patient health status, needs, and resources; develop and revise patient-centered care plans in collaboration with patients, families, and providers
  6. Coordination: Arrange and schedule appointments, referrals, therapies, and follow-ups; coordinate clinical, psycho-social, and spiritual services as needed
  7. Advocacy: Act as a liaison between patients, families, and healthcare systems; ensure patient preferences and needs are met, including navigating insurance coverage and pre-approvals
  8. Education: Provide information on disease management, medication use, self-care, and preventive measures to patients and caregivers
  9. Monitoring & Adjustment: Track progress, adjust care plans as needed, and update medical records to reflect changes
  10. Transition Care: Facilitate smooth transitions between healthcare settings (e.g., hospital to home.
  11. Compliance: Uphold state and federal regulations, safety standards, and ethical conduct
  12. Support: Offer emotional and physical support to patients and families, especially during crises
  13. Discuss and explain advance care plan options and benefits; obtain informed consent.
  14. Assist with the review of member usage patterns for medical necessity and appropriateness.
  15. Perform continuing review of medical records and supporting documentation for medical necessity where appropriate.
  16. Tracks and analyzes service utilization patterns monthly and compares to regional benchmarks
  17. Participates in interdisciplinary collaboration with professional staff.
  18. Performs concurrent, prior service authorizations and retrospective reviews
  19. Analyze per member per month (PMPM) data
  20. Educate and promote the ISNP MOC with staff, patients and families
  21. Other duties as assigned

Job Qualifications:

  1. Current NYS RN licensure.
  2. Three or more years of home health care or long-term care experience is strongly preferred.
  3. Three or more years of utilization management or quality improvement experience preferred.
  4. Experience with CMS regulatory requirements.

Professional competencies, skills, and abilities:

  1. Excellent relational communication and management skills
  2. Demonstrates professional decorum
  3. Demonstrated ability to problem-solve complex, multifaceted situations
  4. Successfully manage conflict and negotiate solution focused outcomes
  5. Strong organizational, prioritizing, and delegation skills
  6. Strong critical thinking and ability to anticipate change
  7. Strong communication skills written and verbal
  8. Advocacy focused
  9. Computer literacy with Microsoft Office products

Physical Requirements:

  1. Speech, visual, and hearing ability sufficient to express and comprehend written and

verbal communication

  1. Ability to sit or stand 90% of the day
  2. Frequent sitting, standing, walking
  3. Pushing, pulling, reaching, kneeling
  4. Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Determination Category: Category III- Employee who rarely has contact with blood and body fluids.

Compensation & Benefits:

Competitive Salary [This position is an S03 exempt position with a min-max rate of: $75,250- $87,138.92/annually] with:

  • Retention Bonuses

Nascentia Health is leading the way in home care, post acute care and long-term community health. Position Summary

As a member of a multidisciplinary team, the Time Limited Rental Assistance Program (TLRA) Case Manager provides comprehensive counseling, case management, advocacy, and group work services to young adults ages 18–24 who are experiencing homelessness. The Case Manager supports participants as they transition into permanent housing while building employment readiness, educational attainment, and essential independent living skills. Direct Service & Case Management

  • Assist participants in managing and resolving potential crises.

Advocacy, Referrals & Skill Building

Organizational Values

  • Promote and model the trauma informed Sanctuary Model’s 7 Commitments and the SELF (Safety, Emotional Management, Loss, and Future) framework.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree required.
  • Minimum of two (2) years of experience providing services to at-risk youth and young adults, including LGBTQ+ youth.
  • Experience conducting assessments, providing individual and group counseling, and implementing individualized service plans.
  • Demonstrated collaboration with community-based organizations and NYC systems.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

You build trust across teams, turn unclear requests into well-defined problems, and validate what applications can actually do. Your work delivers measurable business value, follows established security and data governance standards, and remains maintainable as business needs evolve.

title: Land Development Designer / Landscape Architect
description:

This position is an in-office/on-site support role. NorthPoint provides an inclusive environment that cultivates collaboration and mentorship. Our core values set the foundation of our culture and guide us in every business decision.

“We truly believe, and I’m convinced, we have some pretty incredible assets. But those assets have all come from our people.” - Nathaniel Hagedorn | CEO.

How We Put You First:

At NorthPoint Development we ask a lot of our employees, which is why we give so much in return. In addition to your competitive salary, we offer market-leading benefits and perks:

  • A selection of comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans
  • 401k with 100% match up to 6%, immediately vested upon enrollment

title: Order Processing and Returns Associate - ESCO (Remote)
location: Remote (US), Charlotte NC, Raleigh NC, Jacksonville FL, Tampa FL, Richmond VA, Virginia Beach VA, Atlanta GA, Columbus OH, Cincinnati OH, Lansdale PA
description:
Candidates residing within 50 miles of our office will be expected to work onsite Tuesday through Thursday as part of a hybrid schedule. Candidates residing outside of the 50-mile radius will be eligible for a remote position. If remote, this position would require travel to the Headquarters location (Lansdale, PA) for onboarding and training during the first week. Please do not apply unless you are located on EST and are able to travel to Headquarters during the first week of employment.

About Keystone Technologies:

Founded in 1945, Keystone Technologies is a third-generation, family-owned business headquartered in the Greater Philadelphia area. A national leader in the commercial and industrial lighting industry, Keystone reaches customers across the U.S. with its mission of "Light Made Easy."

Who We Are:

We’re not your typical lighting company — and we like it that way. At Keystone, we move fast, think big, and challenge the status quo to deliver on our promise of Light Made Easy®. Our team thrives on new ideas, supports one another, aims high, works hard, and laughs often. And we always put people first — whether that’s our customers, partners, or each other. If you’re passionate about growing, collaborating, and making a difference, you’ll feel right at home here.

Our Core Values

  • Wow Customers: Every interaction is an opportunity to show how much we care and appreciate all our customers, internal and external, so we create unique experiences that go above and beyond their expectations.
  • Grow Passionately: We embrace growth through creativity, curiosity, and an eagerness to learn. Our work isn’t just about achieving more; it’s about evolving personally and professionally, transforming at every opportunity.
  • Do Right: It’s not just good ethics to do the right thing; it’s good business. We uphold the highest integrity, and we do the right thing even when it’s hard. Why? Because trust is our most important currency.
  • Value People: We come from a range of backgrounds, affiliations, and experiences. We honor everybody’s story and build lifelong relationships, whether with colleagues, customers, or partners, because to reach our fullest potential means empowering people to thrive.
  • Challenge Convention: We refuse to blindly accept the status quo. With agility, courage, and tenacity, we continuously improve — asking tough questions, looking beyond surfaces, and not stopping to rest on our accomplishments.

What we offer:

Our benefits include medical, dental, vision, voluntary life insurance, employer-paid group life insurance, short-term disability, a 401k plan with company match, paid time off, and philanthropic opportunities.

The Opportunity:

The Order Processing & Returns Team ensures that customer orders are filled, and customer returns are processed timely, accurately, and to the customers' specifications. The team manages the flow of customer purchase orders from receipt to shipment to ensure fulfillment of our Light Made Easy promise by problem-solving and working effectively with customers and various departments to fill every order and complete returns as expeditiously as possible.

Your Impact:

  • Entering customer purchase orders into computer system and work with warehouse team to fill orders

  • Processing shipments released from third party warehouses

  • Managing back orders and communicate with internal and external customers accordingly

  • Working with various internal departments to resolve issues related to pricing, credit, inventory availability, shipping, etc.

  • Communicating directly with customers to provide order status updates

  • Developing a working knowledge of our part numbers and product offering

  • Serving as a customer service contact for external and internal customers to see RMA cases through to completion

  • Interacting with customers and sales personnel to initiate claims

  • Collaborating with product development team to have warranty claims reviewed

  • Investigating shipping discrepancies with warehouse team and perform required computer transactions to adjust inventory levels

  • Communicating with accounting team to ensure customers receive proper credits

  • Coordinating all logistics to collect returned goods and ship replacements

  • Communicating directly with customers to provide case status updates

  • Maintaining key customer records in computer system

What you bring:

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required

  • 1-3 years of customer service experience or in a related field

  • 1-3 years of data entry experience

  • Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, specifically Excel

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills

  • Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail

  • Ability to work individually and in a team

  • Ability to prioritize and juggle tasks while maintaining accuracy in a fast-paced work environment

  • Ability to process in a timely manner

  • Able to maintain professional relationships with internal and external customers

title: Area Manager
description:
Pediatric Home Service is a leader in home health care, we are committed to taking care of the child! PHS has been committed to providing state-of-the-art home medical equipment, supplies, clinical respiratory care and enteral nutrition services since 1987. We are looking for an experienced leader in home health care who will be responsible for the overall direction of all customer-facing departments.

  • Position: Area Manager
  • Location: Houston, Texas
  • Hours: Monday-Friday, 8 am- 5 pm
    • In office, on call as needed
    • Travel required within the assigned area

The Position:

The Area Manager oversees all customer-facing and operational activities to ensure high-quality patient care and effective team performance. This includes managing staff hiring, training, and development; coordinating patient services; and resolving issues with patients, families, and internal teams. The role involves preparing reports, budgets, and improvement plans, collaborating with leadership on strategic goals, and maintaining compliance with professional standards. Additionally, the manager negotiates with vendors, manages facility needs, and implements workflows and training programs to support continuous improvement in pediatric home health and DME service.

  • Oversees day-to-day operations of area location to ensure efficient service delivery and patient needs are met in accordance with physician orders, company policies and procedures and professional standards of home-based care
  • Responsible for the overall direction of all customer-facing and customer-enabling area location employees
  • In conjunction with Regional VP, manage P&D, ensure financial targets and budgets are met or exceeded
  • Analyze financial statements and key performance indicators (KPIs) to identify areas for improvement
  • Develop and manage budgets for each area location, ensuring cost control and profitability
  • Ensure all areas deliver exceptional customer service, managing escalated customer concerns and complaints, ensuring timely resolution
  • Confers with managers and staff concerning problems of patient care or policies and assists in analyzing problems and formulating solutions
  • Develops and promotes cooperative working relationships with other provider agencies and referral sources
  • Acts as liaison with caregivers and clinical staff on appropriate home medical equipment choices and ensures coordination of care with other company services, such as RT, CN, PHAR/IV
  • Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement that promotes teamwork, professional growth, employee engagement and recognizes high performance
  • Set clear goals and expectations, providing regular feedback and performance management.
  • Seeks ways to improve and promote quality by participating in departmental and corporate quality improvement activities
  • Monitor customer satisfaction levels and implement improvements as needed

Supervisory Responsibilities:

  • Interviewing, hiring, and onboarding new team members
  • Providing training, coaching, and ongoing development
  • Planning, assigning, and monitoring daily work activities
  • Conducting performance evaluations and giving feedback and recognizing and rewarding strong performance
  • Addressing concerns, resolving issues, and handling corrective actions when needed

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, healthcare administration, operations, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of relevant education and progressive leadership experience may be considered
  • Seven (7) years of progressive experience in healthcare operations, DME, home health, multi-site operations, or a related environment preferred
  • Previous experience leading and developing teams, including other leaders
  • Experience with budgeting, financial statements, operational metrics, and P&L responsibility
  • Understanding of healthcare reimbursement, insurance processes, revenue cycle, and/or DME operations preferred
  • Demonstrated ability to improve processes, solve complex operational challenges, and manage competing priorities
  • Strong relationship-building skills and ability to partner effectively across clinical, operational, and corporate teams
  • Comfortable using data and KPIs to identify trends and guide decisions
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to lead through change and bring teams together
  • A hands-on, collaborative leadership style and willingness to stay connected to day-to-day operations

The Company:

Pediatric Home Service is a pediatric home health agency that has provided high-quality DME and nursing services to medically fragile children since 1990. Our services allow our clients to remain and thrive in their homes, schools, and communities. The majority of the clients we serve are age’s birth through 21 years old and have a variety of technologies that might include a trach, ventilator or g-tube.

As an Area Manager, you’ll have the opportunity to make an impact at several levels developing employees and leaders, strengthening operations, supporting growth, and ultimately helping our teams provide an exceptional experience for the children and families we serve. If you’re a people-focused operations leader who enjoys building strong teams, improving processes, and turning strategy into action, we’d love to hear from you.

Benefits:

  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) for full time employees to ensure a healthy work-life balance
  • 401(k) Matching to help secure your future
  • Tuition Reimbursement to support your educational and professional growth
  • Professional Development & Learning Opportunities to expand your skills and knowledge in pediatric care
  • A supportive and fulfilling work environment where your contributions directly impact children’s health and well-being

Interested candidates should apply online at http://www.phscareers.com.

We look forward to learning more about you and the skills you can bring to Pediatric Home Service!

Pediatric Home Service is an equal opportunity employer; we are committed to affirmative action and equal employment opportunities for all regardless of protected veteran status, race, color, creed, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation or identity, disability, age, marital status, familial status, membership or activity in a local human rights commission, or status with regard to public assistance.

title: Internship - Acoustic metamaterials and active noise control
description:
We are seeking graduate students interested in advancing acoustic metamaterials and active noise control technologies for reducing machine noise and improving acoustic privacy. The interns will collaborate with MERL researchers to develop novel approaches for controlling sound propagation through a combination of passive acoustic structures and active sound field control. Research may involve the design and optimization of acoustic metamaterials, microphone and loudspeaker array processing, adaptive noise cancellation, and experimental validation of noise reduction and speech privacy systems. The interns will develop and implement algorithms, conduct acoustic simulations and measurements, build experimental prototypes, and prepare results for publication.

The ideal candidates are Ph.D. students with experience in some of the following: acoustics, acoustic metamaterials, active noise control, adaptive filtering, acoustic wave propagation, microphone and loudspeaker arrays, numerical simulation, and signal processing. Experience with finite element modeling, optimization, or physics-informed machine learning is also desirable.

Flexible start dates and internship durations (typically 3–6 months) are available.

The pay range for this internship position will be 6-8K per month.

  • Integrate the Sanctuary Model SELF (Safety, Emotional Management, Loss and Future) framework into daily practice to ensure quality care and an effective work environment.

Qualifications:

  • High School Diploma or GED required.
  • Associate or bachelor’s degree preferred.
  • Must have excellent written, organizational, and prioritization skills.
  • Ability to transition easily between working independently with a high degree of self-initiative and contributing as part of a team.
  • Valid Driver's License required
  • Participate in creating a safe and therapeutic milieu.
  • Effective in conflict resolution and crisis intervention techniques and practices.
  • Must be able to successfully complete state mandated crisis intervention training, and perform physical restraint of a resident.
  • Must be able to successfully complete state mandated medication administration training.
  • Must be flexible to work evening, overnight, weekend and holiday hours.
  • Must have a commitment to work from a strength-based, youth and family development and trauma-informed perspective.
  • Bilingual – Spanish preferred

Additional Qualifications:

  • Must successfully complete a pre-hire physical ability test.

title: Senior Manager M&A Due Diligence
description:
Senior Manager, Financial Institutions M&A Due Diligence

Doeren Mayhew is a tax, assurance and advisory firm headquartered in Troy, Michigan with 25 offices across the country and abroad. Founded in 1932, Doeren Mayhew is recognized as the 36th largest CPA firm in the U.S. and is positioned for successful future growth. Doeren Mayhew's Financial Institutions Group is comprised of cross-functional professionals delivering industry-focused expertise to more than 400 institutions across the nation. Our group of trusted advisors assists a wide range of financial organizations in assessing opportunities, managing risk and delivering stakeholder value.

Doeren Mayhew is seeking a Senior Manager to help lead financial due diligence engagements within its growing Financial Institutions Group M&A and Strategic Advisory practice. The role will work primarily with credit unions, banks, credit union service organizations and other financial institution-related businesses on mergers, acquisitions and strategic transactions. This position offers direct exposure to executive management, significant engagement responsibility and the opportunity to help develop a differentiated financial institutions M&A platform. Hours will fluctuate based on transaction activity and client deadlines.

Responsibilities

  • Lead merger and buy-side financial due diligence engagements from initial scoping through final client presentation.
  • Analyze historical and projected financial performance, including quality and sustainability of earnings, capital, liquidity, asset quality, loans, investments, deposits, profitability and other transaction-specific matters.
  • Lead loan portfolio and credit diligence, including concentrations, delinquencies, nonaccrual loans, charge-offs, risk ratings, underwriting practices and the allowance for credit losses under CECL.
  • Assess purchase accounting, fair value marks, merger-related costs, transaction liabilities, opening balance-sheet considerations and post-close earnings implications.
  • Identify and communicate risks, value drivers and opportunities that may affect valuation, deal structure, negotiated terms or integration planning.
  • Prepare clear diligence reports, executive summaries and presentations and lead meetings with senior management, boards and transaction committees.
  • Manage engagement scope, budgets, timelines, workplans, client communications and delivery under compressed transaction deadlines.
  • Collaborate closely with professionals across valuation, tax, audit, regulatory, legal, technology, cybersecurity and other specialists to provide an integrated transaction assessment.
  • Supervise and develop team members, review workpapers and analyses and maintain engagement quality standards.
  • Support practice growth through proposal development, prospect meetings, client relationships, thought leadership and continued improvement of FIG diligence methodologies.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance or a related field. Masters in accounting preferred
  • CPA, CFA or other relevant financial, accounting or credit credentials are preferred.
  • A minimum of 7 years of relevant experience, including at least 4 years in financial due diligence, transaction advisory, quality of earnings, loan review or a comparable financial institution M&A role.
  • Financial institutions’ experience required with direct credit union experience preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, financial statement analysis, ASC 805, ASC 326 and financial institution regulatory reporting is preferred.
  • Strong analytical, project management and problem-solving skills, including the ability to prioritize issues and manage multiple concurrent deadlines.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead engagements from planning through final client presentation with limited day-to-day supervision.
  • Executive-level written and verbal communication skills
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel and financial analysis skill preferred; proficiency in Microsoft Office required.
  • Ability to travel up to 10%.
  • Ability to work effectively in a transaction-driven environment where hours will fluctuate based on transaction activity and client deadlines.

title: Transportation Design Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
description:

title: Senior Director, Financial Planning & Analysis - Healthcare
description:
Pediatric Home Service is a friendly and professional leader in home health care with a singular passion for and commitment to taking care of the child. As a leader in home health care, we help kids achieve their best lives at home and in their communities while providing our employees a fun and rewarding place to work.

  • Position: Senior Director, Financial Planning & Analysis
  • Location: Roseville, MN
  • Schedule: Full-time, Monday-Friday, 8:00 am to 5:00 pm
    • Work Arrangement: Hybrid schedule with two (2) days per week in the office

The Position:

The Director of Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A) provides strategic leadership for the organization's financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance analysis functions. This role partners closely with executive leadership to deliver meaningful financial insights, support data-driven decision-making, and ensure the organization achieves its operational and growth objectives. They also oversee financial reporting, budget management processes, and long-term financial planning initiatives.

  • Develop, prepare, and maintain on a monthly, quarterly, and annual basis executive financial reporting packages for distribution to the Executive Team, our Private Equity Sponsor(s), the Board, and other Company leaders, which include an understanding of all variances and key action items
  • Responsible for leadership activities of the Financial Planning & Analysis team, including performance evaluations, compensation determination, recruitment, and hiring
  • Foster a culture of inclusivity, value diverse perspectives, and focus on team development and advancement
  • Lead ad hoc projects that drive efficiencies and savings and ultimately increase bottom line profitability
  • Continually develop and refine internal financial modeling and process improvements
  • Serve as the subject matter expert on PHS’s service lines and financial drivers, and use that knowledge to give management clear, actionable recommendations
  • Lead an annual integrated, collaborative strategic, financial, and capital planning process – updating quarterly as required
  • Partner with Service Line leaders and the Executive Team to capture all critical inputs for annual budget, analysis, and decision support
  • Provide market analytics necessary to support business development, planning, and strategic decision making
  • Lead a collaborative quarterly forecasting processes that enables operations leaders to drive results and consistently achieve plans
  • Ensure forecast deadlines are met, assist with the consolidation of forecast and budget across teams, and enhance / streamline the process
  • Partner with CEO and CFO and Private Equity Sponsor(s) on M&A opportunities, including the provision of financial models
  • Oversee the utilization and continuous improvement of the financial reports and analytics used by the Company
  • Lead the development and testing of rolling forecast model and other financial and business insight tools
  • Direct the preparation of reports, statistics, and / or business analytics related to financial performance and analysis as needed
  • Demonstrate ability to build consensus, navigate disagreement constructively, and secure genuine buy-in from cross-functional leaders and team members, with a collaborative style that earns trust

Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance or Business Administration
  • Eight (8) years of experience including at least three (3) years leading an FP&A department
  • Possess strong analytical and critical-thinking skills with the ability to synthesize complex financial, operational, and market data, identify trends and risks, and translate findings into actionable business recommendations.
  • Demonstrated business partnership and communication skills, including the ability to influence senior leaders and effectively present financial results and strategic insights to executive leadership, Board members, and financial sponsors.
  • Strong understanding of business drivers, profitability, capital planning, and M&A financial analysis, with the ability to evaluate opportunities and support strategic growth decisions.
  • Demonstrated leadership and strong change-management capabilities with the ability to develop high-performing teams, develop culture and foster engagement; Lead cross-functional planning processes, drive accountability, and continuously improve financial systems, reporting, and processes
  • Ability to exercise sound judgment, executive presence, discretion, adaptability, and a high degree of accuracy while managing multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced environment

Preferred:

  • Master's degree in Finance or Business Administration
  • Experience in healthcare services provider or payer
  • Experience supporting private equity-backed organizations, including board and investor reporting
  • Demonstrated experience supporting mergers and acquisitions, business expansion initiatives, and enterprise-wide strategic planning
  • Experience leading organizational change, financial transformation initiatives, and implementation of reporting, planning, and analytics tools

The Company:

Pediatric Home Service is a pediatric home health agency that has provided high-quality DME and nursing services to children that are medically fragile since 1990. Our services allow our clients to remain and thrive in their homes, schools, and communities. The majority of the clients we serve are age’s birth through 21 years old and have a variety of technologies that might include a trach, ventilator or g-tube.

Benefits:

  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) for full time employees to ensure a healthy work-life balance
  • 401(k) Matching to help secure your future
  • Tuition Reimbursement to support your educational and professional growth
  • Professional Development & Learning Opportunities to expand your skills and knowledge in pediatric care
  • A supportive and fulfilling work environment where your contributions directly impact children’s health and well-being

Salary Range:

At PHS, we are committed to providing specialized care for medically complex children. Every role, from direct patient care to customer support, plays a vital part in improving the lives of kids and families. The impact you make is invaluable. We are dedicated to offering fair and transparent compensation to our team members. The range for this role is $180,000 to $210,000 annually, based on experience and qualifications.

title: Project Manager
description:
Headquartered in Houston, Texas, Summit Midstream Corporation (NYSE: SMC) is a value-driven corporation focused on developing, owning and operating midstream energy infrastructure assets that are strategically located in unconventional resource basins, primarily shale formations, in the continental United States.

We currently operate natural gas, crude oil and produced water gathering systems in four unconventional resource basins:

  • the Williston Basin in North Dakota, which includes the Bakken and Three Forks shale formations;
  • the Denver-Julesburg Basin, which includes the Niobrara and Codell shale formations in Colorado and Wyoming;
  • the Fort Worth Basin in Texas, which includes the Barnett Shale formation; and
  • the Piceance Basin in Colorado, which includes the liquids-rich Mesaverde formation as well as the emerging Mancos and Niobrara Shale formations.

Our systems and the basins they serve are as follows:

  • the Polar & Divide system, which serves the Williston Basin;
  • the DFW Midstream system, which serves the Fort Worth Basin;
  • the Grand River system, which serves the Piceance Basin; and
  • the Niobrara G&P system, which serves the DJ Basin.

SMC has an equity investment in and operates Double E Pipeline, LLC, which is natural gas transmission infrastructure that provides transportation service from multiple receipt points in the Delaware Basin to various delivery points in and around the Waha Hub in Texas.

We generate a substantial majority of our revenue under primarily long-term and fee-based gathering agreements with our customers. The majority of our gathering agreements are underpinned by areas of mutual interest (“AMIs”) and minimum volume commitments (“MVCs”). Our AMIs provide that any production drilled by our customers within the AMIs will be shipped on our gathering systems. The MVCs are designed to ensure that we will generate a minimum amount of gathering revenue over the life of each respective gathering agreement. The fee-based nature of the majority of the gathering agreements enhances the stability of our cash flows and limits our direct commodity price exposure.

Since our formation in 2009, our management team has established a track record of executing this strategy through the acquisition and subsequent development of DFW Midstream, Grand River, Polar & Divide, Niobrara G&P, and Double E Pipeline.

Summit Midstream is proudly committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse and inclusive workforce. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical condition), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Relocation: No Relocation assistance provided.

Work Sponsorship: Summit Midstream will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. Any offer of employment is contingent upon the Company receiving satisfactory results from a pre-employment drug screening, a criminal background check, and reference checks and your satisfaction of all other applicable fitness for duty requirements.

Summary:

We are seeking a highly skilled and results-driven Project Manager to lead and coordinate midstream oil and gas facility and pipeline projects from concept through completion. This role will oversee the planning, design, cost estimating, and execution of projects including compressor stations, pump and meter stations, storage terminals, gas processing facilities, new well connects and pipelines.

The Project Manager will manage multidisciplinary teams, external contractors, and stakeholders to ensure safe, timely, and cost-effective project delivery. The ideal candidate will have strong technical expertise in the midstream oil and gas sector, with proven leadership and communication skills to drive successful project execution.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with Commercial and Operations teams to develop project scopes for new opportunities and facility improvement proposals.
  • Prepare cost estimates for various project alternatives and develop funding authorization documents for sanctioned projects.
  • Solicit design input from customers and internal stakeholders; design facilities in accordance with industry codes and company policies.
  • Lead HAZOP reviews and ensure safety and operability are built into designs.
  • Manage procurement planning, contractor selection, bid evaluations, and contract execution.
  • Review and approve contractor documents, invoices, and ensure proper cost coding and documentation.
  • Coordinate with Land and Regulatory teams to secure right-of-way, permits, and regulatory approvals.
  • Work closely with the Construction team to develop implementation plans and allocate internal and external resources.
  • Monitor and track all project activities to ensure adherence to schedule and budget.
  • Prepare and distribute regular project progress reports; proactively communicate material deviations to stakeholders.
  • Manage scope, cost, and schedule changes through structured change control processes.
  • Support commissioning and turnover activities with operations and maintenance teams.
  • Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental, and regulatory standards (e.g., PHMSA, OSHA, and applicable local agencies).
  • Complete all project close-out activities, including as-built drawings, construction records, updates to operations manuals, and regulatory closure documentation.

Education & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering (Civil, Chemical, Mechanical, or Electrical) preferred or equivalent experience.
  • Minimum 3-5 years of relevant post-degree experience in project management or engineering.
  • Experience with FERC and DOT transmission projects.

The National Domestic Workers Alliance (NDWA) is the leading national voice for dignity, respect, and recognition for domestic workers in the United States. NDWA was founded in 2007 by organizers and worker leaders in six cities representing nannies, house cleaners, and care workers, and now represents an alliance of more than 76 organizations across 22 states and 395,000 domestic workers nationally.

We envision a society where domestic work is valued as essential to our collective well-being, domestic workers are leaders in shaping the care sector, and domestic work jobs are good, economically secure jobs.

For over 15 years, we’ve worked to advance our mission by making domestic work visible. We’ve worked to pass policies that enable rights and higher wages for domestic workers across the country, changed public awareness and opinion about the dignity and value of care work, and built the capacity and leadership of domestic workers to organize and advocate for their rights.

We see the next era of our organization as an opportunity to move domestic work from newfound visibility towards transformation, and we’re ready to elevate care workers to the essential workers of the 21st-century economy.

We’re a multi-racial, multi-lingual organization building a powerful movement rooted in the human rights, dignity, and equality of domestic workers, care workers, immigrant women, and women of color.

POSITION SUMMARY

The National Domestic Workers Alliance () is the leading national voice for dignity, respect, and recognition for domestic workers in the United States. Through leadership development, strategic campaigns, and alliance building, we are building a powerful movement rooted in the human rights, dignity, and equality of domestic workers, care workers, immigrant women, and women of color.

Care in Action seeks a strategic, detail-oriented, and mission-driven Director of Finance to lead financial management across Care in Action (501(c)(4)), its PAC, and affiliated entities including NDWA Labs. Reporting to the VP of Finance, this role serves as the primary financial steward for Care in Action, with responsibility for budgeting, financial reporting, treasury management, audit, grants compliance, and financial governance. The Director of Finance manages monthly close, expense and treasury approvals, and intercompany transactions across multiple entities; serves as Board Treasurer and the lead point of contact for external auditors; and works in close coordination with NDWA's accounting team, the Development department, legal/compliance staff, and senior leadership to ensure the financial health, accuracy, and sustainability of the organization.

Please note: Candidates must have at least 5 years of progressive financial management experience in nonprofit organizations, including direct experience managing the finances of a 501(c)(4) within a multi-entity structure (such as a 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), and PAC). Applications that do not clearly demonstrate both will not be considered.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Budget Management and Financial Reporting

  • Play a leading role in the annual budget process by supporting key staff in developing program budgets; providing accurate reports on budget vs. actuals, income projections, including both restricted and unrestricted funding, and progress on funding deliverables.

  • Prepare timely financial packages for Care in Action and NDWA Labs; ensure monthly close occurs by the 15th of each month with reports completed by the 20th.

  • Ensure accurate coding of revenue and expenses to various programs and departments.

  • Review monthly revenues with the AR team, ensuring accurate classification of restricted and unrestricted funds. Responsible for regular revenue reconciliation with the Development team.

  • Update and maintain the Temporarily Restricted Net Assets (TRNA) schedule, tracking monthly releases.

  • Maintain and update the Chart of Accounts for both CiA and CiA PAC.

  • Prepare payroll coding sheets and upload journal entries as needed.

  • Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to ensure payroll allocations are updated regularly.

Expense Approvals and Treasury Management

  • Review and approve all expenses for CiA, NDWA Labs, and the PAC, including staff reimbursements.

  • Hold expense and invoice approvals in Bill.com.

  • Handle occasional treasury functions including managing investments, approving disbursements, and managing cash flow.

  • Maintain appropriate cash balances in line with organizational policy.

  • Authorize the transfer of funds for electoral work advances; track PAC prepayments and their drawdown.

  • Approve invoices for inter-company charges between entities.

  • Responsible for ensuring monthly close of accounts.

Grants and Development Support

  • Work closely with the Development team to ensure the timely conduct of grant processes including application, documentation, reimbursements, and audit requirements.

  • Support the Development team in preparing restricted grant reports and proposals, including reviewing deliverables in Salesforce.

Audit and Compliance

  • Serve as the lead point of contact for auditors in annual audits.

  • Update and implement financial policies and procedures to ensure compliance and efficiency in all aspects of financial management.

  • Ensure consistent implementation of CiA's financial handbook and financial manual.

Board and Leadership Engagement

  • Prepare and present financial updates and budget materials to the CiA board; conduct meetings with CiA management and the board.

  • Promote the organization's financial health by providing financial updates and responding to requests from the Executive Director and the Leadership Team.

  • Serve as Board Treasurer for Care in Action.

Affiliate Financial Management (NDWA Labs)

  • Ensure the accuracy and compliance of day-to-day financial accounting functions and processes for Care in Action and affiliated entities, such as NDWA Labs. Prepare financial reports for the same.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • 5+ years of progressive financial management experience in a nonprofit organization. For-profit experience alone does not meet this requirement.

  • Direct, hands-on financial management experience with a 501(c)(4) organization, including its distinct compliance and reporting requirements.

  • Experience managing finances across multiple related nonprofit entities (such as a 501(c)(3), 501(c)(4), and PAC), including intercompany transactions, cost allocations, and entity-level reporting.

  • Demonstrated ability to prepare, analyze, and present financial statements, budget vs. actual reports, and cash flow projections.

  • Strong understanding of restricted and unrestricted fund accounting, grant financial reporting, and nonprofit revenue recognition.

  • Experience managing an audit process and working with external auditors.

  • Excellent organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail and accuracy.

  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills; ability to translate complex financial information for non-finance staff and board members.

  • Ability to work independently in a remote environment with a distributed team.

  • Alignment with NDWA's and Care in Action's mission, vision, and values.

Preferred

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Business Administration, Finance, or a related field; CPA or equivalent credential a plus.

  • Experience with PAC financial management and reporting.

  • Proficiency with Financial Edge (Blackbaud) accounting software.

  • Experience with Martus budgeting software or comparable budget management tools.

  • Experience with Divvy, Bill.com, Expensify, or similar expense management platforms.

  • Familiarity with Salesforce for grant tracking and reporting.

  • Prior experience coordinating with the Board of Directors.

  • Demonstrated commitment to racial, economic, and gender justice.
