title: Universal Design for Learning Specialist (PA)
description:
The Universal Design for Learning (UDL) Specialist provides guidance and serves as a resource to faculty and staff regarding UDL frameworks in instructional design, curriculum development, classroom practice, accessibility, and inclusive pedagogy. This position collaborates with faculty and staff to integrate UDL strategies that improve accessibility and foster engagement in online and in-person learning environments. The UDL Specialist will assesses and evaluate the effectiveness of UDL implementation. This role will promote a culture of inclusivity by developing and delivering professional development workshops and training. The UDL Specialist ensures compliance with federal, state, and institutional regulations regarding accessibility in education (ADA, Section 504, etc.). This position has a commitment to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) by working with faculty to expand accessibility in remote learning environments by ensuring accessibility of instructional materials, engagement tools, and authentic assessment measures.

FLCC is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion, and strives to provide an environment that embodies these principles. We strive to attract talented personnel from diverse backgrounds and traditions, particularly of race and ethnicity, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, nationality, culture, religion, worldview and physical and mental abilities. As such, applicants from historically under-represented groups are highly encouraged to apply.

This is a full-time, grant-funded position.

Qualifications:

  1. Educational Background: Bachelor’s degree in Education, Instructional Design, Special Education, Educational Technology, or a related field required. Universal Design for Learning certification or equivalent experience in accessibility, instructional design, or related areas preferred. Master’s degree preferred.

  2. Experience: Minimum of two (2) years experience in an educational setting, instructional design, curriculum design or accessibility services required. Demonstrated experience with UDL implementation in higher education or K-12 environments required. Experience in developing, delivering, and evaluating curriculum in varied modalities required.

  3. Special Skills: Ability to collect, analyze and interpret data required. Working knowledge of federal accessibility laws (ADA, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, Section 508, etc.) and assistive technologies required. Effective communication and collaboration skills and ability to provide leadership and guidance in a dynamic and diverse educational setting required.

Essential Functions:

  1. UDL Framework Implementation:

    1. Leads the integration of UDL principles into curriculum, instruction, and assessment practices, focusing on creating inclusive learning environments for all students.

    2. Develops resources to assist faculty in adopting UDL strategies through varied modalities.

    3. Collaborates with instructional designers to create accessible course materials, assessments, and multimedia content, ensuring the content meets UDL guidelines for diverse learners.

    4. Assesses and implements curriculum needs and goals.

    5. Implements learning design and principles and techniques.

    6. Collaborates with subject matter experts to create accessible and well-designed learning experiences.

    7. Applies innovative strategies to course design using UDL Principles.

    8. Researches, assesses, and shares emerging trends and best practices.

  2. Faculty and Staff Support:

    1. Consults with faculty to improve course accessibility, design, and implementation of UDL principles and strategies.

    2. Facilitates professional development opportunities regarding UDL best practices, accessibility, inclusive teaching strategies, and highlighting the benefits of UDL for all students.

    3. UDL liaison to faculty, instructional designers, and disability services staff, to ensure effective collaboration and communication.

    4. Partners with instructional designers to review Online Course Quality Review Rubrics to ensure accessibility standards are followed in all modalities, including but not limited to asynchronous online, hybrid, and HyFlex courses.

  3. Assessment and Evaluation:

    1. Assesses the effectiveness of UDL implementation and identifies areas for improvement through data collection, student feedback, and faculty input.

    2. Recommends continuous improvement in instructional practices related to UDL by enhancing inclusivity and student engagement.

  4. Collaboration and Advocacy:

    1. Partners with academic leaders to ensure UDL practices are inclusive and compliant with institutional policies and long-term strategic goals.

    2. Advocates for the creation of an inclusive learning environment across all educational programs by challenging barriers and promoting equity.

  5. Compliance and Accessibility:

    1. Ensures all course materials, assessments, and activities comply with institutional accessibility standards and relevant legal requirements, such as the ADA and Section 508.

    2. Supports the integration of assistive technology and other resources for students with disabilities, promoting equitable access to education.

Physical Requirements:
In accordance with the American with Disabilities Act, this job description contains only qualifications that are required, with or without reasonable accommodation.

  1. Ability to use computer for extended periods of time.

  2. Ability to sit or stand for extended periods of time.

  3. Frequently moves boxes weighing up to 20 pounds across office for various needs.

Benefits and Salary Range

  1. Competitive starting salary in the range of $55,382 to $59,537 and is commensurate with qualifications

  2. Flexible work schedule available upon completion of training; some on site work required at the Canandaigua campus

  3. NYS retirement or Optional SUNY Retirement Program

title: Hilton Phoenix Airport- General Manager
description:

The General Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, operational performance, financial results, and strategic direction of a full-service airport Hilton hotel.

This individual will drive revenue and profitability, maintain Hilton brand standards, deliver exceptional guest satisfaction, and build a strong, accountable leadership team.

The General Manager must understand the unique demands of an airport hotel, including 24-hour operations, airline crew and distressed-passenger business, airport transportation, fluctuating arrival and departure patterns, group and corporate demand, and maximizing short-booking-window revenue opportunities.

Hotel Operations

  • Maintain a highly visible presence throughout the hotel and actively engage with guests, employees, airline partners, corporate accounts, and Hilton representatives.

  • Ensure airport shuttle operations are reliable, safe, efficient, and appropriately staffed.
  • Champion a culture of urgency, accountability, service excellence, and measurable performance.
  • Maintain compliance with Hilton brand standards, operating procedures, and quality
  • assurance requirements.

  • Maintain full responsibility for the hotel’s P&L, annual budget, forecasting, cash flow, and operating performance.
  • Drive RevPAR, ADR, occupancy, GOP, and EBITDA, with an emphasis on outperforming the hotel’s competitive set.
  • Work closely with Sales and Revenue Management to optimize pricing and inventory based on airport traffic, compression periods, flight disruptions, citywide events, and short-term booking patterns.
  • Aggressively develop and maintain airline crew contracts, distressed-passenger relationships, corporate negotiated accounts, group business, and airport-related demand generators.
  • Identify opportunities to increase ancillary revenue through Food & Beverage, parking, meetings, transportation partnerships, and other hotel services.

Sales & Market Leadership

  • Serve as an active leader in the hotel’s sales strategy rather than relying solely on the sales department.

• Minimum 7-10 years of progressive hotel leadership experience.

• Previous General Manager, Hotel Manager, or Director of Operations experience in a

full-service hotel environment.

• Demonstrated success managing hotel financial performance and profitability.

• Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.

• Experience leading large, multi-department teams.

Preferred

• Previous Hilton brand experience.

• Luxury or upper-upscale full-service hotel experience.

• Bachelor’s degree in hospitality management, Business Administration, or related field.

• Experience working with ownership groups and asset managers.

Ideal Candidate Profile

• Proven leader who inspires teams and drives results.

• Strong financial and commercial acumen.

• Guest-focused and service-oriented.

• Effective communicator with management, corporate partners, and team members.

• Strategic thinker capable of executing operational excellence while driving long-term

growth.

benefits package.

title: Pricing Analyst (Remote)
location: Lansdale PA, Lawrenceville GA, Charlotte NC, Houston TX, Grand Prairie TX, Austin TX, San Antonio TX, Nashville TN, Tampa FL, Orlando FL, Kansas City MO, Saint Louis MO, Louisville KY, Remote (US)
description:
Candidates residing within 50 miles of our office (Lansdale, PA) will be expected to work onsite Tuesday through Thursday as part of a hybrid schedule. Candidates residing outside of the 50-mile radius will be eligible for a remote position. If remote, this position would require travel to the Headquarters location (Lansdale, PA) for onboarding and training during the first week.

Please do not apply unless you are located on EST or CST and are able to travel to Headquarters during the first week of employment.

About Keystone Technologies:

Founded in 1945, Keystone Technologies is a third-generation, family-owned business headquartered in the Greater Philadelphia area. A national leader in the commercial and industrial lighting industry, Keystone reaches customers across the U.S. with its mission of "Light Made Easy."

Who We Are:

We’re not your typical lighting company — and we like it that way. At Keystone, we move fast, think big, and challenge the status quo to deliver on our promise of Light Made Easy®. Our team thrives on new ideas, supports one another, aims high, works hard, and laughs often. And we always put people first — whether that’s our customers, partners, or each other. If you’re passionate about growing, collaborating, and making a difference, you’ll feel right at home here.

Our Core Values

  • Wow Customers: Every interaction is an opportunity to show how much we care and appreciate all our customers, internal and external, so we create unique experiences that go above and beyond their expectations.
  • Grow Passionately: We embrace growth through creativity, curiosity, and an eagerness to learn. Our work isn’t just about achieving more; it’s about evolving personally and professionally, transforming at every opportunity.
  • Do Right: It’s not just good ethics to do the right thing; it’s good business. We uphold the highest integrity, and we do the right thing even when it’s hard. Why? Because trust is our most important currency.
  • Value People: We come from a range of backgrounds, affiliations, and experiences. We honor everybody’s story and build lifelong relationships, whether with colleagues, customers, or partners, because to reach our fullest potential means empowering people to thrive.
  • Challenge Convention: We refuse to blindly accept the status quo. With agility, courage, and tenacity, we continuously improve — asking tough questions, looking beyond surfaces, and not stopping to rest on our accomplishments.

What we offer:

Our benefits include medical, dental, vision, voluntary life insurance, employer-paid group life insurance, short-term disability, a 401k plan with company match, paid time off, and philanthropic opportunities.

The Opportunity:

The Pricing Analyst will focus on developing job quotes, analyzing customer pricing, and collaborating closely with our sales team to enhance our pricing strategies and profitability, and improve customer satisfaction.

Your Impact:

  • Develop pricing structures for job quotes based on market trends and inventory levels

  • Manage customer pricing effectively in P21/ ERP software

  • Analyze pricing results including trends, turnaround time, win ratios, and price competitiveness

  • Collaborate with the sales team to understand customer needs and provide timely and accurate pricing information

  • Utilize advanced Excel to manage and analyze pricing data, eventually expanded into Power BI analytics

  • Build strong relationships with sales representatives to ensure alignment on pricing strategies and customer expectations

  • Proactively identify opportunities for process improvement and recommend creative solutions to optimize pricing strategies

  • Analyze competitive market research and maintain competitive database

  • Prepare regular reports on pricing trends and competitive analysis for management review

  • Support the implementation of pricing-related projects and initiatives

  • Expand pricing support to all divisions within the company (Distribution, OEM, ESCO, etc.)

  • Other duties as assigned

What you bring:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Economics, Business, Finance or related field preferred; equivalent work experience will also be considered

  • 3-5 years of experience in pricing analysis roles within a manufacturing or distribution environment

  • Experience in the lighting industry preferred but not required

  • Proficient knowledge in lighting products preferred

  • Proficiency in Power BI, Excel and SQL; experience with P21 software is highly desirable

  • Ability to think creatively and propose innovative solutions to pricing challenges

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to foster relationships with the sales team and other departments

  • Strong organizational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously

  • Uphold and implement Keystone’s Core Values, consistently aligning actions and decisions that reflect the core principles

Please note that we do not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies.

title: Technology Support Specialist (PA)
description:
The Technology Support Specialist’s primary focus is to support and maintain FLCC end-user technology such as desktops, laptops, tablets, printers, and classroom technology for students, faculty and support staff. The Technology Support Specialist will work as a member of a team of support specialists, responding to IT Helpdesk Tickets relating to end-user technology. The Technology Support Specialist will carry out system replacements based on the life-cycle replacement schedules and/or as needed.

FLCC is committed to diversity, equity and inclusion, and strives to provide an environment that embodies these principles. We strive to attract talented personnel from diverse backgrounds and traditions, particularly of race and ethnicity, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, nationality, culture, religion, worldview and physical and mental abilities. As such, applicants from historically under-represented groups are highly encouraged to apply.

Qualifications:

Educational Background: Associate’s degree in an IT related field is required, Bachelor’s degree preferred.

Experience: 1 to 2 year’s experience supporting a technology rich and diverse environment. Experience and knowledge of one or both of Microsoft and/or Apple applications and operating systems required. Experience in a managed-device environment preferred.

Special Skills: Preferred qualifications include experience managing both Apple and Windows devices, as well as familiarity with classroom technologies such as projection systems and collaboration tools like WebEx, Zoom, Teams, and other similar platforms used in educational settings. A basic understanding of networking concepts, including Wi-Fi, LAN, and VPN, is also preferred. Experience with IT in a Higher Education
setting strongly preferred. A commitment to ongoing professional development and staying up-to-date with emerging technologies is highly valued. Additionally, the ability to handle multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment is essential.

Essential Functions:

  1. Demonstrates a customer-focused attitude with strong attention to detail, ensuring timely effective resolution of issues.

  2. Applies excellent analytical and diagnostic skills to resolve issues quickly and escalate when necessary, collaborating with the IT team to ensure issues are fully resolved.

  3. Designs and configures desktop software setups, plans system upgrades, and ensures proper configuration for both employee and student desktop and laptop systems.

  4. Provides end-user support for all technology-related needs.

  5. Uses device management tools (e.g., JAMF, SCCM, InTune) to ensure all devices are properly installed with required software for enterprise and instructional purposes.

  6. Troubleshoots and resolves issues with classroom technology, including document cameras, instructor PCs, SmartBoards, flat-panel TVs, projectors, Hyflex cameras/mics, PowerPoint sharing, and “clickers.”

  7. Supports the FLCC student laptop/tablet loaner program by assisting students, coordinating with the Helpdesk Specialist to track inventory, and ensuring devices are properly distributed and returned as part of College programs.

  8. Ensures all technology is accounted for in the FLCC Inventory and asset tracking system, updating inventory according to the college’s lifecycle replacement plan.

  9. Uses scripting tools to automate daily tasks where applicable.

  10. Assists faculty in utilizing instructional technology and classroom learning tools such as VR/AR, Poll Everywhere, Hyflex systems, and collaboration tool recordings.

  11. Follows best practices to safeguard college-owned devices from cyber threats.

  12. Investigates complex issues, collaborates with IT staff from other SUNY institutions, and evaluates potential solutions to design effective and proven strategies.

  13. Supervises student interns, providing guidance and support.

  14. Utilizes the Helpdesk Ticketing system, working with IT Helpdesk staff to ensure all necessary details are captured for each new ticket.

  15. Demonstrates flexibility in work schedule and locations as needed.

Physical Requirements:
In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, this job description contains only qualifications that are required, with or without a reasonable accommodation.

  1. Capable of using a computer for extended periods.

  2. Frequently travels to different areas of the building and bends to assist with equipment setup.

  3. Able to lift up to 20 pounds to assist with various office tasks.

  4. Able to communicate ideas and information clearly so others can understand, ensuring accurate exchange of information in all situations.

Benefits and salary range:

  1. Competitive starting salary in the range of $50,190 to $52,699 and is commensurate with qualifications

  2. NYS retirement or Optional SUNY Retirement Program

  3. SUNY Voluntary Savings Plan

  4. Comprehensive Health and Dental Insurance through Excellus BCBS

  5. FSA

  6. 21 days of annual leave, 12 sick days, and 13.5 holidays annually

  7. FLCC Tuition Waiver for employee and dependents

  8. Tuition assistance – 4-year institutions

Special Notes: Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. If you currently need sponsorship or will need it in the future to maintain employment authorization, you do not meet eligibility requirements.

For full consideration, please apply by August 21, 2026.

title: Youth Ministry Director at Camp Zama, U.S. Military Installation, Japan
description:
*Please note this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Description:

There are nearly 300,000 teenagers of active-duty U.S. military parents who are stationed all over the world. These teens move an average of seven times during their school-aged years. The questions of identity and belonging that all teens face grow even more challenging to answer amid starting over and meeting new friends at each location.

This is where you can be the difference in a military teen’s life! By being in their world, walking alongside them, and creating a community where they experience the truth of God’s love and purpose for them, our staff provide a safe space where teens can develop friendships and connections to experience laughter, build hope, and generate resiliency.

We are currently providing incarnational ministry at many military installations around the world. You will have the opportunity to lead and oversee the overall Young Life Military program, known as Club Beyond, which is ecumenically focused and outreach oriented.

We are currently looking for both full-time and part-time staff throughout the United States, as well as international locations. Colorado Springs, CO, is the headquarters.

Responsibilities:

  • Actively develop healthy relationships with adults, as well as kids, and build vibrant relationships with the local community, the military installation, and the chapel community.
  • Be a role model (incarnational) and assist with developing community outreach to "unchurched" teens, discipleship to Christian teens, and leading and equipping volunteers to do "hands-on" middle and high school Christian youth programs.
  • Work well in an environment that sees (due to high military operational tempo) a high degree of turnover among teens, families, chaplains and volunteers.
  • Be respectful of and embrace a community that is deeply influenced by a military culture.
  • In this ministry, you will need to live out the Club Beyond Core Value Statement:

Club Beyond is a Christ-centered community of leaders with an exclusively military focus. Our methods are incarnational, and our perspective is ecumenical. We leverage strategic partnerships for the greatest results. We value professionalism from our staff and excellence in our stewardship.

Qualifications:

  • A deep love for Christ and for lost teens.
  • Competent communicator with youths, parents, and senior military leaders.
  • Teachable heart.
  • Willingness to make a three-year commitment.
  • Minimum of three years' youth ministry experience preferred.
  • College degree preferred.
  • Willingness to raise part of the budget through personal support.
  • Committed to a relational ministry approach.
  • Energetic.
  • Small event planning skills.
  • Strong initiative.
  • Note, this position would require our Staff to live near the community where they would be doing ministry.

Benefits:

  • Full-time salary: Based on experience, responsibility, and fundraising levels.
  • Benefits: Full health coverage (including dental, vision and life insurance).
  • Expense reimbursement (mileage [office and ministry related]).
  • Training and career development is built into the job.

Salary:

The Base Salary range: $45,000 to $60,000 (Salary is based on education and experience). In addition to salary, a Cost of Living Adjustment, dependent on location, is available. The Annual National Funding provided is $16,667.

Location:

title: Field Operator - Entry
description:
Headquartered in Houston, Texas, Summit Midstream Corporation (NYSE: SMC) is a value-driven corporation focused on developing, owning and operating midstream energy infrastructure assets that are strategically located in unconventional resource basins, primarily shale formations, in the continental United States.

We currently operate natural gas, crude oil and produced water gathering systems in four unconventional resource basins:

  • the Williston Basin in North Dakota, which includes the Bakken and Three Forks shale formations;
  • the Denver-Julesburg Basin, which includes the Niobrara and Codell shale formations in Colorado and Wyoming;
  • the Fort Worth Basin in Texas, which includes the Barnett Shale formation; and
  • the Piceance Basin in Colorado, which includes the liquids-rich Mesaverde formation as well as the emerging Mancos and Niobrara Shale formations.

Our systems and the basins they serve are as follows:

  • the Polar & Divide system, which serves the Williston Basin;
  • the DFW Midstream system, which serves the Fort Worth Basin;
  • the Grand River system, which serves the Piceance Basin; and
  • the Niobrara G&P system, which serves the DJ Basin.

SMC has an equity investment in and operates Double E Pipeline, LLC, which is natural gas transmission infrastructure that provides transportation service from multiple receipt points in the Delaware Basin to various delivery points in and around the Waha Hub in Texas.

We generate a substantial majority of our revenue under primarily long-term and fee-based gathering agreements with our customers. The majority of our gathering agreements are underpinned by areas of mutual interest (“AMIs”) and minimum volume commitments (“MVCs”). Our AMIs provide that any production drilled by our customers within the AMIs will be shipped on our gathering systems. The MVCs are designed to ensure that we will generate a minimum amount of gathering revenue over the life of each respective gathering agreement. The fee-based nature of the majority of the gathering agreements enhances the stability of our cash flows and limits our direct commodity price exposure.

Since our formation in 2009, our management team has established a track record of executing this strategy through the acquisition and subsequent development of DFW Midstream, Grand River, Polar & Divide, Niobrara G&P, and Double E Pipeline.

Summit Midstream is proudly committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse and inclusive workforce. As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical condition), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

Relocation: No Relocation assistance provided.

Work Sponsorship: Summit Midstream will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States. Any offer of employment is contingent upon the Company receiving satisfactory results from a pre-employment drug screening, a criminal background check, and reference checks and your satisfaction of all other applicable fitness for duty requirements.

DOT Compliance: Responsibilities may include Department of Transportation (DOT) covered functions per PHMSA or FMSCA. Job duties also require the employee to be alert and respond immediately to dangerous or hazardous conditions, and where impaired performance, or failure to follow safety precautions, could result in serious injury or property damage. Maintain working knowledge of regulatory requirements, perform required tasks, and complete associated documentation (OSHA, DOT, EPA, etc.)

Summary:

A Field Operator inspects, maintains and repairs all facilities as assigned, including but not limited to pipelines, LACT units, components of well pads and measurement facilities, with supervision from management, mentors, or subject matter experts.

Principle Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Check wind direction, muster points, evacuation routes, etc. when arriving on location
  • On-call responsibility for areas of responsibility as needed
  • Maintain working knowledge of regulatory requirements, (OSHA, DOT, etc.) and document required regulatory activities
  • Work independently as liaison between Summit Midstream and outside entities, i.e. landowners, emergency response agencies, contractors and other pipeline companies
  • Operate and assist in maintenance activities at LACT facilities, and understand how pressures at certain terrains react and tank levels required to maintain proper head pressure
  • Perform pipeline patrols and inspect lines throughout the area and coordinate the activities of crews at other locations
  • Utilize hand tools to remove or replace valves, and have a basic understanding of riser locations and underground valves
  • Perform Lock-out/Tag-out procedures and write Safe Work Permits, as well as performing emergency shut-downs and operations control center protocols
  • Manage all activities with a focus on safety and compliance
  • Use proper tools and equipment to perform integrity management and regulatory tasks on oil or liquids pipelines
  • Monitor activity in and around pipeline and facilities and respond as necessary to protect system integrity, with the understanding of what to do in case of an emergency and/or spill
  • Look for leaks in the pump room and outside piping
  • Put in work orders in Maximo, and be able to utilize CYGNET
  • Maintain required forms, records and reports
  • Respond to pipeline emergencies; perform cleanup associated with field ops and corrosion control activities
  • Other duties as assigned

Education & Experience

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • 0 to 2 or more years of general pipeline experience in the natural gas industry or related experience in similar industry

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Basic knowledge and experience with line location equipment and techniques
  • Ability to identify pipes and valves and what they do
  • Ability to read and utilize drawings, schematics, alignment sheets
  • Basic knowledge and understanding of procedures used to safely pig pipeline, i.e. launching, receiving and inspection
  • Ability to identify specific hazards involved with cleaning strainers, such as proper isolation points and general troubleshooting of problems with each location visited
  • Basic understanding of functions of HMI’s and related programs
  • Basic knowledge of liquid handling equipment, pigging facilities required
  • Basic knowledge to conduct pressure surveys on gathering lines and central delivery points
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills required
  • Must have a valid driver license with acceptable driving record
  • Demonstrate the ability to operate off-road vehicles safely

Physical Demands and Working Conditions

  • Above average physical mobility to enable access to elevated height areas via stairs or ladders, as well as movement from place to place on the job, taking distance and speed into account
  • Strenuous physical activity-pushing, pulling and lifting requirements up to 50 lbs. manually transport a load up to 75 lbs. and apply up to 100 ft. lbs. of torque
  • Must be able to work out of doors in extreme weather conditions and perform heavy physical labor operating equipment in a safe manner
  • Work indoors and outdoors in and around industrial and electrical equipment

title: Senior Transportation Construction QA Inspector
description:
ATCS’s Construction Services group is expanding in Virginia! We are seeking an experienced Senior Transportation Construction QA Inspector to join our team in Northern Virginia.

This is a senior-level role requiring strong transportation construction inspection experience, current required certifications, and demonstrated experience managing project records and materials documentation. The ideal candidate will have experience working in a consultant/QA or owner-representative capacity and be comfortable independently handling both field inspection and project documentation responsibilities.

Duties:

  • Perform transportation construction inspections on highway, bridge, environmental, traffic, and facilities projects.
  • Provide oversight of contractor work crews to ensure compliance with contract documents, plans, specifications, and applicable standards.
  • Read and interpret contract documents and verify that safe construction practices are being utilized to produce quality results.
  • Write detailed daily progress and inspection reports.
  • Maintain complete and accurate project records and documentation throughout the project.
  • Manage materials documentation and project materials records/books to ensure required information is complete, accurate, and properly maintained.
  • Document materials, labor compliance, safety, estimates, work orders, adjustments, and other construction activities.
  • Report on-site activities and daily progress to the Project Engineer using standardized reporting.
  • Calculate, verify, and document pay quantities.
  • Perform applicable field testing of materials, including concrete slump/air, soil compaction, and HMA.
  • Coordinate with contractors, project staff, engineers, and owner representatives to resolve field and documentation issues.

Requirements:

  • 6+ years of transportation construction inspection experience, with senior-level responsibility strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated experience maintaining project records on transportation construction projects is required.
  • Experience maintaining materials documentation/materials books is required.
  • Consultant, QA, or owner-representative construction inspection experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience with Virginia roadway construction and VDOT projects preferred.
  • Knowledge of VDOT Road and Bridge Specifications and Standards.
  • Knowledge of OSHA safety requirements for road and bridge construction sites.
  • Knowledge of mathematics, including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry.
  • Skill in the use of field engineering and inspection/testing equipment, methods, and materials.
  • Valid driver’s license.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office and applicable construction/project management systems.

Certifications:

Candidates must possess the applicable certifications required for the assignment. Relevant certifications may include:

  • Work Zone Traffic Control
  • Asphalt Concrete Field
  • ACI Hydraulic Cement Concrete Field
  • Soils and Aggregate Compaction
  • Nuclear Safety and Transportation
  • Pavement Marking and Guardrail Installation
  • Stormwater Inspection
  • DEQ Erosion and Sediment Control Inspection
  • OSHA Safety training
  • Flagging

Important Experience Requirement

This position requires experience beyond traditional construction materials testing. Candidates must have hands-on experience with the broader project-records and documentation responsibilities associated with transportation construction inspection. Experience that is primarily limited to performing materials tests and preparing individual test reports may not meet the requirements of this senior-level assignment.

Our employees are the most critical part of ATCS. For this position, we offer a competitive salary range of $35.00 to $55.00 per hour, commensurate with experience and qualifications. ATCS is committed to providing equal opportunities and reasonable accommodation for individuals with disabilities in employment, its services, programs, and activities. title: Director, Commercial
description:
Headquartered in Houston, Texas, Summit Midstream Corporation (NYSE: SMC) is a value-driven corporation focused on developing, owning and operating midstream energy infrastructure assets that are strategically located in unconventional resource basins, primarily shale formations, in the continental United States.

We currently operate natural gas, crude oil and produced water gathering systems in four unconventional resource basins:

  • the Williston Basin in North Dakota, which includes the Bakken and Three Forks shale formations;

  • the Denver-Julesburg Basin, which includes the Niobrara and Codell shale formations in Colorado and Wyoming;

  • the Fort Worth Basin in Texas, which includes the Barnett Shale formation; and

  • the Piceance Basin in Colorado, which includes the liquids-rich Mesaverde formation as well as the emerging Mancos and Niobrara Shale formations.

Our systems and the basins they serve are as follows:

  • the Polar & Divide system, which serves the Williston Basin;

  • the DFW Midstream system, which serves the Fort Worth Basin;

  • the Grand River system, which serves the Piceance Basin; and

  • the Niobrara G&P system, which serves the DJ Basin.

SMC has an equity investment in and operates Double E Pipeline, LLC, which is natural gas transmission infrastructure that provides transportation service from multiple receipt points in the Delaware Basin to various delivery points in and around the Waha Hub in Texas.

We generate a substantial majority of our revenue under primarily long-term and fee-based gathering agreements with our customers. The majority of our gathering agreements are underpinned by areas of mutual interest (“AMIs”) and minimum volume commitments (“MVCs”). Our AMIs provide that any production drilled by our customers within the AMIs will be shipped on our gathering systems. The MVCs are designed to ensure that we will generate a minimum amount of gathering revenue over the life of each respective gathering agreement. The fee-based nature of the majority of the gathering agreements enhances the stability of our cash flows and limits our direct commodity price exposure.

Since our formation in 2009, our management team has established a track record of executing this strategy through the acquisition and subsequent development of DFW Midstream, Grand River, Polar & Divide, Niobrara G&P, and Double E Pipeline.

Summit Midstream is proudly committed to recruiting and retaining a diverse and inclusive workforce. title: Financial Management Analyst – (Joint Training Exercise and Evaluation Program (JTEEP))
description:
***This position is contingent upon task order award***

Job Description

The Financial Management Analyst (JTEEP Operational Liaison) provides financial management, budget execution support, and programmatic analysis to the Marine Corps Training and Education Command (TECOM) Joint Training Exercise and Evaluation Program (JTEEP). The incumbent works in coordination with the Joint Staff J7 (VDJS J7) in Suffolk, VA to support execution of Service Incremental Funds (SIF) and other joint training resources in support of Service Level Training Exercise Program (SLTE-P) events.

This position serves as the financial and programmatic liaison between TECOM, Marine Forces, and VDJS J7, ensuring accurate tracking of funding execution, compliance with fiscal guidance, and delivery of financial analysis products supporting leadership decision-making.

Essential Duties

Financial Execution & Analysis

  • Execute, monitor, and reconcile Service Incremental Funds (SIF) and joint training funding in support of SLTE-P exercise requirements.
  • Track obligations, expenditures, and execution rates across assigned programs.
  • Analyze cost variances, execution trends, and funding shortfalls across joint training activities.
  • Develop spend plans, execution forecasts, and financial analysis products for leadership review.
  • Provide courses of action (COAs) and recommendations for funding adjustments and risk mitigation.

Budget & Program Support

  • Support development of annual Service Incremental Funds (SIF) budget inputs in coordination with TECOM stakeholders.
  • Maintain visibility of funding status across programs to support decision-making.
  • Ensure funds are properly allocated, obligated, and executed in accordance with approved guidance and fiscal law.

Systems & Financial Reporting

  • Maintain and update Defense Agencies Initiative (DAI), Joint Investment Database (JIDB), and CE2T2 Program Tracking Tool (JPTT).
  • Reconcile financial transactions and supporting documentation across reporting systems.
  • Ensure accuracy and audit readiness of all financial records and data submissions.
  • Generate routine and ad hoc financial reports for TECOM leadership and Joint Staff requirements.

Coordination & Compliance

  • Provide financial input supporting compliance with fiscal law and DoD financial regulations.
  • Coordinate with TECOM, Marine Forces, and Joint Staff J7 on financial execution matters.
  • Provide timely updates on funding execution status, risks, and program issues.

Additional Duties

  • Support TECOM initiatives related to Joint Training and Integrated Campaigning, Service Joint Training, and Joint Training Enablers.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or related field required.
  • Five (5) years of DoD financial experience required.

Experience

  • Minimum five (5) years of experience in DoD financial management, budget execution, or program analysis.

Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Knowledge of DoD financial systems (DAI preferred).
  • Strong analytical and quantitative skills.
  • Understanding of fiscal law and federal financial regulations.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint).
  • Strong communication and reporting skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple financial data sources and reconcile discrepancies.

Additional Requirements

  • Ability to sit for extended periods and perform detailed analytical work.

title: Commercial Loan Processor II
description:
Commercial Loan Processor II

Job Type: Full- time/ Remote

Exemption Type: Non- exempt

Wage Amount: $28.57 per hour minimum

Primary Functions

The primary purpose of this position is to provide outstanding internal and external (team) member service by providing a variety of loan funding support services to the business lending membership. You will be responsible for the processing of commercial loan files from approval to closing of the transaction, including extensive collection and tracking of sensitive financial documents.

You will collect and verify purchase contracts, title work, appraisals, income, credit, asset, and loan disclosure documentation and ensure file completeness while working with underwriters, loan officers, members, and other credit union departments daily. This role requires a strong focus on member service, file accuracy, turn times, and problem-solving skills to resolve any issues with loan files.

This role will also serve as a subject matter expert for commercial loan processing and support training and coaching of Level I team members.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  1. Answer all incoming phone calls regarding commercial loan processing questions relating to new applications and coordinating and closing of new loan requests and loan renewals.

  2. Assist branch staff and other credit union departments with commercial loan closing questions.

  3. Obtain necessary information from members, CUSO (Credit Union Services Organization), or outside sources.

  4. Review loan applications for accuracy and completeness and verify all applicable information, including rates and terms.

  5. Review company agreements and other entity documentation to appropriately capture signatures on borrowing authorizations.

  6. Independently prepare loan documents, coordinate loan closings, fund and book loans for non-complex transactions.

  7. Assist with loan documents, closings, and funding for complex transactions such as portfolio loans or complex entity structures.

  8. Independently review real estate documentation including warranty deeds, title commitments, and closing statements.

  9. Communicate with members, dealers, title companies, and realtors as needed regarding loan closing processes and policies.

  10. Manage personal commercial loan pipeline in accordance with process flow expectations, including meeting closing dates and communicating with members, team members, and third parties associated with loan files being processed.

  11. Order, review, and clear conditions on all real estate appraisals, title commitments, tax valuations, insurance, flood determinations, surveys, and payoffs.

  12. Identify, prepare, and validate all fees associated with processed loan files to ensure accurate and compliant preparation of loan documents.

  13. Work with loan officers and members to clear all conditions and outstanding items prior to requesting clear to close.

  14. Independently monitor and track application flow from member to loan officer to closing and funding.

  15. Collect signatures for loan closings via mail or DocuSign and coordinate with mobile notaries as needed.

  16. Create and fund loans and disburse loan proceeds by wire, cashier’s check, or share deposit.

  17. Prepare title work packets for all vehicle loans and file UCC liens when applicable.

  18. Ensure loan packets and supporting documentation are filed in the imaging system.

  19. Complete quality control audits of closed loans.

  20. Assist with set up and implementation of new products and processes utilizing technology.

  21. Provide routine information, in person or by phone, concerning credit union services or policies.

  22. Make override or exception decisions for non-complex situations within established guidelines and procedures.

  23. Assist leadership team with resolving problems and triaging complex situations.

  24. Assist with training and basic coaching of Level I team members.

  25. Assist with leading team huddles and meetings.

  26. Work toward advanced knowledge of complex processing functions including commercial real estate loan documents and disclosures, federal and state regulatory requirements.

  27. Consistently meet or exceed Level II minimum expectations.

  28. Maintain job-level knowledge by attending assigned training and reviewing procedures to perform all duties required of the position.

  29. Participate in departmental projects and initiatives.

  30. Complete annual regulatory training as assigned.

title: VP, Government Relations
description:
The Vice President, Government Relations leads Nascentia Health’s government relations and public policy strategy, with a primary focus on New York State and coordinated federal and local advocacy. The VPGR position advances organizational priorities through legislative engagement, government partnerships, and policy analysis. The VPGR works with executive leadership to protect access to care, support sustainable reimbursement and workforce capacity, and identify public funding opportunities across Nascentia’s programs and services.

Performance Responsibilities and Standards

Strategic Leadership and Management

• Develop and lead an annual government relations agenda with executive leadership, establishing priority issues, desired outcomes, engagement plans, and measures of progress.

• Advise the CEO/President and executive leadership on emerging government actions, policy opportunities, and risks affecting organizational strategy and services.

• Manage the approved government relations budget and oversee external lobbyists, consultants, and association relationships; evaluate performance and alignment with organizational priorities.

• Lead, coach, and evaluate assigned staff; establish clear responsibilities, work standards, and professional development goals.

Legislative Advocacy and Government Relationships

• Build and maintain productive relationships with elected officials, legislative staff, executive branch officials, and public agencies at the state, federal, and local levels.

• Represent Nascentia’s approved positions in legislative meetings, hearings, advisory groups, and policy discussions; coordinate executive participation when appropriate.

• Develop advocacy strategies addressing healthcare access, home and community-based services, managed long-term care, reimbursement, workforce shortages, and other organizational priorities.

• Organize legislative visits, briefings, and facility or program tours that demonstrate Nascentia’s services, community impact, and policy needs.

Policy Analysis and Regulatory Coordination

• Monitor proposed legislation, budgets, regulations, and agency guidance; maintain an issue tracker identifying deadlines, organizational impact, recommended action, and responsible leaders.

• Assess policy proposals with Finance, clinical and operational leadership, health plan leadership, Human Resources, and Compliance to identify financial, service, and workforce implications.

• Coordinate development of policy recommendations, position statements, testimony, and regulatory comments, obtaining subject matter review and leadership approval before submission.

• Translate government developments into timely executive and Board briefings, distinguishing pending proposals from enacted requirements and identifying decisions or follow-up needed.

Reimbursement and Public Funding Advocacy

• Partner with Finance and operational leaders to support advocacy for adequate Medicare and Medicaid funding, sustainable payment methodologies, and resources for community-based care.

• Use validated financial and operational information to explain how reimbursement and workforce constraints affect service capacity, patient and member access, and organizational sustainability.

• Identify government funding and partnership opportunities for workforce development, service expansion, and capital or community initiatives; coordinate evaluation with the departments responsible for grants, development, and implementation.

• Support approved funding requests and government engagement, while ensuring financial commitments and application submissions receive the required internal approvals.

Coalitions and Advocacy Communications

• Develop working relationships with healthcare associations, community organizations, and other partners to advance shared policy priorities and strengthen Nascentia’s representation.

• Evaluate coalition positions and association activities for alignment with Nascentia’s interests; elevate conflicting positions or proposed commitments to executive leadership.

• Partner with Marketing and Communications on clear, consistent advocacy materials, including policy briefs, fact sheets, talking points, and community impact examples.

• Prepare executives and other authorized representatives for policymaker meetings and public testimony; coordinate appropriate participation by employees, patients, members, and community partners.

Ethics Compliance and Accountability

• Coordinate with Compliance, legal counsel, and Finance on applicable lobbying registrations, disclosures, activity records, reporting deadlines, and ethics requirements.

• Maintain accurate records of government contacts, advocacy expenditures, consultant activities, and approved positions; protect confidential organizational, patient, and member information.

• Ensure advocacy activities follow organizational approval requirements and applicable nonprofit restrictions; disclose potential conflicts and obtain guidance before making commitments.

• Report progress against advocacy priorities, including policy outcomes, funding developments, unresolved risks, and recommended next steps; distinguish organizational contributions from outcomes driven by broader coalitions.

• Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications Experience Education and Training Requirements

• Bachelor’s degree in public policy, political science, public administration, healthcare administration, business, or a related field required; master’s degree or law degree preferred. Equivalent relevant education and substantial professional experience may be considered.

• Minimum five years of progressively responsible experience in government relations, legislative affairs, public policy, or related work, including at least five years leading advocacy strategies, teams, or significant policy initiatives.

• Demonstrated knowledge of New York State legislative, executive, regulatory, and budget processes, with experience engaging policymakers and government agencies.

• Healthcare policy experience required; experience with home and community-based services, managed care, Medicare, Medicaid, or nonprofit healthcare organizations strongly preferred.

• Demonstrated ability to develop policy positions, build coalitions, and advance organizational priorities across differing political perspectives.

• Strong analytical, writing, presentation, and negotiation skills; ability to explain complex policy and financial issues to executive, government, and community audiences.

• Experience managing consultants, budgets, and competing priorities; sound judgment, discretion, and ability to work effectively across departments.

• Working knowledge of lobbying disclosure and ethics requirements, with the ability to coordinate compliance obligations with legal counsel and responsible internal departments.

Physical and Environmental Requirements

• Ability to perform the essential functions of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

• Ability to communicate effectively and use a computer and standard office equipment; work involves frequent sitting and intermittent standing and walking.

• Ability to travel regularly within New York State, including Albany, and periodically to Washington, D.C., or other locations; attend evening or weekend meetings and respond to changing legislative schedules as needed.

• Bloodborne Pathogens Exposure Category: III — Employee who rarely has contact with blood and body fluids.

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive Salary [This position is an S10 exempt position with a min-max rate of: $143,423 - $179,052/annually] with:

  • Retention Bonuses
  • Internal Mentoring Program
  • 401K with generous Employer match
  • On-Site Gym (free for all employees)
  • Potential Hybrid Position (Partial Work From Home)
  • Medical, Dental, Vision plans
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • Partially funded HSA
  • Employee Recognition Platform
  • Paid Time Off, Holidays, Sick and Extended Sick Leave
  • Short/Long term Disability
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
  • Much More!

About Nascentia Health:

Nascentia Health is leading the way in home care, post acute care and long-term community health. A healthcare system without walls, Nascentia is an innovator in the concept of healthcare, truly focused on the patient as a whole. By serving people in their homes, Nascentia Health is able to provide true holistic care. We can address immediate needs, help support positive long term medical and lifestyle choices that provide for better outcomes, leverage cutting edge in-home care technologies, and help avoid unnecessary visits to busy healthcare facilities.

Our employees are our greatest asset. They work hard every day to make our system amazing and are dedicated to our mission of being the premier home and community-based care system for the regions we serve. We want everyone to love what they do, be excited about coming to work, and take pride in being part of our team.

title: ADAS Calibration Technician & Analyst
description:
SUMMARY:

This is a mobile position traveling throughout the assigned territory, we do provide a company vehicle.

The ADAS Technician & Analyst is a hybrid role that combines both technical calibration responsibilities and analytical duties to ensure vehicles are restored to OEM safety and performance standards. This role works onsite within a CollisionRight repair center, performing dynamic and static calibrations, while also reviewing scan data, interpreting repair estimates, and coordinating with both internal and external teams. The position bridges technician execution with analyst-level oversight, providing a seamless workflow for ADAS calibration.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Calibration Responsibilities:

  • Perform static and dynamic calibrations in accordance with OEM procedures.

  • Use scan tools and calibration systems to restore ADAS components post-collision.

  • Maintain proper documentation of completed calibrations and work performed.

  • Conduct pre- and post-scans to support proper repair workflows.

  • Perform module programming as required to complete repairs and restore system functionality.

  • Troubleshoot diagnostic fault codes and address failed calibrations to determine root cause and next steps.

Analyst Responsibilities:

  • Analyze vehicle system scan data to determine required calibrations.

  • Review collision damage and repair estimates to confirm ADAS impact.

  • Research OEM procedures using approved service information tools.

  • Communicate ADAS needs to shop estimators, technicians, and leadership.

  • Ensure documentation, scan reports, and calibration records are uploaded and tracked accurately.

Collaboration & Workflow:

  • Work onsite daily at an assigned CollisionRight repair center.

  • Maintain a strong relationship with shop staff while reporting directly to 360Align leadership.

  • Support scheduling and prioritization of calibrations to ensure timely repair delivery.

  • Collaborate with centralized ADAS analysts, technicians, and managers for ongoing support.

Additional Responsibilities:

  • Maintain up-to-date training and certifications as required.

  • Participate in feedback sessions and process refinement to enhance ADAS workflows.

  • Adhere to all company and body shop safety procedures and policies.

EXPERIENCE & QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years of experience in automotive diagnostics, collision repair, or ADAS calibrations.

  • Working knowledge of ADAS components and calibration procedures.

  • Ability to read and interpret scan data and collision repair estimates.

  • Strong communication and customer service skills.

  • Experience with OEM service software and scan tools preferred.

  • I-CAR, ASE, or manufacturer certifications preferred.

  • Ability to work independently onsite while collaborating remotely with the broader ADAS team.

  • Self-motivated with strong organizational and time management skills.

  • Must have a valid driver’s license and clean MVR.

  • Ability to work 8+ hours in a shop environment and use computers/mobile devices efficiently.

This position description is intended to be dynamic and subject to change. Position requirements and essential functions may be altered from time to time based upon the needs of the organization and department. This position may be required to execute special projects or other related duties on occasion.

The Installation Services Fitter is responsible for the safe, accurate, and professional field installation of sanitary process systems, including process piping, tubing, skids, and related equipment. This hands-on role requires TIG welding, sanitary stainless fabrication and installation skills, flexibility to travel, and a commitment to representing CSI professionally.

Fitters work at customer sites to install equipment and process systems while meeting customer GMP requirements and CSI safety and quality standards. The role may also support shop fabrication, job-site cleanup, equipment organization, and guidance for less experienced team members.

If you take pride in skilled hands-on work, work safely, and enjoy supporting customers on the jobsite, this is your kind of role.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Sanitary Installation & Fabrication
  • Install sanitary process systems, including process piping, tubing, skids, and related equipment.
  • Perform TIG welding to CSI and customer standards; grind, polish, and finish welds and surfaces to sanitary standards.
  • Perform basic fit-up, including tube offsets, and apply knowledge of process equipment and instrumentation.
  • Read and interpret P&IDs, blueprints, isometric drawings, schematics, and specifications; sketch ISO drawings as required.
  • Operate tools and equipment such as saws, drill motors, plasma torches, scissor lifts, and forklifts as needed.
  • Load and unload materials and tools; operate a company vehicle and transport materials and equipment to jobsites.
  • Follow CSI and customer safety requirements, GMP regulations, and all trained or implemented safety procedures.
  • Represent CSI professionally when interacting with customers and promote CSI’s image and standards.
  • Act as lead on small jobs when assigned, and mentor and guide less experienced team members.
  • Maintain company vehicles, equipment, and tools; assist with shop fabrication, preventive maintenance, demobilization, cleanup, and equipment organization as needed.

What you Bring

You don’t need to know everything, but you do need the right mindset.

  • A strong commitment to safe work practices, quality, and sanitary installation standards
  • TIG welding skills and the ability to use tools and equipment needed to complete installation tasks
  • Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, P&IDs, schematics, and specifications
  • A professional, customer-focused approach and willingness to travel and work flexible schedules

Required Education/Experience

  • High School Diploma or equivalent.
  • Welding certificate preferred.
  • Class E Driver’s License, or the ability to obtain one, required.
  • 2+ years of TIG welding/GTAW experience.
  • Sanitary process piping experience preferred; previous fitting experience is a plus.

Travel Requirements

Overnight and/or weekend travel is necessary and may, at times, be as much as 100%. Travel may be by air or company vehicle.

CSI provides required tools, travel, hotel accommodations, meals, and other miscellaneous travel expenses associated with the position.

Work Environment / Physical Requirements

Field installation positions are very active and require frequent and/or continuous standing, walking, bending, kneeling, stooping, crouching, crawling, and climbing. The employee must frequently lift and/or move items weighing up to 75 pounds with assistance. Visual acuity is required to perform work using close, distance, and peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. The employee may be exposed to environmental factors typical of welding and field installation. Working outside or in non-climate-controlled environments may be required. The employee must be able to wear required personal protective equipment, including fall protection, safety glasses, steel-toe shoes, and other PPE appropriate to the work being performed.

Why CSI

  • Health and wellness benefits
  • Paid time off
  • Paid holidays
  • Company-provided tools and required equipment
  • Company-paid travel and hotel accommodations
  • Company-paid meals and eligible travel expenses
  • Opportunities for continuing education and professional growth
  • Team-oriented work environment
  • Opportunities to participate in company activities and community events

About CSI

CSI provides state-of-the-art stainless-steel process equipment and services to the food, dairy, beverage, pharmaceutical, and personal care industries.

We are a growing company with a passion for providing superior customer service. Our work environment is rooted in respect, teamwork, continual learning, growth, and community.

We believe our employees are our greatest resource, which is why we are committed to investing in our team. We offer a wide range of benefits including health and wellness, paid time off, retirement planning, and continuing education support. We also enjoy hosting company luncheons, casual Fridays, a wellness program, and providing opportunities for volunteering in local community charitable events.

Equal Opportunity Employer

CSI has a long-standing policy of Equal Opportunity in employment. Our practice is to fill positions by selecting applicants who can perform the work in a competent and professional manner. We do not discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, color, religion, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status, or individuals with disabilities.

U.S. federal law requires completion of employment eligibility verification upon hire. CSI participates in E-Verify. Applicants must have the right to work in the United States.

title: Wargaming Analyst (CEME)
description:
Wargaming Analyst (CEME)

Green Cell Consulting LLC

Location: Quantico, Virginia
Position Type: Full Time
Annual Salary: $105,000 to $115,000, depending on qualifications and experience
Security Clearance: Must possess or be eligible to obtain a security clearance
Employment Status: Contingent Upon Contract Award and Final Customer Requirements

How to Apply

If you are viewing this position on LinkedIn, Indeed, or another third-party employment website, please visit Green Cell Consulting's official careers page to submit your application directly.

Apply here:

Position Overview

Green Cell Consulting (GCC) is seeking a qualified Wargaming Analyst II to support the Marine Corps University (MCU) College of Enlisted Military Education (CEME) in Quantico, Virginia.

The Wargaming Analyst will serve as a college-level integrator for educational wargaming, supporting the development, implementation, and assessment of wargaming activities across enlisted professional military education programs.

The successful candidate will bring military experience, wargaming expertise, and instructional capabilities to help strengthen critical thinking, tactical decision-making, and warfighting judgment among Marines and other military professionals.

This position is contingent upon contract award, execution of the applicable contract modification, availability of funding, and final customer requirements.

Military Experience and Resume Submission

Military applicants are strongly encouraged NOT to civilianize their resumes.

At Green Cell Consulting, we understand and value military experience. We encourage applicants to retain their military ranks, billets, units, assignments, deployments, and relevant military terminology when describing their qualifications.

Please clearly identify your leadership responsibilities, operational experience, military education, specialized training, and experience with wargaming, planning, and instruction.

Our goal is to accurately evaluate your military experience and understand how your background aligns with the position's requirements. There is no need to translate your military accomplishments into civilian terminology.

Applicants must ensure their resumes do not disclose classified information, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), sensitive operational details, or any information restricted from public release.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide expert instruction on wargaming theory, educational wargaming techniques, and wargame facilitation.

  • Develop, revise, and maintain instructional curriculum and training materials supporting MCU educational programs.

  • Design, adapt, test, document, and maintain educational wargame systems and scenarios.

  • Develop decision points, scenario injects, player guides, facilitator materials, and supporting wargaming products.

  • Facilitate tabletop and computer-based wargaming exercises for military students and faculty.

  • Support faculty development programs focused on wargaming instruction and facilitation.

  • Integrate educational wargaming activities into enlisted professional military education curricula.

  • Develop assessment rubrics, observation protocols, and after-action review materials to evaluate student learning.

  • Participate in wargaming program assessments and recommend improvements to instructional effectiveness.

  • Mentor Marines, Sailors, other service members, interagency personnel, and international military officers in wargaming concepts and applications.

  • Collaborate with MCU faculty and staff to ensure wargaming activities support established educational objectives.

  • Travel up to 20% as required to support assigned duties.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.

  • 5 to 10 years of military and/or wargaming experience.

  • Significant firsthand experience participating in and facilitating traditional board wargames and computer-based wargames.

  • Foundational knowledge of wargaming concepts, methodologies, and educational applications.

  • Familiarity with wargame design and scenario development fundamentals.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop instructional materials and deliver effective training.

  • Ability to communicate complex military and wargaming concepts to diverse audiences.

  • Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work collaboratively with military faculty, government personnel, and other stakeholders.

  • Must possess or be eligible to obtain a security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Marine Corps background with experience in professional military education.

  • Completion of resident or nonresident Intermediate Level School (ILS), or Command and Staff College equivalent.

  • Experience developing and facilitating educational wargames within military training or academic environments.

  • Familiarity with Marine Corps doctrine, tactical decision-making, and enlisted professional military education.

  • Experience developing wargaming scenarios, assessment tools, and after-action review products.

  • Previous experience supporting Marine Corps University or comparable military educational institutions.

Compensation and Benefits

Green Cell Consulting offers a competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits package designed to support our employees and their families.

Annual Salary: $105,000 to $115,000, depending on qualifications, experience, and final contract requirements.

Benefits Include

  • Competitive Compensation

  • 401(k) Retirement Plan with Immediately Vested Company Match

  • Professional Development (Tuition Assistance, Professional Memberships, LinkedIn Learning)

  • Paid Holidays, Including Your Birthday

  • Vacation Accrual Beginning on Day One

  • Sick Leave with Carryover

  • Annual Clothing Allowance

  • Voluntary Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance

  • Health Savings Account (HSA) for Eligible Participants

  • Voluntary TRICARE Supplement Insurance Option for Eligible Participants

  • Paid Community Service Leave

  • Employer-Paid Life Insurance

  • Employer-Paid Accidental Death and Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance

  • Employer-Paid Long-Term Disability

  • Voluntary Short-Term Disability

  • Voluntary Life Insurance for Employees and Dependents

Benefits are subject to eligibility requirements, applicable plan terms, and company policy.

About Green Cell Consulting

Green Cell Consulting LLC is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) providing professional services and operational support to the Department of Defense and other government customers.

Founded in 2014, GCC specializes in delivering experienced personnel and mission-focused solutions that support military training, education, planning, and operational readiness.

Our core values of Trust, Service, and Value guide our commitment to our customers, employees, and the missions we support.

Why Join Green Cell Consulting?

At Green Cell Consulting, you will have the opportunity to directly support the Marine Corps' professional military education mission by helping develop and deliver educational wargaming experiences that strengthen decision-making, critical thinking, and warfighting judgment.

You will work alongside experienced military professionals, educators, and wargaming specialists to support the development of the next generation of Marine Corps leaders.

Join a team that values military experience, professional excellence, and a commitment to supporting the warfighter.

Important Employment Notice

This position is contingent upon contract award, execution of the applicable contract modification, availability of funding, and final customer requirements.

Submission of an application, participation in an interview, or selection as a candidate does not constitute an offer or guarantee of employment.

The position's responsibilities, qualifications, compensation, clearance requirements, and anticipated start date may be adjusted based on final contractual and customer requirements.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Employment decisions are based on job-related qualifications, experience, and business needs without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.
