title: Data Scientist II
description:
At ACT, Your Work Makes a Difference

Education has power – a power that changes lives forever. It creates opportunities that lift up individuals, their families, and sparks societal change that echoes through generations to come. From our grassroots we have fought the good fight for equity in education, and we remain devoted to helping anyone who struggles to access that power. This is what matters to us and we must do better -- we’ve never been more sure of our purpose.

ACT team members are part of an organization dedicated to a mission that has never been more important: Helping people achieve education and workplace success. Advancing that mission within our organization, by helping our team members achieve education and workplace success of their own, is core to our values. ACT values a diverse workplace and is committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable environment in which every team member has an opportunity to grow.

We want our team members to have the well-being and confidence they need to do their best work, in an environment where both they and ACT thrive. To support this, our total rewards include company paid life insurance, medical, dental, vision, flexible health and dependent spending accounts, 401(k) retirement savings with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and so much more. You can find a comprehensive list of our benefits here.

We are seeking a Data Scientist II to help us fulfill that mission.

ACT is seeking a Data Scientist II to help build a new pathway navigation experience that helps high school students explore, plan, and take confident next steps toward college and career. This role will design, test, and validate the data models that power personalized college, career, and pathway recommendations. You will work cross-functionally with product, engineering, research, design, and business partners to combine student, education, assessment, interest, skills, and career data into relevant, explainable, and actionable recommendations. You will move quickly from early experimentation to production implementation while ensuring that models are accurate, transparent, fair, and appropriate for use with students and families.

The finalist will be hired at the salary and level commensurate with their qualifications. For this position, we anticipate offering an annual salary in the range of $95,000 to $105,000. ACT manages salaries within the range based on relevant factors including, skills, experience, and internal equity.

Location: This is a remote position, based in the United States.

Visa: Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S. without the need for visa sponsorship.

Please Note: This is a Fixed Term Position that will last 6 months, with the possibility of an extension.

What you will be working on:

Data Science and AI Development:

  • Design, prototype, and evaluate models that generate personalized college, career, and pathway recommendations
  • Apply statistical modeling, machine learning, and generative AI to rapidly test and improve product capabilities
  • Evaluate model performance, fairness, bias, and appropriate use

Product Data and Experimentation:

  • Design data collection strategies that capture student behavior, performance, and engagement while supporting rapid product development
  • Analyze pilot and user-study data and translate findings into actionable product recommendations
  • Define metrics and experiments to evaluate recommendation quality and product impact

Data Architecture and Production:

  • Partner with engineers to build scalable cloud-based data pipelines and move models from prototype into production
  • Integrate data from student, education, assessment, skills, career, and labor-market sources
  • Establish reliable processes for data security, model documentation, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance

Student-Centered Personalization:

  • Develop approaches that produce useful recommendations when student data is incomplete and adapt as new information becomes available
  • Use behavioral and performance data to support personalized and adaptive product experiences
  • Make model outputs understandable and actionable for various stakeholders

Cross-Organizational Collaboration:

  • Collaborate across teams to align data, modeling, research, and product requirements
  • Translate research and business needs into data collection plans and technical solutions
  • Communicate analytical findings, assumptions, risks, and tradeoffs to technical and nontechnical stakeholders

This could be the job for you if you have (minimum requirements):

  • Bachelor’s degree in data science, computer science, statistics, applied mathematics, economics, operations research, or a related quantitative discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and experience from which comparable knowledge and abilities can be acquired
  • At least 3 years of applied data science experience, including building statistical or machine-learning models and analyzing product experiments, pilots, or user studies
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience developing scalable data pipelines and moving data products or models from prototype toward production

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • A hands-on, product-oriented data scientist who can move from analysis and rapid prototyping to production implementation
  • Strong in statistical modeling, machine learning, experimental design, and model evaluation
  • Experienced in scalable data pipelines, cloud environments, and integrating complex data sources
  • Skilled at using behavioral and performance data to develop personalized product experiences
  • Thoughtful about responsible AI, including fairness, bias mitigation, transparency, privacy, and appropriate use
  • An effective cross-functional communicator who translates research and business needs into actionable technical solutions

It’s a plus if you have (preferred requirements):

  • Master’s degree in data science or related field
  • Experience with recommender systems, generative AI, natural language processing, or personalized and adaptive systems
  • Experience with education, assessment, career, workforce, labor-market, occupational, or skills data

About ACT

When ACT was founded in 1959, it disrupted the assessment industry with a new approach to helping students better understand their readiness so they could take steps to improve it. By leveraging our expertise and authority in assessment and research, we will again disrupt the industry—helping more people learn, better measure their progress, and improve their navigation through life’s transitions.

More than ever before, ACT is fulfilling its mission of helping people achieve education and workplace success. We’re doing it by pushing the boundaries of learning innovation through the work of our people, who we call team members because we’re all in this together.

We know transformation does not come without challenge. That’s why ACT invests in a variety of experiences for team members to strengthen their connections, explore ideas, learn from customers, and celebrate success.

Learn more about working at ACT at !

Completion of the ACT National Career Readiness Certificate is recommended. Find a testing site near you to register for the WorkKeys assessments. Finalists for this position will be subject to a criminal background check as a condition of employment.

  • Current license issued by the Indiana Behavioral Health and Human Services Licensing Board as an LCSW, LMFT, or LMHC

  • Evidence receipt of monthly reflective supervision related to activities as mental health consultant.

Preferred Education and Experience:

  • Infant Mental Health Specialist Endorsement (IMHS)

Qualifications:

title: Entry-Level Behavior Specialist - Autism
description:
Psychology Opportunity in Nevada,MO

Seeking candidates who are able to a make a long term commitment (minimum 6 months) | Competitive Pay | Flexible Hours |

Are you a seasoned Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) seeking the ideal organization to join? We're actively seeking enthusiastic and devoted RBTs to become valued members of our team, contributing your expertise to support our clients in achieving their unique goals. As an accomplished professional in the Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) field, your skills and dedication align with our dedication to providing excellence to our clients.

Qualifications:

  • High school diploma or equivalent.

  • Willingness to learn and passionate about making a difference for children with Autism.

  • Patience, compassion, and the ability to maintain a calm demeanor in challenging situations.

  • RBT certification is required before working

Perks:

  • Same Day Pay! No more waiting for payday — now you can access a portion of your paycheck right after you clock in and out. Whether it’s an emergency or you just need funds sooner, you’ll have the flexibility to get paid immediately.
    Your time. Your money. On your schedule.

  • Elevate your career with job stability and opportunities for professional advancement in the thriving ABA industry.

  • Enjoy the flexibility and autonomy you deserve, catering to your schedule and professional preferences.

  • Receive competitive compensation that reflects your experience.

  • Ideal for those seeking part-time positions.

  • Access career advancement assistance through partnerships with BCBA schooling programs.

  • Benefit from a robust clinical team dedicated to providing the support you deserve.

  • Fellowship and internship opportunities to accumulate both restricted and unrestricted hours.

  • Enjoy the freedom to choose your own cases, without a minimum case requirement.

Responsibilities:

  • Provide one-on-one ABA services to clients, using evidence-based interventions supporting independence and positive behavior.

  • Serve as an integral member of our clinical team, responsible for the direct implementation of skill-building and care plans.

  • Record session data accurately using electronic devices.

  • Foster a positive learning environment for clients and connect with families.

Need to Know:

  • Services will be provided in clients' homes or in community-based locations.

Great Fit If You Have Experience In:

  • Education or early childhood development

If you're compassionate, patient, and passionate about making a difference, we encourage you to apply.

Join our team, contribute your skills to our mission, and continue your journey of making a meaningful difference in the lives of children with Autism. Apply today and be a part of our dynamic and fulfilling community!

title: Program Coordinator
description:
Title: Program Coordinator, ARCHES Brownsville

Reports To: Vice President of Justice Initiatives

Location: 1709 St. Mark's Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11233

Hours: 35 Hours/Week; Exempt

Salary: $55,000-$61,000 / Year

JOB SUMMARY: The Program Coordinator is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the ARCHES Brownsville site. ARCHES is an innovative, curriculum-based group mentoring intervention that helps young adults between the ages of 16-24 and on probation transform attitudes and behaviors that have led to criminal activity.

Major Duties:

  • Supervise implementation of Arches Program consistent with contractual mandates, standards and procedures set by GSS and Department of Probation (DOP)
  • Create opportunities for participants to maximize their potential through engaging programming, high expectations, and quality services
  • Develop and implement processes that ensure integration of participant feedback in program planning
  • Recruit, screen, hire and supervise Mentors.
  • Ensure program utilization meets contractual goals
  • Coordinate DOP technical assistance
  • Ensure that staff participate in all required DOP meetings
  • Ensure that mentoring groups maintain proper mentor/young adult ratios and fidelity to the Arches model
  • Schedule weekly mentoring groups and individual one-on-one secessions with mentees
  • Lead case conferences & staff meetings
  • Develop on-call schedule
  • Serve as liaison with DOP, having at minimum weekly contact with Probation Officers
  • Complete and provide narrative and statistical reports to Good Shepherd administrative departments and public funders as needed.
  • Monitor and manage program budget
  • Ensure proper staff usage of internal and external databases
  • Participate in agency work groups and committees.
  • Represent Good Shepherd Services at relevant external meetings.

Qualifications:

  • BA/BS in related field preferred.
  • Prior supervisory experience
  • Solid understanding of youth development principals and education.
  • Experience and comfort working with court-involved young adults
  • Ability to work from a strength-based, non- judgmental approach
  • Solid group work skills, familiarity with cognitive-behavioral interventions, and/or evidence-based practice, preferred
  • Proficiency using word processing, spreadsheet and databases
  • Excellent interpersonal, organizational, oral and written communication skills.
  • Must be available to work flexible, non-traditional schedule, which in addition to weekdays may include emergency on-call and weekend hours
  • Sense of humor a plus

title: Student Ministry Resident
description:
Student Ministry Residency

The Student Ministry Resident supports and enhances the ministry to the Junior High and High School students at each of our six campuses. They work under the leadership of the Campus Pastor and the Student Ministry Pastor.

General Duties and Responsibilities

  • Lead by example in character, passion, commitment to Christ and His Word, and genuine love and care for people.
  • Provide encouragement and support to the rest of the Student Ministry Team.
  • Help create a collaborative and encouraging environment for both the paid staff and the volunteers who support the ministry.
  • Participate in regular staff meetings for the Student Ministry team.
  • Following the lead of the Student Ministry Pastor, understand and share the Ministry’s vision and purpose with others.
  • Assist in developing solid relationships with parents and other interested adults, to encourage them to be involved in the Student Ministry.
  • Help in the recruiting and training of volunteers to help support the ministry.
  • Provide teaching on Wednesday or Sunday mornings as requested.
  • Attend regularly scheduled Ministry Residents/Internship meetings throughout the year.

Specific Weekly Duties and Responsibilities

  • Work with all of the Student Ministry Team to provide strong organizational and logistical support.
  • Help provide activities and events geared for Junior High and High School students.
  • Meet regularly with students for the purpose of discipleship, helping them grow in their faith relationship with God.
  • As opportunities arise, share your faith with students and adults.
  • Participate in the Student Ministry staff meetings.
  • Follow-up with first time guests and MIA students.
  • As requested, meet with parents and other interested adults to encourage them and provide a healthy connection to the Student Ministry.
  • Joining the other Student Ministry staff, be on campus as much as possible.
  • Meet with your Student Ministry Pastor and other leaders to determine and support campus-level activities and events.
  • Work with the Student Ministry Team in coordinating plans for Sunday mornings and LIVE on Wednesday nights.
  • Speak as requested on Sundays and Wednesdays.
  • Connect with current volunteers to encourage, support, and equip them to be effective in their work.
  • Provide leadership and planning for the events and activities of the Student Ministry.
  • Work with the Global Student Ministry Team to build the ministry at all six of our campuses.
